name: First-Year Experience for Transfer Students
oneLiner: The goals of higher education, mission and structure of the university, communication…
description: The goals of higher education, mission and structure of the university, communication and information competency, academic skill development, and personal and interpersonal skills related to academic success. Preparation for upper-division writing in the major (GWAR).
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2*.

name: Living in San Francisco
oneLiner: Learn about the historical, geographic and environmental, socio-cultural, and political…
description: Learn about the historical, geographic and environmental, socio-cultural, and political context of the SF Bay Area that draws people to this place. Explore the challenges and opportunities of living in San Francisco. Learn about the history of SF State University and the deep connections between this institution and its location. Build community as you explore the opportunities available to you as a student at SF State. (CR/NC grading only)

name: Pathways Seminar for Pre-Health Majors
oneLiner: Exploration of health-related fields to enhance options for career and graduate school…
description: Exploration of health-related fields to enhance options for career and graduate school pathways (e.g., pre-med, pharmacy). Assistance with preparing for these paths included. (Plus-minus ABC/NC, CR/NC)

name: First Year Undeclared Success
oneLiner: Exploration of values and interests by undeclared students to identify major options…
description: Exploration of values and interests by undeclared students to identify major options that align with their goals. Active participation in an engaging learning environment, utilization of self-assessment tools, and navigation of online and on-campus resources to support the major exploration process. Introduction to how to be a successful member of SF State's vibrant campus community. (Plus-minus ABC/NC, CR/NC)
prereqNotes: Restricted to undeclared students or permission of the instructor.

name: SF State and Braven Career Accelerator
oneLiner: Prepare for the competitive, global marketplace and begin to build your professional…
description: Prepare for the competitive, global marketplace and begin to build your professional network. Develop communication, teamwork, career, and project management skills that prepare you for opportunities after graduation, both in the job market and graduate school.
prereqNotes: 30 units of coursework. Intended for sophomores and new transfer students.

name: Peer Mentor Support
oneLiner: Develop student mentor leadership, communication, and peer mentoring skills, as well as…
description: Develop student mentor leadership, communication, and peer mentoring skills, as well as an understanding of university rules, regulations, and support services offered across campus. Mentors learn strategies to engage mentees and identify best practices for connection. (CR/NC grading only)

name: Presidential Scholars Seminar
oneLiner: Development of an understanding of the diverse opportunities and challenges in…
description: Development of an understanding of the diverse opportunities and challenges in leadership positions. Examination of fundamental leadership theories and development of the skills necessary to be engaged citizens. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Presidential Scholar.

name: Internship Reflection and Career Readiness Seminar
oneLiner: Reflect on an internship or experiential learning experience and build career readiness…
description: Reflect on an internship or experiential learning experience and build career readiness skills. Assess professional skills, core competencies, and workplace habits developed through hands-on experience in a wide range of professional settings. Emphasis on self-reflection, ethical practice, and goal setting, with opportunities to consider how individual work connects to organizations, teams, and communities. Learn to identify strengths, areas for growth, and next steps toward career goals. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Lecture: 1 unit; supervision: 2 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: An approved internship, practicum, or structured experiential learning placement; or permission of the instructor.

name: Peer Mentoring
oneLiner: Explore theories and concepts of peer mentoring and evidence-based studies on the…
description: Explore theories and concepts of peer mentoring and evidence-based studies on the impact of peer mentoring on student success. Develop an understanding of and practice using inclusive classroom and communication strategies that will facilitate student development, academic skills, and community building to effectively support students transitioning into higher education. Apply understandings of peer mentoring in different settings, including first-year seminars, new student orientation, and the transfer student transition. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Peer Mentor Support
oneLiner: Develop student mentor leadership, communication, and peer mentoring skills, as well as…
description: Develop student mentor leadership, communication, and peer mentoring skills, as well as an understanding of university rules, regulations, and support services offered across campus. Mentors learn strategies to engage mentees and identify best practices for connection. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor.

name: College Corps Fellowship Seminar
oneLiner: Reflection and analysis of College Corps Fellowship experience.
description: Reflection and analysis of College Corps Fellowship experience. Development of an academic understanding of the context of service learning placement and topics, as well as professional identities and skills for equitable and just civic and community engagement. Contribution to addressing societal challenges and helping build equitable communities in the San Francisco Bay Area. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: College Corps Fellow or permission of the instructor.

name: Willie Brown Internship Seminar
oneLiner: Overview of public sector issues at the local level with a focus on professional…
description: Overview of public sector issues at the local level with a focus on professional development and career pathways. Guest speakers will discuss topics related to the public sector.
prereqNotes: Willie Brown Internship.

name: Integrating Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Study Abroad
oneLiner: The culminating experience for students completing an SF State Abroad program to…
description: The culminating experience for students completing an SF State Abroad program to enhance learning outcomes related to cross-cultural perspectives and skill development. Student works with various faculty and staff advisors to complete a series of workshops upon re-entry that integrate interdisciplinary perspectives gained from study abroad with the student's own transformative experiences living in a different culture. May be repeated for a total of 2 units.
prereqNotes: Completion of an SF State Exchange or CSUP IP Study Abroad Program; permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Supervised individual study of a particular issue in higher education.
description: Supervised individual study of a particular issue in higher education.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: First-Year Experience
oneLiner: Preparation for Asian American Studies courses and future careers.
description: Preparation for Asian American Studies courses and future careers. Provides a framework of social justice, equity, and culturally relevant and responsive practices to address issues facing the Asian American and Pacific Islander communities. Engage in life skills that will help students retain and engage them in school and their lives.
prereqNotes: Restricted to first-year freshmen.

name: Identity, Equity, and Student Success
oneLiner: Exploration of racial/cultural identity, equity, and student success.
description: Exploration of racial/cultural identity, equity, and student success. Topics include an overview of academic success skills, racial/cultural identity development, social justice, equity, personal and community responsibility, educational strategies and planning, interpersonal communication, career development, health issues, and self-assessment strategies. May be repeated for a total of 2 units.

name: Asian American Activism
oneLiner: Introduction to the discipline of Asian American studies and the practice of…
description: Introduction to the discipline of Asian American studies and the practice of interdisciplinary, social-justice based inquiry and research. Focus on the human behavior of Asian American leadership, visionary activism, activist movements, and activist-related knowledge paradigms. Emphasis on rhetorical strategies of communication for self-reflection, self-determination, and community empowerment, and for the development of social relationships.
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2*.

name: Asian American Artistic Explorations: Creativity, Identity, and Community
oneLiner: Examine Asian American artistic explorations as self-expression, a reflection of…
description: Examine Asian American artistic explorations as self-expression, a reflection of community, and a tool for organizing. Study how artists utilize creative work for the exploration, recording, understanding, and expression of Asian American life. Investigate the importance of visual literacy in enacting social justice and empowerment in the Asian American community. Explore how Asian American artists employ autobiography and self-portraiture to analyze and express concerns such as well-being, identity formation, social justice, and community activism. Analyze works by Asian American creators in relation to the Asian American community. Writing and creative assignments. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2*.

name: Critical Thinking and the Asian American Experience
oneLiner: Development of basic critical thinking skills involved in understanding, criticizing…
description: Development of basic critical thinking skills involved in understanding, criticizing, and constructing arguments reflective of the experience of Asian Americans and key themes in Asian American Studies.

name: History of Asians in the United States
oneLiner: Comparative analysis of the experience of different Asian American groups and their…
description: Comparative analysis of the experience of different Asian American groups and their place in the general history and development of American society.

name: Contemporary Asian Americans
oneLiner: Examination of factors that define minority groups and their positions in contemporary…
description: Examination of factors that define minority groups and their positions in contemporary U.S. society, using Asian Americans as a case study.

name: Asian Americans and Mass Media
oneLiner: Images and treatment of Asian Americans in mass media, especially motion pictures…
description: Images and treatment of Asian Americans in mass media, especially motion pictures, television, advertising, popular literature, and commercial art. American minorities in the entertainment industry.

name: Asian Americans and American Ideals and Institutions
oneLiner: The Asian American experience in the U.S. focusing on basic governmental ideals and…
description: The Asian American experience in the U.S. focusing on basic governmental ideals and institutions. Impact of Asians on legal-constitutional America and the countervailing impact of political-legal structures imposed on Asians.

name: Second Year Written Composition: Asian American Studies
oneLiner: Reading and writing with speech as a supportive language skill. (Plus/minus ABC/NC…
description: Reading and writing with speech as a supportive language skill. (Plus/minus ABC/NC, CR/NC allowed)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2. Must be taken after completing 24 units and before completing 60 units.

name: Introduction to Asian American Literature
oneLiner: Reading and analysis of Asian American literature.
description: Reading and analysis of Asian American literature. Appreciation of literature from a literary standpoint with a focus on history, identity, and representation.

name: Asian American Culture
oneLiner: Ethnic values and cultures in America using Asian American arts, languages, and…
description: Ethnic values and cultures in America using Asian American arts, languages, and literatures. How these works reflect and express the character of the Asian American experience and the forces that have shaped that experience.

name: Asian Americans of Mixed Heritages
oneLiner: Issues concerning Asian Americans of mixed racial and ethnic heritages focusing on…
description: Issues concerning Asian Americans of mixed racial and ethnic heritages focusing on mixed heritage identities in relation to their ethnic and cultural sensibilities.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Futurism: Music, Art, Technology, Culture, and Identity
oneLiner: Explore the foundations of Asian American Futurism.
description: Explore the foundations of Asian American Futurism. Gain insight into the diverse roots of Asian American futurism in relation to other BIPOC futurisms to examine how they intersect and mutually influence one another, leading to the liberation of cultural narratives of Asian American and other BIPOC communities.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese in the United States
oneLiner: The Chinese American experience in critical historical perspective from the beginning…
description: The Chinese American experience in critical historical perspective from the beginning of immigration in the 19th century to the present.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese American Language and Literature
oneLiner: The cultural identity of the Chinese American as expressed in the language and literature.
description: The cultural identity of the Chinese American as expressed in the language and literature. The Chinese community and its influence on the creative process in literature.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese American Identities
oneLiner: Historical, institutional, and cultural sources of Chinese American identity and…
description: Historical, institutional, and cultural sources of Chinese American identity and sensibility. Mental health issues related to self-perception, stereotypes, family problems, institutional racism, and the development of autonomy. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Nikkei in the United States
oneLiner: The historical experience of Japanese Americans in the United States: prewar…
description: The historical experience of Japanese Americans in the United States: prewar immigration and settlement, the struggle against racial exclusion, World War II incarceration, and the postwar return and development of contemporary Nikkei community. Includes mixed race, war brides, Okinawan American, Yonsei and Gosei, LGBTQIA, and other populations not usually included in dominant Japanese American narratives.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Japanese American Art and Literature
oneLiner: Examination of Japanese American art and literature through the historical, social, and…
description: Examination of Japanese American art and literature through the historical, social, and cultural factors that influenced its development. Specific works and artists representing different genres and periods will be analyzed.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Japanese American Identities
oneLiner: Japanese American character, identity, self-image, and behavioral manifestations of the…
description: Japanese American character, identity, self-image, and behavioral manifestations of the interaction of American and Japanese cultural values.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Okinawan American Heritage and Culture
oneLiner: Analyzes the identity formation and cultural preservation of Okinawans in the U.S. and…
description: Analyzes the identity formation and cultural preservation of Okinawans in the U.S. and other parts of the Americas. Theoretical frameworks such as racial formation theory and world systems theory will be explored and developed to understand the complex evolution of the Okinawan diaspora within the dual imperial contexts of American and Japanese empires. [Formerly AA S 337]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Filipina/os in the United States
oneLiner: Immigration of the Filipina/os to the United States, coping mechanisms used in response…
description: Immigration of the Filipina/os to the United States, coping mechanisms used in response to adjustment problems, and the changing structure of the community.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Filipina/o American Literature, Art, and Culture
oneLiner: Critical perspectives on Filipina/o American culture through the examination of diverse…
description: Critical perspectives on Filipina/o American culture through the examination of diverse genres of art and literature primarily written in English about Filipina/os in the United States, the Philippines, and the diaspora.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Filipina/o American Identities
oneLiner: The historical, social, and cultural influences that impact the identities of…
description: The historical, social, and cultural influences that impact the identities of Filipina/o Americans through a framework of decolonization.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Koreans in the United States
oneLiner: Korean Americans in the U.S., examining the historical experience and the sociological…
description: Korean Americans in the U.S., examining the historical experience and the sociological, political, and economic implications of being a minority and immigrant in the U.S.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Vietnamese in the United States
oneLiner: Origins and causes of Vietnamese movements to the U.S. and nature of Vietnamese…
description: Origins and causes of Vietnamese movements to the U.S. and nature of Vietnamese experience in America in terms of political, cultural, and economic factors.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Vietnamese American Literature
oneLiner: A critical survey of Vietnamese American literature, taking into account issues of…
description: A critical survey of Vietnamese American literature, taking into account issues of race, class, gender, sexuality, and trauma.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Vietnamese American Identities
oneLiner: Vietnamese American experience since 1975: psychological adaptation, educational…
description: Vietnamese American experience since 1975: psychological adaptation, educational adjustment, socioeconomic integration, and cultural/ethnic maintenance.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Cambodians in the United States
oneLiner: Examine the push-pull factors that led people to flee Cambodia.
description: Examine the push-pull factors that led people to flee Cambodia. Focus on the constraints and strategies (institutional, artistic, community, and cultural) deployed by Cambodian Americans to negotiate their status in the US: politically, culturally, economically, and socially. [Formerly AA S 377]
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian Americans in California
oneLiner: Asian American contributions to the building of the state from their first arrival in…
description: Asian American contributions to the building of the state from their first arrival in the 19th century to their role within California's multiracial racial formation and their growing influence on contemporary California.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Children's/Adolescent Literature
oneLiner: Literary works with Asian American themes written for youth (preschool to middle school).
description: Literary works with Asian American themes written for youth (preschool to middle school). How Asian Americans are depicted from the 19th century to the present. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Photographic Explorations
oneLiner: Photography as a personal tool for the exploration, recording, understanding, and…
description: Photography as a personal tool for the exploration, recording, understanding, and expression of Asian American life.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Musical Communities
oneLiner: Review of the Asian American musical experience including the cultural sources that…
description: Review of the Asian American musical experience including the cultural sources that have informed artists' projects and the history that has shaped collective arts organization and activism among Asian Americans.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing.

name: Community Building Through The Performing Arts: Methods and Strategies
oneLiner: Acquire skills and perspectives utilized by artists and activists in creating Asian…
description: Acquire skills and perspectives utilized by artists and activists in creating Asian American performing arts communities as a means to imagine and pursue community-building practice. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: AA S 520 or permission of the instructor.

name: South Asians in the United States
oneLiner: History of South Asian immigration to the U.S. and how South Asian Americans negotiate…
description: History of South Asian immigration to the U.S. and how South Asian Americans negotiate ethnic belonging and national citizenship. Topics include racialization, class divides, gender, inequalities, queer and trans politics, and youth culture.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: South Asian Diaspora
oneLiner: Uses transnational and comparative frameworks to examine South Asian immigration to…
description: Uses transnational and comparative frameworks to examine South Asian immigration to various countries. How colonialism, nationalism, and the politics of race, gender, class, and sexuality shape diasporic identities and communities. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as RRS 657 and AA S 541. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Southeast Asians in the United States
oneLiner: A comparative exploration of Southeast Asian Americans by examining the histories and…
description: A comparative exploration of Southeast Asian Americans by examining the histories and experiences of Burmese, Cambodian, Filipina/o, Hmong, Indonesian, Lao, Mien, Mong, Vietnamese, and Thai Americans.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Women's Literature and the Arts
oneLiner: Works by Asian American women writers and artists.
description: Works by Asian American women writers and artists. How Asian American women are depicted in literature and the arts.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Sexualities
oneLiner: Introduction to Asian American queer theory and sexuality studies.
description: Introduction to Asian American queer theory and sexuality studies. Examination of how sexuality impacts the lived experience of immigration, race, gender, class, and generational differences among Asian Americans.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Religiosities
oneLiner: Major issues particular to the predicaments of Asian Americans and their religions.
description: Major issues particular to the predicaments of Asian Americans and their religions. Interdisciplinary and anchored in critical Asian American Studies perspectives constructed within the context of the intersections of race and religion.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian Americans and Environmental Justice
oneLiner: Examination of the environmental racism issues faced by Asian Americans and how their…
description: Examination of the environmental racism issues faced by Asian Americans and how their communities have organized for justice.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Media Workshop
oneLiner: Film and media arts as self-expression, a reflection of community, and a tool for…
description: Film and media arts as self-expression, a reflection of community, and a tool for activism in the Asian American community.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Community Health Issues
oneLiner: Examination of community health concepts and needs specific to the Asian American…
description: Examination of community health concepts and needs specific to the Asian American communities including practical skills in community health issues and service.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian Americans in Education
oneLiner: Exploration of the historical and contemporary narratives and counter-narratives of…
description: Exploration of the historical and contemporary narratives and counter-narratives of Asian Americans in education, development of Asian American Studies, pedagogical issues and interventions that have shaped their identities and communities, and the duality of education as a tool for oppression and as a means toward liberation. (Plus-minus ABC/NC, CR/NC)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Communities and Public Policy
oneLiner: Public policy issues and their impact on and the responses from the Asian American…
description: Public policy issues and their impact on and the responses from the Asian American communities. The relationship and complexities of local, state, and federal policies facing the Asian American communities. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian Transnational Communities
oneLiner: Examine the social, economic, political, and cultural realities of place and their…
description: Examine the social, economic, political, and cultural realities of place and their relationship with the formation of transnational Asian communities. Explore the impact of historic and contemporary Asian migration.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Community Changes and Development
oneLiner: Exploration of the sources, patterns, and processes of Asian American community change.
description: Exploration of the sources, patterns, and processes of Asian American community change. Sixty hours of community internship are required. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Projects in the Teaching of Asian American Studies
oneLiner: Academic service learning practicum/internship experience as an undergraduate…
description: Academic service learning practicum/internship experience as an undergraduate instructional aide. Participation in the teaching of a regular instructionally-related class. (Students may earn a maximum of 4 units toward the baccalaureate degree for any course(s) numbered 685 regardless of discipline.)
prereqNotes: Undergraduate students only; upper-division standing; 3.3 GPA in AA S courses; permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Community Service Internship
oneLiner: Supervised fieldwork/service for 100 hours minimum in an approved Asian American…
description: Supervised fieldwork/service for 100 hours minimum in an approved Asian American organization or agency, plus regular meetings with supervising faculty. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (CR/NC grading only) [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Approaches to Asian American Studies
oneLiner: Study of fundamental tools of critical thinking and theorization through the lens of…
description: Study of fundamental tools of critical thinking and theorization through the lens of Asian American Studies. Focus on reading, thinking, and writing critically by exposing topics and theories of Asian and Ethnic Studies. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Asian American Studies majors; 24 upper-division units in AA S courses; or permission of the instructor.

name: Proseminar in Asian American Studies
oneLiner: Practical application of research methodology in Asian American Studies through…
description: Practical application of research methodology in Asian American Studies through critical examination, analysis, and peer critique to develop a publishable product. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Asian American Studies majors; senior standing; AA S 696*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Supervised individual study of a particular issue in Asian American Studies.
description: Supervised individual study of a particular issue in Asian American Studies. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; 3.0 GPA; permission of the instructor and department chair.

name: Critical Approaches to Asian American Studies
oneLiner: Critical understanding of theory and research methodologies in Asian American Studies.
description: Critical understanding of theory and research methodologies in Asian American Studies. Review of available resources in preparation for graduate-level research. Guidance on the literature review and bibliography in the student's chosen area.
prereqNotes: Graduate Asian American Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Theory and History in Asian American Studies
oneLiner: Integration of historical review with contemporary theory relating to Asian Americans.
description: Integration of historical review with contemporary theory relating to Asian Americans.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar: Asian American Immigration
oneLiner: Theoretical and methodological understanding of Asian immigration to the U.S. and Asian…
description: Theoretical and methodological understanding of Asian immigration to the U.S. and Asian Americans within structures of American immigration history.
prereqNotes: Graduate Asian American Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar: Asian American Literature and Arts
oneLiner: Intersections of history, gender, culture, and creativity as they pertain to the…
description: Intersections of history, gender, culture, and creativity as they pertain to the conception of an Asian American literary aesthetic. Placing Asian American literature within the genre of U.S. literature.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Asian American Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar: Asian American Family and Identity
oneLiner: Issues concerning Asian Americans in family and group structures.
description: Issues concerning Asian Americans in family and group structures.
prereqNotes: Graduate Asian American Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Community and Public Policy
oneLiner: Assessment and critique of policy issues and their impact on, and the responses from…
description: Assessment and critique of policy issues and their impact on, and the responses from, the Asian American community. Relationship and complexities of local, state, and federal policies facing the contemporary Asian American community.
prereqNotes: Graduate Asian American Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Asian American Community Health Issues
oneLiner: Major health issues and their impact on, and the responses from, the Asian American…
description: Major health issues and their impact on, and the responses from, the Asian American community. Health perspectives and practices affected by the cultural dichotomy between Asia and Euro-America. (AB/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Graduate Asian American Studies and Healthcare Administration Certificate students or permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Asian American Educational Experience and Pedagogy
oneLiner: Historical narratives and counter-narratives of Asian Americans and education, the…
description: Historical narratives and counter-narratives of Asian Americans and education, the development of Asian American Studies, and pedagogical issues and interventions that have shaped Asian American identities and communities. (Plus-minus AB/NC grading only; RP allowed)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Creative Work Project
oneLiner: An original creative work.
description: An original creative work. Projects must be described in a written document that summarizes the project's relation to other work in the area, its rationale, its significance, and its creative methodologies. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor and department chair; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies before registration.

name: Field Study in Asian American Studies
oneLiner: An alternate culminating study in fulfillment of the requirement for the master's degree.
description: An alternate culminating study in fulfillment of the requirement for the master's degree. Students develop a project under the advisement and direction of a graduate adviser. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies before graduation.

name: Directed Reading in Asian American Studies
oneLiner: Directed reading in a specific area of Asian American studies based upon a standing…
description: Directed reading in a specific area of Asian American studies based upon a standing bibliography or reading list developed in consultation and under the supervision of a specialist in that field. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor and graduate adviser.

oneLiner: Study ethical issues and professional responsibilities in the accounting industry.
description: Study ethical issues and professional responsibilities in the accounting industry. Topics include understanding and applying guidance such as the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC), Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB), AICPA, Government Accountability Office (GAO), Treasury (IRS), and California State Board of Accountancy (CBA) Laws, Standards, Regulations, Codes of Professional Conduct, and Guidance. Exercises and case studies are used to apply these and other authoritative documents to examine decisions made by individuals at real-world entities. Meets the California Board of Accountancy accounting ethics education requirement for CPA licensure. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Business Administration: Concentration in Accounting majors and Accounting minors.

oneLiner: Legal rules and principles that apply to business transactions, including contracts…

(Plus-minus letter grade only)

Federal estate and gift taxation and income taxation of trusts and estates. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

oneLiner: Examination of corporate governance structures and the design and testing of internal…
description: Examination of corporate governance structures and the design and testing of internal controls related to financial reporting. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to either graduate Business students with ACCT 780; or SF State Scholars Accounting and Certificate in Accounting students. Graduate students in other majors permitted with the permission of the Faculty Director of Graduate Programs.

oneLiner: How to integrate data analytics into IT audit processes, allowing for more thorough and…
description: How to integrate data analytics into IT audit processes, allowing for more thorough and efficient examination of an organization's IT systems and processes. Emphasis on using data-driven techniques to extract data, assess risk, evaluate controls, and generate audit findings. Through hands-on assignments and case studies, develop practical skills in data extraction, preparation, analysis, and insight development tailored to audit objectives. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Business students with a grade of B- or better in ACCT 780; SF State Scholars Accounting students, and Certificate in Accounting students.

name: Seminar in Cost Accounting

description: Examination of organizational control and strategic performance evaluation, measurement issues, and current topics associated with cost accounting. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to either graduate Business students with ACCT 780, or SF State Scholars Accounting and Certificate in Accounting students. Graduate students in other majors permitted with the permission of the Faculty Director of Graduate Programs.

oneLiner: Examination of the complexities of recording and reporting for business combinations…

prereqNotes: Restricted to either graduate Business students with ACCT 801 (may be taken concurrently); or SF State Scholars Accounting and Certificate in Accounting students. Graduate students in other majors permitted with the permission of the Faculty Director of Graduate Programs.

oneLiner: Development of the abilities required to conduct cybersecurity audits and cybersecurity…

Discussion of cybersecurity audit principles, cybersecurity risk management concepts, mandatory disclosure regulations, and voluntary disclosure practices on cybersecurity topics. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to either graduate Business students with a grade of B- or better in ACCT 780, or SF State Scholars Accounting and Certificate in Accounting students.

name: Independent Study

name: Textiles
oneLiner: Fiber, yarn, and fabric terminology and production with an emphasis on the chemical…
description: Fiber, yarn, and fabric terminology and production with an emphasis on the chemical impact the fiber/textile industry has on the environment. Scientific innovations in fiber technology and dyeing, printing, finishing, and consumer care techniques.
prereqNotes: Restricted to sophomore standing and above.

name: Apparel Construction: Industry Methods
oneLiner: Hands-on training in garment construction using fashion industry methods and equipment…
description: Hands-on training in garment construction using fashion industry methods and equipment from pattern analysis to final pressing. Gain skills in factory-standard sewing machines, pressing systems, and production-style workstations while developing professional techniques, vocabulary, and quality benchmarks to meet industry standards for apparel production and manufacturer collaboration. May be repeated for up to 6 units. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Apparel Design and Merchandising majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Fashion Illustration and Design Communication
oneLiner: Explore illustration and visualization techniques used in the fashion industry to…
description: Explore illustration and visualization techniques used in the fashion industry to communicate design concepts and technical details. Emphasis on developing skills in garment rendering, technical communication, and visual storytelling through a combination of digital and traditional methods. Includes the creation of professional mood boards, fashion figures, and technical sketches using computer-aided and emerging design tools to support product development and presentation. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Apparel Design and Merchandising majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to the Fashion Industry
oneLiner: In-depth exploration of the fashion industry, focusing on the design, manufacturing…
description: In-depth exploration of the fashion industry, focusing on the design, manufacturing, and distribution of textile and apparel products for various markets. Comprehensive study of the processes involved in creating fashion products, from initial design concepts to final market distribution. Explore diverse career opportunities within all market segments, providing insights into professional pathways in the global fashion industry.

name: Designers of the 20th and 21st Centuries
oneLiner: The impact that outstanding 20th and 21st century designers have on the fashion industry.
description: The impact that outstanding 20th and 21st century designers have on the fashion industry. Examination of the creative processes and business strategies of diverse designers that define contemporary fashion.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Fashion, Clothing, and Society - GWAR
oneLiner: Social, psychological, and economic forces which underlie fashion and affect both the…
description: Social, psychological, and economic forces which underlie fashion and affect both the consumer and the clothing industry. The function of clothing for diverse individuals and communities. Issues of social justice related to appearance, clothing, and the fashion industry.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Apparel Design and Merchandising majors; GE Area 1A/A2.

name: Apparel Design I: Patternmaking Foundations
oneLiner: Introduction to flat patternmaking through the development and manipulation of slopers…
description: Introduction to flat patternmaking through the development and manipulation of slopers as the foundation of apparel design. Emphasis on accuracy, fit analysis, and pattern adjustments for diverse body types. Techniques focus on creating balanced, production-ready patterns while applying professional standards in drafting and documentation. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.

name: Apparel Design II: Advanced Patternmaking with 2D/3D CAD
oneLiner: Advanced patternmaking techniques using traditional drafting alongside digital methods.
description: Advanced patternmaking techniques using traditional drafting alongside digital methods. Development of technical expertise through creation of advanced garments while learning to visualize, test, and refine designs through 2D pattern software and 3D virtual prototyping. Emphasis on digital workflows, fit and technical specifications, and sustainability practices that reflect evolving industry standards. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: ADM 261* and ADM 361*.

name: Textile Laboratory
oneLiner: Yarn and cloth identification and textile fiber identification through microscopic and…
description: Yarn and cloth identification and textile fiber identification through microscopic and chemical testing. Stain removal, detergency, dye, and finish tests. Laboratory.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Apparel Design and Merchandising majors.

name: Forecasting Apparel and Interior Design Trends
oneLiner: Forces in society that influence apparel and interior design trends.
description: Forces in society that influence apparel and interior design trends. Data used to develop trend reports, color reports, and retail reports. Culminating in a professional forecasting presentation of colors, silhouettes, fabrications, and lifestyles. (This course is offered as ADM 366 and ID 366. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: College-level drawing class or consent of the instructor.

name: Fashion Merchandising and Buying
oneLiner: Explore factors that affect the merchandising and management of fashion products with…

Apply the principles of visual presentation to trend boards, online merchandising layouts, and in window displays. Principles and methods of promotion for manufacturers and retailers. (Extra fee required).
prereqNotes: Restricted to Apparel Design and Merchandising majors.

name: Supply Chain Management in the Textile and Apparel World Marketplace
oneLiner: World textile and apparel production and consumption.
description: World textile and apparel production and consumption. U.S. apparel import program including domestic policies and international agreements. U.S. textile and apparel exports, international apparel manufacturers, and retailers.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; a GWAR course.

name: Culture and Historical Costume

name: Fashion and the Consumer

prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Apparel Design and Merchandising majors; ADM 360GW*.

name: Visual Merchandising and Promotion

Practice with equipment, materials, and techniques used in the presentation of merchandise. Principles and methods of promotion for manufacturers and retailers. [CSL may be available] (FCS 769/ADM 569 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Apparel Design & Merchandising graduating seniors; ID 240; a college-level drawing class; concurrent enrollment in ADM 560 and FCS 600; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Advanced Apparel Design
oneLiner: Advanced apparel design related to diverse populations.
description: Advanced apparel design related to diverse populations. Development of design prototypes based on creative research and market analyses. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (FCS 761/ADM 661 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Apparel Design & Merchandising graduating seniors; ADM 361 and ADM 362; concurrent enrollment in ADM 560 and FCS 600; GPA of 2.5 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

description: Design, merchandising, and quality assurance in the apparel and sewn products industry. Development and implementation of a design idea geared to a specific market.

oneLiner: Exploration of variable topics and techniques in apparel design.
description: Exploration of variable topics and techniques in apparel design. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit.
