name: American Indians in Contemporary U.S. History
oneLiner: Overview of the historical lived realities of major indigenous cultures and people…
description: Overview of the historical lived realities of major indigenous cultures and people residing within the present day boundaries of the United States from 1930 through 2000. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Modern Creative and Performing Arts
oneLiner: Individual and group performance of creative and performing arts in American Indian…
description: Individual and group performance of creative and performing arts in American Indian communities. Fine art, oral poetry, dramatic modes, and media. Adaptation of traditional modes to modern situations.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; AIS 100*; or permission of the instructor.

name: State Terrorism and Native Abolition
oneLiner: Examine the intersection of race, gender, and class in the context of the history of…
description: Examine the intersection of race, gender, and class in the context of the history of anti-terrorism laws and policies both domestically and internationally. Explore how Native peoples have experienced and struggled against state regimes of national security and social stability. Highlighting how states use terrorism to control Native lands, resources, labor, and Native forms of opposition and the unique worldviews that inform that opposition.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: American Indian Studies Senior Seminar
oneLiner: Directed guidance leading to the completion of a senior research project based on…
description: Directed guidance leading to the completion of a senior research project based on intensive study of a topic or problem related to American Indian peoples. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: AIS 300 and AIS 694.

name: Projects in the Teaching of American Indian Studies
oneLiner: Academic service-learning practicum/internship experience as an undergraduate…
description: Academic service-learning practicum/internship experience as an undergraduate instructional aide. Participation in the teaching of a regular instructionally-related class. Limited to undergraduate students only. (Students may earn a maximum of 4 units toward the baccalaureate degree for any course(s) numbered 685 regardless of discipline.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; permission of the instructor.

name: Community Service Learning
oneLiner: Community service learning support course.
description: Community service learning support course. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Supervised, individual study of a particular problem in American Indian studies.
description: Supervised, individual study of a particular problem in American Indian studies. Students may select the supervisor and must state the problem, method of data gathering, and method of data analysis. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in American Indian Studies
oneLiner: Issues in the study of American Indians: understanding of the Indian tribes and nations…
description: Issues in the study of American Indians: understanding of the Indian tribes and nations as sovereign political entities; political, economic, and social developments of self-determination and its implications for Indian tribes.
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor.

name: Self, Place, and Knowing: Introduction to Interdisciplinary Inquiry
oneLiner: Introduction to Liberal Studies, American Studies, the practice of interdisciplinary…
description: Introduction to Liberal Studies, American Studies, the practice of interdisciplinary inquiry, and the culmination of the first-year experience sequence. Project-based focus on different ways of understanding oneself in relationship the University, and San Francisco and the larger Bay Area. Emphasis on experiential learning through mapping (exploring, navigating, understanding, and cataloging). [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as LS 200 and AMST 200. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2* or permission of the instructor.

name: Values in American Life
oneLiner: Explores the ideas, concepts, and values that have been central to how Americans…
description: Explores the ideas, concepts, and values that have been central to how Americans understand themselves and the United States as a nation. Focuses on literature, film, music, visual culture, and popular culture in a historical context. Emphasis on analytical skills, close reading practices, and critical thinking. (This course is offered as HUM 225, AMST 225, and ENG 225. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: Christmas and Hanukkah in the United States
oneLiner: Examination of the social, political, and cultural history of Christmas and Hanukkah in…
description: Examination of the social, political, and cultural history of Christmas and Hanukkah in the United States from the colonial period to the present day. Focus on the relationship between religion, politics, commerce, and popular culture, including gender roles and the changing role of religious, ethnic, and racial minorities in U.S. public culture. (This course is offered as JS 265, AMST 265, HIST 265, and RELS 265. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: Junior Seminar in American Studies - GWAR
oneLiner: Examination of selected topics in U.S. culture and society through the…
description: Examination of selected topics in U.S. culture and society through the interdisciplinary lens of American Studies. Writing-intensive seminar. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GE Area 1A/A2; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Arts and American Culture
oneLiner: Figures in visual, literary, and performing arts who have reflected American culture…
description: Figures in visual, literary, and performing arts who have reflected American culture through the mastery of their arts. The relationships between arts in periods of American cultural development. (This course is offered as HUM 485 and AMST 310. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: California Culture
oneLiner: Dynamics of California society, literature, and culture in recent times: world oasis…
description: Dynamics of California society, literature, and culture in recent times: world oasis, flawed paradise, lifestyle crucible, and creative milieu. The function of California in American culture and Pacific relations. (This course is offered as HUM 450, ENG 450, and AMST 410. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
oneLiner: Overview of the scientific evidence for the origin and evolution of the human species.
description: Overview of the scientific evidence for the origin and evolution of the human species. Examine the biological and behavioral diversity of living and past human populations and the closest mammalian relatives - the non-human primates. Introduction to topics that include natural selection and the mechanisms of evolution; molecular and population genetics; primate diversity and behavior; the fossil record of human evolution, behavior, and ecology; and human biocultural adaptation.

name: Introduction to Archaeology
oneLiner: Overview of the methods and practices of archaeology, including how archaeologists…
description: Overview of the methods and practices of archaeology, including how archaeologists study the material remains of past human life and culture. Topics include identification and excavation of sites, artifact analysis, plant, animal, and human relationships in the past, museum practice, and the politics of archaeology in the present.

name: Introduction to Social and Cultural Anthropology
oneLiner: Principles and concepts of sociocultural anthropology.
description: Principles and concepts of sociocultural anthropology. People and environment. Social relations: kinship, religion, social control, and racism. Social change and applied anthropology.

name: Introduction to Visual Anthropology
oneLiner: The role of film, photography, digital, and multimedia in the examination of human…
description: The role of film, photography, digital, and multimedia in the examination of human diversity. The study of visual aspects of human behavior and the use of visual media in research and visual anthropology. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

name: Foundations of Anthropology: History
oneLiner: Theoretical foundations of anthropology: major trends in anthropological thought and…
description: Theoretical foundations of anthropology: major trends in anthropological thought and practice up to the present.
prereqNotes: ANTH 120.

name: Foundations of Archaeology
oneLiner: Examine the history of archaeological thinking from the antiquarians of the Middle Ages…
description: Examine the history of archaeological thinking from the antiquarians of the Middle Ages to today's use of archaeology by modern politicians and activists. How do people use sites, artifacts, monuments, burials, and art to construct accurate histories and prehistories? What theories and philosophical approaches help people understand the archaeological record? Is archaeology a hard science based on objective facts, or is it a social science that uses subjective knowledge? How do people know what they know about their own and other peoples' past? (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; ANTH 110; or permission of the instructor.

name: Foundations of Human Variation
oneLiner: Examines the nature and extent of heritable differences among human populations from an…
description: Examines the nature and extent of heritable differences among human populations from an evolutionary perspective. The role of genetics and environment in the formation of these differences is considered, as well as the social and biological concept of race.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; ANTH 100* or a college biology course*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Foundations of Visual Anthropology
oneLiner: Introduces and develops theory in visual anthropology.
description: Introduces and develops theory in visual anthropology. Explores major research paradigms in the field including kinesics (proxemics and dance), painting and related arts, photography, commercial, ethnographic and applied film, indigenous media, multimedia, and multimodal anthropology, and museums and audience research. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; ANTH 130; or permission of the instructor.

name: Writing Anthropology - GWAR
oneLiner: Advanced development of writing skills in anthropology focusing on descriptive…
description: Advanced development of writing skills in anthropology focusing on descriptive, interpretive, critical analyses, popular media, and scholarly research. Regional or topical theme varies. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2*; ANTH 120.

name: Regional Ethnography
oneLiner: Apply a cultural area study approach to people and cultures around the world.
description: Apply a cultural area study approach to people and cultures around the world. Focus on the history and contemporary cultures of East Asia, Central America, West Africa, and North America. Topic to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Racism: Cross-Cultural Analysis
oneLiner: The cultural history of racism as related to colonialism and imperialism.
description: The cultural history of racism as related to colonialism and imperialism. Racism as an on-going intellectual and political movement. Anti-racism and educational-anthropological methods to defeat racism. (This course is offered as ANTH 320 and CST 320. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or consent of the instructor.

name: Endangered Cultures
oneLiner: The interaction between non-industrial and industrial societies with a focus on…
description: The interaction between non-industrial and industrial societies with a focus on cultural degradation and extermination of non-industrial societies beginning 150 years ago.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Work, Money, and Power
oneLiner: Exploration of the cultural production of class and status in a comparative perspective.
description: Exploration of the cultural production of class and status in a comparative perspective. Reading of theoretical texts and ethnographies, exploration of class markers, and the production of distinction in students' own lives.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Origins of Art and Visual Representation
oneLiner: Examination of the emergence and development of art and visual representation as a…
description: Examination of the emergence and development of art and visual representation as a human social, political, cognitive, and aesthetic behavior. Geographic coverage is global; temporal coverage from early humans through (pre)history. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropology and Film
oneLiner: Social and cultural anthropology through films, ethnographies, and popular writings of…
description: Social and cultural anthropology through films, ethnographies, and popular writings of anthropologists. (This course is offered as ANTH 327 and CINE 327. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Primate Behavior
oneLiner: Explore the social lives of all primates.
description: Explore the social lives of all primates. Topics include social organization, cooperation/competition, reproduction, communication, and the interrelationship between behavior and ecology. Includes behavioral observations of primates at the zoo. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Women and Work
oneLiner: Position and roles of women in the productive activities of society, both paid and unpaid.
description: Position and roles of women in the productive activities of society, both paid and unpaid. Patterns of household and workplace employment, discrimination in pay and working conditions, relevant laws, and explanations for the evolution of these patterns. (This course is offered as LABR 343 and ANTH 343. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Archaeology of California
oneLiner: Prehistoric heritage of California's Native American cultures studied in the…
description: Prehistoric heritage of California's Native American cultures studied in the comparative light of ethnohistoric and ethnographic data. Archaeological focus on culture-history, economy, settlement pattern, ecology, political organization, and processual adaptation.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Media and Dissent
oneLiner: Examination of contemporary visual culture, particularly commercial culture, for its…
description: Examination of contemporary visual culture, particularly commercial culture, for its impact on personal and collective identity. Technical aspects of creating and altering visual media. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. (This course is offered as SOC 420 and ANTH 420. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2, 1B/A3, 1C/A1, and 2/B4.

name: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Greece
oneLiner: Survey of Greek material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the…
description: Survey of Greek material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the Bronze Age to the second century CE. (This course is offered as CLAR 420, ANTH 424, ARTH 401, and M S 420. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Rome
oneLiner: Survey of Roman material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the…
description: Survey of Roman material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the foundation of Rome to the reign of Justinian. (This course is offered as CLAR 425, ANTH 425, ARTH 402, and M S 425. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Historical Archaeology
oneLiner: Introduction to historical archaeology, key themes in historical archaeology, critical…
description: Introduction to historical archaeology, key themes in historical archaeology, critical examination of methods, development of historical archaeology, key theoretical approaches, and case studies in historical archaeology. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: ANTH 110 or permission of the instructor.

name: Archaeology of Mexico and Central America
oneLiner: Overview of the prehistory and archaeology of what is now the nation-states of Mexico…
description: Overview of the prehistory and archaeology of what is now the nation-states of Mexico and Central America.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Special Topics in Anthropology
oneLiner: Focused study of a special topic of current interest in the field of anthropology…
description: Focused study of a special topic of current interest in the field of anthropology consisting of current academic literature readings, class discussion, and individual or group-based projects. Some topics may include a community service learning component. Topics to be specified in the class schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary. (Plus-minus letter grades only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Latin America: The National Period
oneLiner: Latin America since independence (c. 1825).
description: Latin America since independence (c. 1825). Histories of Latin American peoples: culture, race relations, women, political oppression and resistance, the economy, and development. (This course is offered as HIST 358 [Formerly HIST 501], ANTH 501, and LTNS 501. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Diversity in the Workplace
oneLiner: An overview of workplace diversity and strategies to utilize it positively.
description: An overview of workplace diversity and strategies to utilize it positively. Theoretical debates and issues related to race, ethnic origin, gender, sexual orientation, class, age, and disability. Ways in which individuals and organizations can maximize benefits by respecting and working with diversity. (This course is offered as LABR 525 and ANTH 525. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Human Osteology Practicum
oneLiner: Human skeleton, bone dynamics, and anthropometric and morphological analysis of modern…
description: Human skeleton, bone dynamics, and anthropometric and morphological analysis of modern and fossil skeletal materials. Research on osteological and fossil materials. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (ANTH 730/ANTH 530 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; ANTH 100; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Fossil Humans Practicum
oneLiner: The fossil evidence for human evolution.
description: The fossil evidence for human evolution. Comparative primate anatomy and function including skeletal morphology of hominid fossils. Ecological and geological settings. Trends and processes in human evolution. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (ANTH 731/ANTH 531 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Paleopathology
oneLiner: Bioarchaeology of disease and human health.
description: Bioarchaeology of disease and human health. Evolutionary, cultural, and biological factors of prehistoric epidemiology. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (ANTH 735/ANTH 535 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Pompeii & Herculaneum: Cities in the Shadow of Vesuvius
oneLiner: Core aspects of archaeology, daily life, art, and history in the ancient cities of…
description: Core aspects of archaeology, daily life, art, and history in the ancient cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum. (This course is offered as CLAR 545 [formerly paired with CLAR 845], ANTH 544, and HIST 324. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Bioarchaeology
oneLiner: Reconstruction of past lifeways from the examination of the human skeleton.
description: Reconstruction of past lifeways from the examination of the human skeleton. Patterns of subsistence, diet, disease, demography, and physical activity reconstructed from skeletal populations.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropology of the Body
oneLiner: Comparative cross-cultural approach to the study of the individual in society as…
description: Comparative cross-cultural approach to the study of the individual in society as mediated through an anthropological inquiry of the body. Social construction of the body and self in everyday life and ways that cultural practices, social structures, and psychological tents are inscribed and reproduced through the body and bodies.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Urban Anthropology
oneLiner: Impact of urban environments upon human behavior cross-culturally.
description: Impact of urban environments upon human behavior cross-culturally. Ethnographic fieldwork techniques, the history and theoretical roots of urban anthropology, and case studies from around the world. (This course is offered as ANTH 555 and USP 555. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; USP 400 or one course in cultural anthropology.

name: Ethnography of Urban Inequality
oneLiner: Participant-observation fieldwork techniques with hands-on research projects in…
description: Participant-observation fieldwork techniques with hands-on research projects in inner-city communities in the Bay Area. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. (This course is offered as ANTH 557 and USP 557. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Cross-Cultural Aspects of Sex and Gender
oneLiner: Cross-cultural aspects of sex, sexuality, and gender.
description: Cross-cultural aspects of sex, sexuality, and gender. The control of sexuality, cultural components of gender role and gender identity, and symbolic aspects of sex and gender. (This course is offered as ANTH 569 and SXS 567. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropology and Folklore
oneLiner: Nature and form of folklore, its cultural setting, transmissions, and dynamics.
description: Nature and form of folklore, its cultural setting, transmissions, and dynamics. Psychological, ethnic, and philosophical considerations of folklore and its relationship to drama, art, and music.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Globalization and World Cultures
oneLiner: Effects of globalization and multinational corporations on cultures.
description: Effects of globalization and multinational corporations on cultures. Examination of contemporary globalization from combined political-economic and cultural anthropological perspectives. Understandings of social movements, world building and popular culture (video games, music, manga and related new media) to study and imagine different ways of engaging with the world. Explore multimodal platforms to explore critical social thought and anthropological ideas. (This course is offered as ANTH 585 and CST 585. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Feminist Anthropology
oneLiner: Ethnographic, physical, anthropological, and prehistorical topics related to women.
description: Ethnographic, physical, anthropological, and prehistorical topics related to women. Theories on origins of the family, social structuring of sexuality, and changing sex and gender in modern societies. (This course is offered as ANTH 590, CST 590, and WGS 595. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2.

name: Archaeological Methods
oneLiner: Overview of archaeological practices in academic, government, and private-sector settings.
description: Overview of archaeological practices in academic, government, and private-sector settings. Introduction to archaeological project research design, archaeological fieldwork, artifact analysis, and collections management. Special topics include federal and state cultural heritage protection legislation, museum practice, and repatriation. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: ANTH 110.

name: Zooarchaeology
oneLiner: Introduction to zooarchaeological studies of animal remains including the development…
description: Introduction to zooarchaeological studies of animal remains including the development of zooarchaeology. Exploration of key themes, theoretical and methodological approaches in zooarchaeology, critical evaluation of analytical techniques, and practicums in zooarchaeology. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; ANTH 110; or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropological Filmmaking I
oneLiner: Introduction to ethnographic digital video production, including methods of…
description: Introduction to ethnographic digital video production, including methods of ethnographic fieldwork, the creation of field notes and research design. The basics of digital video planning, production, and editing. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as ANTH 595 and CINE 635. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Anthropology and Cinema majors, minors or ethnography certificate students; ANTH 120 and ANTH 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropological Filmmaking II
oneLiner: Advanced filmmaking-based applied anthropological fieldwork, collaboration, and digital…
description: Advanced filmmaking-based applied anthropological fieldwork, collaboration, and digital post-production techniques. Students complete a video for which they conducted research during the previous semester. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as ANTH 596 and CINE 636. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Anthropology and Cinema majors, minors, and ethnography certificate Students; ANTH 595* or CINE 635*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Approaches to the African Past
oneLiner: Explore the different methodologies for studying the African past, including…
description: Explore the different methodologies for studying the African past, including archaeology, anthropology, oral traditions, and history. (This course is offered as HIST 366 and ANTH 609. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Medical Anthropology
oneLiner: The interplay of culture, genetics, population, and the environment.
description: The interplay of culture, genetics, population, and the environment. Cross-cultural medical education. Folk and urban medical systems as moral, social, and cognitive systems.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: STEM and Social Justice
oneLiner: Introduction to the anthropology of society, technology, and medicine (STM) and to the…
description: Introduction to the anthropology of society, technology, and medicine (STM) and to the field of science and technology studies (STS). Key themes include the history of studying STM in Anthropology, theoretical concepts in STS, and the critical evaluation of case studies. Topics and case studies to be addressed include indigenous science, race and gender in STM fields, anthropological studies of science and scientists, biomedicine and biotechnology, the social consequences of computational algorithms, surveillance technology and privacy rights, work and class in online 'platform' economies, STM and identity, and the social justice dimensions of STM.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Ethnographic Field Methods
oneLiner: Anthropological data-gathering methods including participant observation, scheduled and…
description: Anthropological data-gathering methods including participant observation, scheduled and open-ended interviews, life history, survey, questionnaire, projective techniques, and electronic aids. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. May be repeated for a total of 8 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropological Statistics
oneLiner: Methods and techniques for analysis of data: collecting and describing data…
description: Methods and techniques for analysis of data: collecting and describing data, statistical inference and hypothesis testing, parametric and non-parametric techniques, and SPSS training for data analysis. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Anthropological Film
oneLiner: Philosophical and historical overview of anthropology and filmmaking, from traditional…
description: Philosophical and historical overview of anthropology and filmmaking, from traditional styles to mass market anthropology, textual and reflexive turns, and applied visual anthropology. (ANTH 755/ANTH 655 [Formerly ANTH 620] is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Ethnography of Dance
oneLiner: The function of dance in society in the context of anthropological literature. (This…
description: The function of dance in society in the context of anthropological literature. (This course is offered as DANC 657 and ANTH 657. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Senior Thesis
oneLiner: Provides qualified students the opportunity to undertake a senior thesis.
description: Provides qualified students the opportunity to undertake a senior thesis. Supervised study of a topic mutually agreed upon by student and faculty. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: ANTH 100, ANTH 110, ANTH 120, and ANTH 300 with grades of B or better; major GPA of 3.25 or better.

name: Anthropology Internship
oneLiner: Internship in research, governmental and non-governmental agencies, museums, and other…
description: Internship in research, governmental and non-governmental agencies, museums, and other public and private institutions. Students must find an anthropology faculty to serve as the academic supervisor. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: ANTH 300 or ANTH 301 or ANTH 302; and permission of the academic supervisor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Supervised, individual study of a particular problem in anthropology.
description: Supervised, individual study of a particular problem in anthropology. The student must state the problem, method of data-gathering, and the method of data-analysis. May be repeated provided that the area of study is different. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; permission of major adviser, department chair, and instructor.

name: Sexual Cultures, Sexual Identities
oneLiner: Concepts of "sexual culture" and "sexual identity" in history and across cultures.…
description: Concepts of "sexual culture" and "sexual identity" in history and across cultures. (This course is offered as SXS 701 and ANTH 701. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Proseminar in Anthropological Theory and Method
oneLiner: Directed application of anthropological theory, methods, and research techniques.
description: Directed application of anthropological theory, methods, and research techniques. Cannot be repeated for credit.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing in Anthropology or permission of the instructor. Must be taken before or concurrently with other graduate seminars.

name: Anthropological Ethics
oneLiner: Exploration of the ethical principles and practices in the subfields of Anthropology.
description: Exploration of the ethical principles and practices in the subfields of Anthropology. Emphasis on the history of human subjects research and the principles guiding data collection from or related to human populations, with the opportunity for hands-on practice of these principles in research situations and professional activities. Discussion of the subfield ethics and the Institutional Review Board (IRB) process, how to develop research projects and proposals that meet ethical requisites, and ethical issues and debates in Anthropology. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Research Skills: The Craft of Anthropological Writing
oneLiner: Strategies to enhance creative thinking.
description: Strategies to enhance creative thinking. Advanced review of grammar and sentence construction. Planning of MA thesis argument and organization. Dominant writing styles in anthropology understood through the study of Author's Guides to publishing in major journals. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing; concurrent enrollment in ANTH 710; or permission of the instructor.

name: Research Skills: The Literature Review
oneLiner: The importance of qualitative and quantitative literature reviews in academic research.
description: The importance of qualitative and quantitative literature reviews in academic research. Finding the problem and contending with information glut. Advanced online and offline search skills. Avoiding plagiarism, using evidence matrices, synthesizing data, and mastering the authorial tone. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Research Skills: The Research Proposal
oneLiner: Developing the research question, originality, and timeliness.
description: Developing the research question, originality, and timeliness. Defining the research context and specific qualities and antecedents. Selecting the appropriate research method, suitability, practicality, and availability. Contending with ethical constraints and necessary permissions. (Plus-minus letter grade only.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Research Skills: The Research Presentation
oneLiner: Discussion of what goes into the most effective deliveries of both oral and poster…
description: Discussion of what goes into the most effective deliveries of both oral and poster presentations. Focus on understanding the principles of good design, using presentation software, effective charts and graphics, and crafting a clear, compelling, and technically accurate presentation that is appropriate to a professional setting. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate Anthropology students or permission of the instructor.

name: Foundations in Visual Anthropology
oneLiner: Classic and contemporary literature in visual anthropology: proxemics and kinesics…
description: Classic and contemporary literature in visual anthropology: proxemics and kinesics, semiological studies, indigenous media, shared and sensory anthropological filmmaking, the archive as active, and three approaches to photography: colonialist, Photovoice, and photo-elicitation. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing in Anthropology or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Archaeological Problems
oneLiner: Archaeological approaches and explanations of the past understood through key works in…
description: Archaeological approaches and explanations of the past understood through key works in interpretive archaeology and examples of the major archaeological theories. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing in Anthropology or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Biological Anthropology
oneLiner: Historical and contemporary primary literature in biological anthropology.
description: Historical and contemporary primary literature in biological anthropology. The importance of evolutionary theory, primatology, the primate fossil record, human diversity, anthropological genetics, and NAGPRA to anthropology. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing in Anthropology or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Problems in Cultural Anthropology
oneLiner: Advanced exploration of literature in contemporary schools in cultural anthropology.
description: Advanced exploration of literature in contemporary schools in cultural anthropology. Topics include post-structuralism, cultural materialism, neo-evolutionism, and symbolic anthropology. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing in Anthropology or permission of the instructor.

name: Human Osteology Practicum
oneLiner: Human skeleton, bone dynamics, and anthropometric and morphological analysis of modern…
description: Human skeleton, bone dynamics, and anthropometric and morphological analysis of modern and fossil skeletal materials. Research on osteological and fossil materials. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (ANTH 730/ANTH 530 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing.

name: Fossil Humans Practicum
oneLiner: The fossil evidence for human evolution.
description: The fossil evidence for human evolution. Comparative primate anatomy and function including skeletal morphology of hominid fossils. Ecological and geological settings. Trends and processes in human evolution. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (ANTH 731/ANTH 531 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Paleopathology
oneLiner: Bioarchaeology of disease and human health.
description: Bioarchaeology of disease and human health. Evolutionary, cultural, and biological factors of prehistoric epidemiology. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (ANTH 735/ANTH 535 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing.

name: History of Anthropological Film
oneLiner: Philosophical and historical overview of anthropology and filmmaking, from traditional…
description: Philosophical and historical overview of anthropology and filmmaking, from traditional styles to mass market anthropology, textual and reflexive turns, and applied visual anthropology. (ANTH 755/ANTH 655 [Formerly ANTH 620] is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Creative Work Project
oneLiner: Original creative project demonstrating artistic or professional achievement, clarity…
description: Original creative project demonstrating artistic or professional achievement, clarity of purpose, and integration of knowledge and techniques acquired in the student's area of study. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) for the Master of Arts and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

name: Master's Thesis
oneLiner: Original research thesis demonstrating critical and independent thinking, clarity of…
description: Original research thesis demonstrating critical and independent thinking, clarity of purpose, and thorough documentation. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor and chair of the thesis committee; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Individual research into a problem in anthropology.
description: Individual research into a problem in anthropology. The student must state the problem, method of data-gathering, and method of data analysis. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: ANTH 710; permission of the student's graduate major adviser, department chair, and supervising faculty member.

name: First Semester Arabic
oneLiner: Basic elementary Arabic.
description: Basic elementary Arabic. Conversation in the language, diction, reading, study of the fundamentals of grammar, simple oral and written exercises, and an introduction to Arabic-speaking cultures.

name: Second Semester Arabic
oneLiner: Continuation of First Semester Arabic.
description: Continuation of First Semester Arabic.
prereqNotes: ARAB 101 or equivalent.

name: Reading Qur'anic Arabic
oneLiner: An introduction to readings of the Qur'an, with an emphasis on oral quality and…
description: An introduction to readings of the Qur'an, with an emphasis on oral quality and literary value.
prereqNotes: Completion of al-Kitaab Part 1 or equivalent, or at least four semesters of Arabic or equivalent. For native speakers, permission of the instructor.

name: Contemporary Arabic and Arab American Literature
oneLiner: Contemporary literature from Arab American and Arabic speaking communities and their…
description: Contemporary literature from Arab American and Arabic speaking communities and their diasporas. Exploration of the political and cultural context of the Arab region by using poetry and fiction as a foundation. (This course is offered as RRS 450 and ARAB 450. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Digital Media Arts
oneLiner: The fundamentals, principles, and tools for 2D/3D graphics, time-based media, and…
description: The fundamentals, principles, and tools for 2D/3D graphics, time-based media, and interactive art. Examination of aesthetics, visual and verbal language, and art historical and current practices in the media. Activity.

name: Introduction to Textile Art
oneLiner: Studio experiences correlating textile media with basic techniques and processes.
description: Studio experiences correlating textile media with basic techniques and processes. Activity. Extra fee required.

name: Introduction to Drawing
oneLiner: Studio experiences with dry and wet materials.
description: Studio experiences with dry and wet materials. Visual translation of three-dimensional objects to a two-dimensional surface, as well as approaches to copying, abstraction, and pattern using linear, tonal and volumetric indication, and perspective, with attention to composition. Activity. Extra fee required.

name: Introduction to Printmaking
oneLiner: Studio experiences correlating drawing and printmaking media with basic techniques and…
description: Studio experiences correlating drawing and printmaking media with basic techniques and processes. Activity. Extra fee required.

oneLiner: Studio experiences exploring sculptural, theoretical, and visual processes using a…
description: Studio experiences exploring sculptural, theoretical, and visual processes using a variety of materials, methods, and context as a means of investigation. Emphasis on personal creative growth and development. Activity. Extra fee required.

name: Introduction to Ceramics
oneLiner: Studio experiences correlating clay media with basic techniques and processes.
description: Studio experiences correlating clay media with basic techniques and processes. Activity. Extra fee required.

name: Introduction to the Darkroom
oneLiner: Introduction to black and white film processing, darkroom printing, operation of 35mm…
description: Introduction to black and white film processing, darkroom printing, operation of 35mm film cameras, and photography as a creative medium. 35mm camera with manually adjustable apertures and shutter speeds required. Activity. Extra fee required.

oneLiner: Exploration and development of digital media and skills within an interdisciplinary…
description: Exploration and development of digital media and skills within an interdisciplinary studio art context with an emphasis on concept-driven strategies. Includes 2D and 3D graphics, time-based media (video/sound), and topics such as 3D printing, web development, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, 360-degree video productions, and interactive media. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; a 200-level ART course; or permission of the instructor.

name: Art Handling Workshop
oneLiner: Introduction to best and safe practices for preparing artworks for exhibition or…
description: Introduction to best and safe practices for preparing artworks for exhibition or transport. Hands-on practicum in a variety of methods and skills needed in the field of art handling and for personal art practice. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary. Activity. (Credit/No Credit)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Foundations in Fiber and Textiles
oneLiner: Further studio skills development in textile arts and design.
description: Further studio skills development in textile arts and design. Exploration of surface design, dyeing, fabrication, and building through technical exercises in hand manipulation of cloth, fiber, yarn, and other continuous elements. A range of contemporary, historical, and cultural textiles will be used as a touchstone for how contemporary creative work can be informed and contextualized. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; a 200-level ART class or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Foundations in Painting
oneLiner: Exploration and development of a painting practice with an emphasis on translating…
description: Exploration and development of a painting practice with an emphasis on translating three dimensions into two using color, value, and mark-making toward representational ends. Traditional and non-traditional approaches to starting, developing, and resolving paintings. How to distinguish and articulate quality and meaning in works of art. Activity. Extra fee required. [Formerly ART 430]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 231* or equivalent.

name: Foundations in Printmaking Processes: Drawing the Multiple
oneLiner: Overview of traditional printmaking processes that utilize drawing and the hand-made mark.
description: Overview of traditional printmaking processes that utilize drawing and the hand-made mark. Emphasis on developing students' fluency in materials and connecting printmaking processes and history with contemporary practice. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; a 200-level ART class or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Foundations in Contemporary Sculpture: Materials & Concepts
oneLiner: Development of contemporary sculpture material research and conceptual strategies.

prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; a 200-level ART class; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Foundations of ceramics including material, technique and applications, historic…
description: Foundations of ceramics including material, technique and applications, historic relevance, and contemporary art. Emphasis placed on process, hand-building construction techniques, experimentation, and context of ceramic works. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Foundations in Photography
oneLiner: Digital camera operation, color photography, image processing, workflow, digital image…
description: Digital camera operation, color photography, image processing, workflow, digital image processing, and inkjet printing. Combines technical exercises with conceptual themes in historical and contemporary photography. Digital camera required. Activity. Extra fee required. [Formerly ART 560]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; one 200-level ART course or equivalent.

name: Foundations in Darkroom Photography
oneLiner: Foundations of darkroom photography: black and white film processing, darkroom…

Combines technical exercises with conceptual themes in historical and contemporary photography. 35mm camera with manually adjustable apertures and shutter speeds required. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; one 200-level ART course or equivalent.

name: Visiting Artist Lecture Series
oneLiner: Prominent contemporary artists present their creative and scholarly work.

name: Conceptual Art After Conceptual Art
oneLiner: Interdisciplinary study rooted in conceptual practices, methods, and strategies.

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Interactive Arts
oneLiner: Skills, knowledge, concepts, and aesthetics in designing interactive artworks using…
description: Skills, knowledge, concepts, and aesthetics in designing interactive artworks using basic electronics, microcomputers, and microcontrollers in a fine arts context. Activity. Extra fee required. [Formerly ART 311]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; ART 210 or ART 310; or permission of the instructor.

name: Video Art
oneLiner: Introduction to digital video art and sound, including video art production, history…

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Art majors and minors; ART 210 or ART 310; or permission of the instructor.

prereqNotes: ART 222 or equivalent.

oneLiner: Exploration in relief surface treatments using a variety of approaches incorporating…

Possibilities of raw materials and substrates for adhesion, integration or construction. The conceptual contribution that material selection and working process make. Activity. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Art majors and minors; ART 222.

name: Surface Design Studio
oneLiner: Fundamental surface design techniques on fabric for producing two- and…
description: Fundamental surface design techniques on fabric for producing two- and three-dimensional forms with emphasis on the design process and concept development. Studio activities from portfolio samples to larger fine art pieces are explored. May be repeated for a total of 6 units on advisement. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: ART 222 or equivalent.

name: Intermediate Painting
oneLiner: Concepts, techniques, and disciplines of painting.
description: Concepts, techniques, and disciplines of painting. Creating works on paper, with a focus on acrylic, gouache, and watercolor. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 231* or ART 330* or equivalent.

name: Further Explorations in Drawing
oneLiner: Drawing concepts and media.
description: Drawing concepts and media. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 231* or equivalent.

name: Figure Drawing
oneLiner: Figure drawing concepts in varied media.
description: Figure drawing concepts in varied media. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 231* or equivalent.

oneLiner: Color vocabulary and theoretical concepts of color.
description: Color vocabulary and theoretical concepts of color. Fundamental to painting and other disciplines. Pigments, dyes, and inks. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 231* or ART 330* or equivalent.

oneLiner: Workshop in printmaking processes.

prereqNotes: ART 235 or ART 335 or equivalent.

oneLiner: Screen printing processes that utilizing hand-drawn and photo-emulsion stencils with a…

prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 235 or equivalent.

name: Sculpture and Expanded Practice
oneLiner: Further development of transferable skills, personal lexicon, and critical discourse in…

prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 240 or ART 340 or equivalent.

oneLiner: Clay and glaze.
description: Clay and glaze. Form exploration with wheel and hand-building techniques. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 12 units with permission of the instructor. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Art majors.

name: Studio X
oneLiner: Expands on intellectual, academic, and career preparation in the School of Art.
description: Expands on intellectual, academic, and career preparation in the School of Art. Provides an opportunity to experience and study with diverse art practitioners from the greater Bay Area region. Topics focus on issues such as social justice, equity, representation, opportunity, and decolonized creativity as they relate to a culturally shifting student body. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary for a total of 12 units. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Studio Art and Art: Concentration in Art History and Studio Art majors and Studio Art minors; one 300* or 400*-level art class; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Examination of the art and craft emerging from adversities and celebratory moments…
description: Examination of the art and craft emerging from adversities and celebratory moments, movements, and communities within LGBTQIA history. Studio practice is directed at reimagining queer pasts, investigating current queer art and culture, and speculating on future aesthetics of worlds untethered from binaries, heteronormativity, and colonialism. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Studio Art and Art History majors and minors; one 300* or 400*-level art class; or permission of the instructor.

name: Intermediate Photography
oneLiner: Black and white photochemical and digital processes that reflect evolving contemporary…
description: Black and white photochemical and digital processes that reflect evolving contemporary photographic practice. Topics may include, but are not limited, medium and large format camera operation, complex exposure techniques, studio lighting, analog and digital printing, image dissemination techniques, and the moving image. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Art majors and minors; ART 260 or ART 360 recommended.

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Art majors and minors; basic computer skills and familiarity with Photoshop and Illustrator; or permission of the instructor.

name: Advanced Painting
oneLiner: Contemporary approaches and concerns in painting practice.

oneLiner: Formal, conceptual, and structural aspects of painting using traditional and…

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing.

oneLiner: Investigation of specific printmaking processes, techniques, and different conceptual…

name: Hydrarchy: Nautical Art, Watercraft, and the Art of Resistance

prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; a 300- or 400-level ART course; or permission of the instructor.

prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; ART 245 or equivalent.

Activity. Extra fee required.

name: Art and Social Function
oneLiner: Interdisciplinary examination of the role of the artist as citizen through the…
description: Interdisciplinary examination of the role of the artist as citizen through the production of artworks focusing on Social Justice. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary. Activity. [Formerly ART 441]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors; a 300- or 400-level ART course.

oneLiner: Examination and exploration of the concepts and implementation of the tools and…

Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

Focus on cross-cultural exchange with East and South East Asia, Europe, and West Africa. Emphasis on the impact of socio-political contexts on the production of art and architecture. (This course is offered as ARTH 301 and LTNS 301. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors with sophomore standing or above or LTNS 222* or permission of the instructor.

Themes and topics include abstraction, artistic medium, pop art, minimalism, site-specificity, earth art, conceptual art, performance art, video art, queer and feminist practices, politics of identity, appropriation, social practice, activist art, globalization, art and climate change, and art and disability.

Among the art historical subjects to be covered are: Buddhist sculptures and painting, Hindu temples, and Islamic built environments.

prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors, M.F.A. Art students, and South Asian Studies minors; upper-division standing; ARTH 205 or equivalent recommended; or permission of the instructor.

prereqNotes: Category I or II placement for QR/Math, or completion of GE Area 2/B4, or MATH 197.

prereqNotes: PHYS 121 or PHYS 230 or PHYS 240 with a grade of C or better.

name: Observational Astronomy Laboratory
oneLiner: Introduction to observational astronomy, including the celestial sphere & coordinate…
description: Introduction to observational astronomy, including the celestial sphere & coordinate systems on the sky; apparent motions of the Sun, stars, and planets, astronomical magnitudes, astronomical systems of time, using binoculars & telescopes, geometric optics & telescope design, telescope mounts, limitations of telescope observations, astronomical detectors, photometry, spectroscopy. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: ASTR 115 or ASTR 300; and PHYS 121 or PHYS 230 or PHYS 240; all with grades of C or better.

Emphasis will be on how we know what we know about the universe, including observational and experimental evidence. (ABC/NC grading only)
