prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Writing About the Media - GWAR
oneLiner: Evaluate claims about the nature, uses, and impact of the media.
description: Evaluate claims about the nature, uses, and impact of the media. Compare how writing for the media and writing about the media are similar and different. Investigation of sources, methods, cataloging, philosophies of media research, and how claims about improving the electronic media are made. Acquiring and evaluating information and organizing the results into written form. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Priority enrollment for BECA majors; GE Area 1A/A2*.

name: Media Literacy
oneLiner: Explore electronic media content, effects, and influence on individuals and groups.
description: Explore electronic media content, effects, and influence on individuals and groups. Develop analytical and critical skills necessary to become a discerning user of media. Apply theoretical and media literacy frameworks to everyday life. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: KSFS Radio and Podcasting I
oneLiner: Production and performance for radio and podcasting including.
description: Production and performance for radio and podcasting including. Development of skills used in the daily operation of a radio station including programming, scheduling, and planning. Activity.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Sonic Storytelling: Telling Stories in Sound
oneLiner: Analysis and production of storytelling with sound.
description: Analysis and production of storytelling with sound. Traditional and experimental approaches designed to explore the potential of radio, podcasting, and the art of sound. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Arts majors; BECA 231*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Creative Podcasting
oneLiner: Practice and analysis of podcasting.
description: Practice and analysis of podcasting. Traditional and experimental approaches to production value and podcasting techniques. Explore the potential of podcast production across multiple interest areas. Activity.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Study of Popular Culture
oneLiner: Study and application of theoretical frameworks to electronic and digital media as…
description: Study and application of theoretical frameworks to electronic and digital media as popular culture, including (but not limited to) t.v., film, music, blogs, social media platforms, video games, news and tabloid, etc. and how it shapes and reflects social and cultural norms, values, and power structures.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Law
oneLiner: Legal and regulatory aspects of electronic media with a focus on the impact of F.C.C.…
description: Legal and regulatory aspects of electronic media with a focus on the impact of F.C.C. licensing and regulation within the framework of the First Amendment.
prereqNotes: Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors with BECA 200; or Music Recording Industry Certificate students with BECA 200 or MUS 137; or permission of the instructor.

name: Broadcast Industry Symposium
oneLiner: Student participation with American and foreign broadcasters, international concerns…
description: Student participation with American and foreign broadcasters, international concerns, new communication technologies, program exchange, and production and script workshops. May be repeated for a total of 4 units. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: The Sound Studio I: Consoles & Signal Flow
oneLiner: Radio and television production including in-studio recording on multi-channel…
description: Radio and television production including in-studio recording on multi-channel recording consoles. Use of board equalization, reverberation systems, graphic equalizers, limiters, and the art of overdubbing. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts and Music majors, Music Recording Industry certificate students must contact the BECA department for a permission number to enroll; BECA 231; or permission of the instructor.

name: Audio for Video
oneLiner: Production theory and practice as applied to audio recording for video.
description: Production theory and practice as applied to audio recording for video. Pre-production planning and location and studio recording situations. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 231*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Aesthetics I
oneLiner: Aesthetic analysis of video, film, video games, and related electronic media based on…
description: Aesthetic analysis of video, film, video games, and related electronic media based on an examination of the fundamental image and sound elements. A grade of C or better required for BECA majors.
prereqNotes: Sophomore standing or above; priority enrollment for BECA majors; or permission of the instructor.

name: Aerial (Drone) Imagery Operation and Aesthetics
oneLiner: The use of drones for aerial videography, imagery, and aesthetics.
description: The use of drones for aerial videography, imagery, and aesthetics. Introduction to the operation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), more commonly known as drones, gathering aerial footage for various purposes, and applying the principle of art aesthetics to aerial videography and imagery. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Activity.
prereqNotes: BECA 246* and BECA 340* or permission of the instructor.

name: Video Editing I
oneLiner: Introduction to major aesthetic and technical considerations in video editing and…
description: Introduction to major aesthetic and technical considerations in video editing and practical applications in electronic media production. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 241; or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Performance I
oneLiner: Performance training for electronic media.
description: Performance training for electronic media. Exercises for improving articulation, pronunciation, interpretation, vocal quality, and communicative abilities. The international phonetic alphabet. Activity.
prereqNotes: Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 241; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Art of Voiceover
oneLiner: Performance, production, and analysis of voiceovers, including various techniques and…
description: Performance, production, and analysis of voiceovers, including various techniques and professional best practices; designed for further exploration into the vibrant world of voice acting & directing. Activity. (Plus-minus ABC/NC, CR/NC allowed)
prereqNotes: BECA 231 or permission of the instructor.

name: Esports Studio Tournament and Event Production
oneLiner: Introduction to live event producing for esports and esports tournaments.
description: Introduction to live event producing for esports and esports tournaments. Activities will include weekly Twitch live streams of esports tournaments, including recruiting players and coordinating brackets, as well as creating edited highlight videos of each tournament. Emphasis on cultivating dynamic and engaging audio and video presence, and learning how to produce, direct, and monetize a live studio event. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts majors or Video Game Studies minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Writing for Electronic Media
oneLiner: Fundamentals of writing for audio, visual, and online media.
description: Fundamentals of writing for audio, visual, and online media. Practice scriptwriting across formats, including video, radio, PSAs, commercials, and documentaries. Emphasis on structure, clarity, pacing, and writing for picture and sound. Contemporary tools - including transcription, research aids, and AI-assisted story development - are used to support brainstorming, drafting, and revision. Focus on writing craft rather than on reporting, production, or strategic communication.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Scriptwriting for A/V Media Production
oneLiner: Learning to convey story and information in audio/video script format: only what the…
description: Learning to convey story and information in audio/video script format: only what the audience will be able to hear and see. Presenting scripts in correct format and free of writing mechanics errors. Projects will include PSA and promotional spots, trailers, and short-format video scripts. (Grade of C or better required for BECA majors)
prereqNotes: Restricted to BECA majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Scriptwriting for Audio Media Production
oneLiner: Learn to convey story and information in audio-only script format.
description: Learn to convey story and information in audio-only script format. Practice correct script format and proofreading/writing mechanics. Projects will include PSA and promotional spots, scripted personal audio narratives, and scripted audio drama/comedy/mystery/fiction and nonfiction. (Grade of C or better required for BECA majors)
prereqNotes: Restricted to BECA majors; BECA 300GW with a grade of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Writing for Video Games
oneLiner: Writing for video games, including writing scripts for interactive and multi-branch…
description: Writing for video games, including writing scripts for interactive and multi-branch narratives, gameplay, cutscenes, in-game tutorials, and other game content. Emphasis on social and cultural aspects of video game content and player experience, ethics and responsibilities of game creators, and the potential for video games to promote equity, diversity, inclusion, and social justice. [Formerly BECA 577]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts majors and Video Games Studies minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Non-Fiction Scriptwriting
oneLiner: Writing scripts for radio, television, podcasts, and online stories.
description: Writing scripts for radio, television, podcasts, and online stories. Emphasis on short-format news and clear, conversational writing for the ear, documentary spec scripts, social media live reporting, and podcast episodes. Introduction to AI-assisted research, drafting, and revision with attention to verification, ethics, and transparency in nonfiction storytelling. Pitches crafted for investigative episodes and docu-series. [Formerly BECA 560]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing and permission of the instructor.

name: Close Up on Electronic Media
oneLiner: A close up look at electronic media practices, including specialized production…
description: A close up look at electronic media practices, including specialized production techniques and performance, business environments, social impact, and marketing electronic media content. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 4 units when topics vary. Only 3 units may count towards the BECA major. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Advanced Television Production Workshop
oneLiner: Development and production of Television Center programming for cable or broadcast.
description: Development and production of Television Center programming for cable or broadcast. May be repeated for a total of 6 units with permission of the instructor. Activity. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: BECA 241* and BECA 340*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Media and Society
oneLiner: Examine how media influences individuals and society through media effects theories and…
description: Examine how media influences individuals and society through media effects theories and research. Topics include the psychological and social impact of television, film, social media, and video games. Explore the role of media in shaping attitudes, behaviors, and cultural norms, as well as issues of media freedom, regulation, and technological change.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Economics: Entertainment, Platform, and Technology
oneLiner: Study the structure of media industries and the behavior of media organizations and…
description: Study the structure of media industries and the behavior of media organizations and consumers through the lens of economics. Analyze recent trends in media industries and the forces driving the changes. Discuss competitive and complementary relationships between traditional and new media.
prereqNotes: Priority enrollment for Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 200; or Music Recording Industry Certificate students with BECA 200 or MUS 137; or permission of the instructor.

name: Television and Video Program Design
oneLiner: The process of designing streaming television series.
description: The process of designing streaming television series. Pre-production stages of series development. (BECA 725/BECA 425 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; a GPA of at least 3.0; or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Entrepreneurship
oneLiner: Introduction to the application of entrepreneurship principles to various media…
description: Introduction to the application of entrepreneurship principles to various media industries, with an emphasis on the creation of a media start-up. The principles examined include innovation, rigorous evaluation of the industry, market analysis, and feasible business plans. Exploration of both the creation of new media companies as well as how to work as an independent media professional. A grade of C or better required for Journalism majors and minors. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (This course is offered as JOUR 427 [formerly JOUR 675] and BECA 427. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Management
oneLiner: Concepts, methods, and current practices in electronic media organization and management.
description: Concepts, methods, and current practices in electronic media organization and management. Decision making, implementation approaches, and communication applications for the small electronic media operation. Resource allocation, facility design and operation, project management, operation scheduling, and quality control. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division and graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors.

name: The Sound Studio II: Recording & Mixing
oneLiner: Audio techniques in the specialized fields of audio recording and sound reinforcement…
description: Audio techniques in the specialized fields of audio recording and sound reinforcement for television, film, and music recording. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts and Music majors, Music Recording Industry certificate students must contact the BECA department for a permission number to enroll; BECA 330*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Sound for Games
oneLiner: Training in state of the art techniques used in designing sound for various types of…
description: Training in state of the art techniques used in designing sound for various types of video games and immersive environments. Analysis of theoretical topics in the history and development of modern video game and virtual reality audio design. (This course is offered as MUS 434 and BECA 434. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division and graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts and Music majors; or Video Game Studies minors who have completed CWL 180; demonstrated familiarity with any digital audio workstation.

name: Aesthetics of Sound
oneLiner: Aesthetics of sound and the basic principles involved in the theoretical and critical…
description: Aesthetics of sound and the basic principles involved in the theoretical and critical analysis of audio in media, including radio, television, film, music, and other audio-visual communication. (BECA 735/BECA 435 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors with a GPA of 3.0 or better; BECA 231* and BECA 340*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Aesthetics II
oneLiner: Problems in applied aesthetics.
description: Problems in applied aesthetics. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 340*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Acting for Camera
oneLiner: Rehearsing and performing for multi-camera and single-camera fiction media content in…
description: Rehearsing and performing for multi-camera and single-camera fiction media content in conjunction with video production. Emphasis on scene work, acting technique, working on a TV/film set, and working with directors. Activity.
prereqNotes: BECA 350 and permission of the instructor.

name: International Media Politics
oneLiner: Examination of how communication among states and non-state entities shapes…
description: Examination of how communication among states and non-state entities shapes international relations, from the perspective of various theoretical and epistemological approaches. (This course is offered as I R 452, JOUR 452, and BECA 451. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing.

name: Women and Media in International Relations
oneLiner: Explore how media, broadly defined, perceive and project women's role in international…
description: Explore how media, broadly defined, perceive and project women's role in international relations. Focus on some of "those non-state entities whose power to influence nation-state decisions is growing rapidly," as mentioned in the IR program description. Analyze the portrayal of women's role in international relations, stretching back to Aristophanes' comedy of Greek women ending the Peloponnesian War to current news and popular television series such as "Madame Secretary." (This course is offered as I R 453 and BECA 453. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Live Streaming and Content Creation for Esports
oneLiner: Introduction to talent marketing for the esports industry.
description: Introduction to talent marketing for the esports industry. Activities include tournament live streams on Twitch as well as production assignments aimed at creating and cultivating engaging content for both live and virtual audiences, such as highlight videos to post on social media. Focus on the effective management and operation of a Twitch channel and the monetization of content. Activity. [Formerly BECA 452]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Industry of Broadcast News
oneLiner: Values, theories, sources, and content of radio and television newscasts.
description: Values, theories, sources, and content of radio and television newscasts. Professional roles, management, and operations of broadcast and cable news at the international, national, and local levels.
prereqNotes: BECA 200 or permission of the instructor.

name: Video Documentary: Story Development and Innovation
oneLiner: Analysis of American and international documentary programming on TV, streaming…
description: Analysis of American and international documentary programming on TV, streaming platforms, and social media. Survey of the history, research, development, aesthetics, ethics, and social impacts associated with documentary production. Research, pitch, and propose original documentary topics.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; BECA 300GW*.

name: Ethics and Responsibility in the Electronic Media
oneLiner: The concept of professionalism and roles of individuals, law, and government in…
description: The concept of professionalism and roles of individuals, law, and government in determining ethical standards in electronic media. [Formerly BECA 623]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Media on Media: Media Scandals and Journalism Ethics in Israel, the U.S., and U.K.
oneLiner: Legal, ethical, and normative questions in the work of journalists and media…
description: Legal, ethical, and normative questions in the work of journalists and media organizations are examined in case studies from Israel, the U.S., and the U.K. by analyzing the media's relationships with the political arena, the private sector, and security forces. Topics include libel suits, source protection, and advertising boycotts; appropriate means for monitoring and regulating the media; and the significance of media self-reflection and transparency in the digital age. (This course is offered as JS 469, BECA 469, and JOUR 469. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2.

name: Dramatic Writing for Television and Electronic Media
oneLiner: Television as a unique medium for drama.
description: Television as a unique medium for drama. The limitations and potentialities of the medium in relation to form, style, timing, characterization, and story selection.
prereqNotes: BECA 370; permission of the instructor.

name: Writing for Interactive and Social Media
oneLiner: Creating interactive and social media content for digital platforms, including the…
description: Creating interactive and social media content for digital platforms, including the mindful use of contemporary workflow tools such as AI-assisted ideation, drafting, and testing. Write and adapt content for informative and persuasive purposes while evaluating accessibility, inclusivity, and ethical communication practices. Emphasis on audience-centered storytelling, platform conventions, pro-social messaging, and responsible use of evolving interactive media technologies.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; upper-division standing; or permission of the instructor.

name: Audio Journalism
oneLiner: Planning, reporting, production and publication of audio journalism.
description: Planning, reporting, production and publication of audio journalism. Conveying accurate and compelling reports using audio-based story forms. Examination of digital literacy and media analysis, story development and pitches, interview technique, field producing, scripting and transcribing, plus audio editing, production and publishing. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (This course is offered as JOUR 480 and BECA 480. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; JOUR 226* and JOUR 300GW*, or BECA 231* and BECA 300GW* or equivalents.

name: Women and Media
oneLiner: Analytic modes, including feminist, psychoanalytic, and economic criticism, to assess…
description: Analytic modes, including feminist, psychoanalytic, and economic criticism, to assess both how women are represented in mass media and the status of women employed in mass media. (This course is offered as BECA 485 and WGS 485. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Children and Television
oneLiner: How children use and are affected by mass media, particularly television.
description: How children use and are affected by mass media, particularly television. Theory and research describing children and television. Role of television in children's development. (This course is offered as BECA 487 and ITEC 487. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Asian Media
oneLiner: Critical, theoretical, and cultural analysis of China, India, and Japan.
description: Critical, theoretical, and cultural analysis of China, India, and Japan. Aesthetics of aural and visual representations in Asian television and cinema productions.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Television and Social Change
oneLiner: Nature of social change including television's potential, or lack of potential, to…
description: Nature of social change including television's potential, or lack of potential, to bring about social change, the role of television in achieving that change, and critique of relevant programming intended to effect change. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: International Broadcasting
oneLiner: Broadcast systems of the world including developed and developing nations.
description: Broadcast systems of the world including developed and developing nations. Programming of many cultures, the role of satellites in promoting the exchange of programs, the relationship between governments, societies, and the media, and issues in international communication. (This course is offered as BECA 500 and I R 500. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Audio Visual Translation and Localization of Global Content
oneLiner: Basic concepts and the history of audiovisual translation (AVT).
description: Basic concepts and the history of audiovisual translation (AVT). Assignments on the production of audiovisual texts and translations. Group projects involving the production of a wide range of audiovisual translation modes, including subtitling, dubbing, voiceover, audio description, and the production of remakes.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Environmental Communication on Electronic Media
oneLiner: Representation of environmental issues in electronic media including radio, television…
description: Representation of environmental issues in electronic media including radio, television, and the Internet. Strategies for using electronic media to communicate environmental topics.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: KSFS Radio and Podcasting II
oneLiner: Students become managers and staff responsible for the daily operation of KSFS Radio…
description: Students become managers and staff responsible for the daily operation of KSFS Radio and associated podcasts. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: BECA 305* or permission of the instructor.

name: Music Performance Recording and Production
oneLiner: Student teams are responsible for the production of a weekly, on-air, stereo radio…
description: Student teams are responsible for the production of a weekly, on-air, stereo radio program featuring major campus concert performances. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 231*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Television Center Crew
oneLiner: Hands-on experience including camera operator, lighting, technical director, audio…
description: Hands-on experience including camera operator, lighting, technical director, audio technician, videotape recorder, and floor director. Complex productions with multiple cameras, sets, and lighting set-ups.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 241*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Television News Crew
oneLiner: Hands-on experience as the production crew for Television Center newscasts.
description: Hands-on experience as the production crew for Television Center newscasts. Practical experience as a director, technical director, floor director, camera operator, audio engineer, and other production positions. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors and BECA 241*.

name: The Business of Media Productions
oneLiner: Factors in day-to-day electronic media operations, program scheduling, syndication…
description: Factors in day-to-day electronic media operations, program scheduling, syndication, social media use, labor relations, political and legal considerations, station promotion, and advanced distribution systems. Applied practice in the distribution and operation of Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts media channels. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 200; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Sound Studio III: Music Production & Sound Design
oneLiner: Gain major audio productions skills through active participation in challenging audio…
description: Gain major audio productions skills through active participation in challenging audio media productions. Audio for television, film, record production, and sound reinforcement. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts and Music majors, Music Recording Industry certificate students must contact the BECA department for a permission number to enroll; BECA 231*, BECA 330*, and BECA 430*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Sound Design for Games
oneLiner: Topics include arts and techniques that are used in designing sound for various types…
description: Topics include arts and techniques that are used in designing sound for various types of video games. Activity. (This course is offered as BECA 534 and MUS 534. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts and Music majors; BECA 434; BECA 231 and BECA 335 recommended; or permission of the instructor.

name: Advanced Audio for Video
oneLiner: Sound theory and practice as applied to post-production audio for video.
description: Sound theory and practice as applied to post-production audio for video. Timecode synchronization of sound effects, music, and dialogue. Field recording and mixing for picture. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 335; or permission of the instructor.

name: Creativity and Design Thinking in Electronic Media
oneLiner: Exploration of the creative process for media students.
description: Exploration of the creative process for media students. Use of multimedia, computers, and video games as tools to enhance creativity and to develop problem-solving skills. Design thinking is concerned with solving problems through design. Through a process of divergent thinking, a designer will examine many possible solutions at the beginning of a process where the problem is defined before solving it.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Television Directing I
oneLiner: Creating and directing a variety of television productions.
description: Creating and directing a variety of television productions. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BECA 241* or permission of the instructor.

name: Video Editing II
oneLiner: The developmental study of the video editing process with a focus on editing stages…
description: The developmental study of the video editing process with a focus on editing stages, editing decision making, and editing styles for different program genres. Media asset management and the role of the editor in the production process. Project-based course. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 348; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Broadcast Interview
oneLiner: Interview as an essential tool for broadcast information gathering and presentation.
description: Interview as an essential tool for broadcast information gathering and presentation. Interview styles, question research, production approaches for television and radio, and special interview formats such as talk shows and political debates. Activity.
prereqNotes: BECA 241* or BECA 246*; BECA 350* or BECA 561*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Sports Reporting for Television
oneLiner: Specialized skills and practices of television sports journalism including writing to…
description: Specialized skills and practices of television sports journalism including writing to visuals, sports field reporting, and interviewing athletes. Emphasis on the student's ability to research and select relevant topics and issues. Activity.
prereqNotes: BECA 246 and BECA 560 or permission of the instructor.

name: News Reporting for Television
oneLiner: Techniques of broadcast and cable reporting including writing for visual production…
description: Techniques of broadcast and cable reporting including writing for visual production, production of field reports, use of research retention techniques, and experimental use of visuals in newscasts. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts or Bilingual Spanish Journalism majors; BECA 246* and BECA 375* or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Video Documentary: Production
oneLiner: Develop the skills to research, pitch, produce, shoot, write, and edit a documentary on…
description: Develop the skills to research, pitch, produce, shoot, write, and edit a documentary on an original topic for broadcast and streaming platforms. Explore interviewing techniques, narrative and aesthetic choices, legal and ethical concerns, funding, distribution, and marketing. Culminates in live documentary festival for campus and community. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 246 and BECA 462; or permission of the instructor.

name: Variable Topics in Advanced Media Writing
oneLiner: Advanced practice in writing for specialized media genres and formats.
description: Advanced practice in writing for specialized media genres and formats. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing.

name: Internship in Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts
oneLiner: Internship experience in professional broadcast and electronic media organization.
description: Internship experience in professional broadcast and electronic media organization. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division and graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts students or permission of the instructor; 3.0 minimum GPA required.

name: Media in Community Service
oneLiner: Use of media for public agencies and institutions and by non-profit groups.
description: Use of media for public agencies and institutions and by non-profit groups. Includes creating and placing public service announcements, developing media programs for agencies, institutions, and community groups, budgeting, and grant-seeking. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units with permission of the instructor. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: BECA 246 (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the instructor.

name: AI and Media
oneLiner: Artificial intelligence is transforming the creation and consumption of media.
description: Artificial intelligence is transforming the creation and consumption of media. Explore the application of AI tools in media production, addressing ethical considerations such as bias, privacy, and intellectual property. Examine the broader impact of AI on media professions and its influence on the relationship between creators and audiences.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division and graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts students.

name: Mobile Electronic Media
oneLiner: Aspects of mobile media including business and legal environments, social and personal…
description: Aspects of mobile media including business and legal environments, social and personal impact, writing for mobile and news on mobile, producing, and marketing mobile content.
prereqNotes: Upper-division and graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts students or permission of the instructor.

name: Senior Seminar
oneLiner: Relationships between various academic disciplines and the broadcast media.
description: Relationships between various academic disciplines and the broadcast media.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Television and Video Production Planning
oneLiner: Organization and production planning of live television programs.
description: Organization and production planning of live television programs. Budgets, legal clearances, scripting, casting, distribution, marketing, and logistical problems. Duties of the above-the-line team. Emphasis on live coverage and distribution of television entertainment events. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 231 or BECA 241; or permission of the instructor.

name: Electronic Field Production II
oneLiner: Electronic field production and editing.
description: Electronic field production and editing. Production and analysis of field-based television program material. The relationship between production variables and aesthetic practices. name: Advanced Video Production
oneLiner: Professional-level production of announcements and messages created for a client and…

oneLiner: Theoretical and practical aspects of the principles of digitizing and editing…
description: Theoretical and practical aspects of the principles of digitizing and editing videotape. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 348; or permission of the instructor.

name: Live Sports Production
oneLiner: Production of live sports event coverage for simulcast via the Internet, cable…
description: Production of live sports event coverage for simulcast via the Internet, cable television, and broadcast outlets. Experience in large-scale report audio and video production activities. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors; BECA 241; or permission of the instructor.

name: Television Center News
oneLiner: Produce and/or anchor a live weekly newscast covering campus, community, and the Bay Area.
description: Produce and/or anchor a live weekly newscast covering campus, community, and the Bay Area. Includes extensive fieldwork and beat-reporting for news/sports packages, real-time reporting via social media and streaming platforms, and building a professional performance reel for producing/reporting/multimedia news jobs. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 8 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to BECA and Bilingual Spanish Journalism majors; BECA 375* and either BECA 561* or JOUR 400*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Writing for Interactive Electronic Media
oneLiner: Script writer's role in the creation of interactive electronic media.
description: Script writer's role in the creation of interactive electronic media. Differences between conventional screen narrative and interactive storytelling and information presentation.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division or graduate standing.

name: Projects in the Teaching of Broadcast and Communication Arts
oneLiner: Developing courses and lectures, leading discussions, and teaching and evaluating…
description: Developing courses and lectures, leading discussions, and teaching and evaluating students in the Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts. Teaching experiences as an instructional aide in an assigned Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts course. (Students may earn a maximum of 4 units toward the baccalaureate degree for any course(s) numbered 685 regardless of discipline.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Practicum in Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; permission of the supervising instructor and department chair; GPA of 3.0 or better.

name: Introduction to Graduate Study
oneLiner: Introduction to graduate study in broadcast and electronic communication arts.
description: Introduction to graduate study in broadcast and electronic communication arts. History of mass communication and electronic media theory. Academic writing, graduate-level research, and survey of Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts faculty's teaching, research, and production activity. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts students.

name: Formula and Creativity in the Public Arts
oneLiner: Exploration of the relationship between formula and creativity.
description: Exploration of the relationship between formula and creativity. Discussion of the theory and practice of formulas and genres, particularly in relation to the public arts, as well as systems of criticism. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Ethics and Responsibility in Electronic Media
oneLiner: Examination of broadcast industry self-regulatory codes of ethics and responsibility…
description: Examination of broadcast industry self-regulatory codes of ethics and responsibility including concepts of freedom and responsibility as they relate to broadcasters, the government, and the public. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700 (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Media Aesthetics and Production Theory
oneLiner: Investigation of perceptual conditions and aesthetic theories that guide the…
description: Investigation of perceptual conditions and aesthetic theories that guide the interpretation, analysis, and creation of visual and sound images in the electronic media and how these theories may be creatively applied in the production process. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the instructor.

name: Television and Video Program Design
oneLiner: The process of designing streaming television series.
description: The process of designing streaming television series. Pre-production stages of series development. (BECA 725/BECA 425 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: BECA 700 or permission of the instructor.

name: Aesthetics of Sound
oneLiner: Aesthetics of sound and the basic principles involved in the theoretical and critical…
description: Aesthetics of sound and the basic principles involved in the theoretical and critical analysis of audio in media, including radio, television, film, music, and other audio-visual communication. (BECA 735/BECA 435 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts students or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Electronic field production and editing.

Activity. Extra fee required. (BECA 746/BECA 646 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Developing and Funding Productions for Electronic Media
oneLiner: Development of a media project from idea to funding package including brainstorming…
description: Development of a media project from idea to funding package including brainstorming, research, outline, treatment, and package. Preparation of applications for external and internal funding from local, regional, state, federal, private, and public sources. (AB/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts Pedagogy
oneLiner: The process of curricular and instructional preparation for students who wish to teach…
description: The process of curricular and instructional preparation for students who wish to teach broadcast and electronic communication arts. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Media Writing and Performance
oneLiner: Writing and performance for electronic media, writing scripts for features, persuasive…
description: Writing and performance for electronic media, writing scripts for features, persuasive messages, informational programs, and drama, script analysis, and development of performance skills for the camera and microphone. Activity. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in New Electronic Communication Technologies
oneLiner: Evolving communication technologies including cable television, digital broadcasting…
description: Evolving communication technologies including cable television, digital broadcasting, satellite transmission, video telephony, and the Internet. Hardware, software, and social integration issues.
prereqNotes: BECA 700 or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Electronic Media Production
oneLiner: Laboratory course where rough drafts of projects are shared for critiques.
description: Laboratory course where rough drafts of projects are shared for critiques. Includes discussions of production, scripting and design, and logistical challenges. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule.
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Media and Society
oneLiner: Social implications of broadcasting and electronic media.
description: Social implications of broadcasting and electronic media. Theoretical and methodological issues surrounding electronic media processes and effects. The effects of electronic media on cultural and social institutions. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Directed Experience in Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts Education
oneLiner: Directed experience in teaching broadcast and electronic communication arts.
description: Directed experience in teaching broadcast and electronic communication arts. Students assist in course preparation and instruction and receive supervision from the instructor of record. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts students; BECA 700; or permission of the graduate program advisor and sponsoring faculty member.

name: Seminar in Television Dramatic Writing
oneLiner: Writing the teleplay: premise, character, conflict, dialogue, and structure and how…
description: Writing the teleplay: premise, character, conflict, dialogue, and structure and how these elements are influenced by television as a unique dramatic medium. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BECA 700* or permission of the instructor.

name: Graduate Internship
oneLiner: Internship experience in broadcast and electronic media organization, or working with…
description: Internship experience in broadcast and electronic media organization, or working with approved mentor, or participating in approved community service. (CR/NC grading only).
prereqNotes: Restricted to Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts graduate students; GPA of 3.0 or better; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Readings and discussion concerning principles, issues, and theories in mass…
description: Readings and discussion concerning principles, issues, and theories in mass communication research, criticism, aesthetics, and production. Culminates in the written comprehensive examination. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate BECA students; completion of all other program requirements; permission of the graduate major adviser.

oneLiner: Required for students to satisfy their culminating experience requirement with the…

prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor and committee chair; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies before enrollment.

oneLiner: Preparation of a proposal for a M.F.A. creative project or a M.A. thesis under the…
description: Preparation of a proposal for a M.F.A. creative project or a M.A. thesis under the supervision of the instructor and faculty committee. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (CR/NC grading only).
prereqNotes: Restricted to BECA M.A. and M.F.A. students; permission of the graduate coordinator.

oneLiner: (CR/NC, RP)
