oneLiner: Problems in broadcast and electronic communication arts for graduate students who have…
description: Problems in broadcast and electronic communication arts for graduate students who have demonstrated the ability to work independently. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Permission of the graduate major adviser, supervising instructor, and department chair.

name: Human Biology
oneLiner: Principles of human biology including body structure and function, reproduction…
description: Principles of human biology including body structure and function, reproduction, development, heredity, and evolution. Aspects of modern biology impacting the human species. Intended for non-Biology majors.

name: Human Biology Laboratory
oneLiner: Laboratory exercises demonstrating scientific processes, including the scientific…
description: Laboratory exercises demonstrating scientific processes, including the scientific method, analysis of data, and drawing appropriate conclusions. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 100* (may be taken concurrently).

name: The World of Plants
oneLiner: World of plants, their place in nature, and their relationship to humans.
description: World of plants, their place in nature, and their relationship to humans. Growing plants, field observations, and studies of the economic uses of plants. Intended for non-Biology majors. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.

name: Marine Biology
oneLiner: Introduction to the marine environment including oceanic, intertidal, and nearshore…
description: Introduction to the marine environment including oceanic, intertidal, and nearshore communities of plants, animals, and microbes. Emphasis on marine biological and chemical processes and environmental issues both locally and globally.

name: Climate Change and the Oceans
oneLiner: The world's oceans have absorbed roughly 90% of the Earth's excess heat from global…
description: The world's oceans have absorbed roughly 90% of the Earth's excess heat from global warming and annually absorb one-third of fossil fuel produced CO2, which has a huge impact on the world's oceans that are so important as a global food resource. Examine the politics of climate change, and the ocean's effects on weather, commerce, and humanity.

name: Animal Diversity
oneLiner: Describes the diversity of animal life and provides an overview of basic concepts of…
description: Describes the diversity of animal life and provides an overview of basic concepts of evolution, the fossil record, physiology, behavior, ecology, geographical distribution, and issues in the conservation of biodiversity. Intended for non-Biology majors.

name: General Microbiology and Public Health
oneLiner: Basic concepts of microbiology including practical applications to medicine, public…
description: Basic concepts of microbiology including practical applications to medicine, public health, and the environment. Intended for non-Biology majors.

name: General Microbiology and Public Health Laboratory
oneLiner: Laboratory techniques in isolation, enumeration, and identification of microorganisms.
description: Laboratory techniques in isolation, enumeration, and identification of microorganisms. Laboratory. Extra fee required. Intended for non-Biology majors.
prereqNotes: BIOL 210* (may be taken concurrently).

name: Principles of Human Physiology
oneLiner: Physiology of human organ systems and principles of homeostasis.
description: Physiology of human organ systems and principles of homeostasis. Intended for non-Biology majors.
prereqNotes: CHEM 101* or CHEM 115*; BIOL 100* and BIOL 101*, or BIOL 210*, all with grades of C or better.

name: Principles of Human Physiology Laboratory
oneLiner: Laboratory exercises in mammalian physiology.
description: Laboratory exercises in mammalian physiology. To accompany or follow BIOL 212. Extra lab fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 212* (may be taken concurrently).

name: Principles of Human Anatomy
oneLiner: Study of the gross anatomy of the human body including body systems involving gross…
description: Study of the gross anatomy of the human body including body systems involving gross structure and history. Computerized virtual anatomy lab experience supplemented with enhanced skeletal and specimen study and cadaver visits. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 100* and BIOL 101*, or BIOL 212* and BIOL 213*.

name: Introductory Biology I
oneLiner: Fundamentals of biology including chemical basis of life, cell structure…
description: Fundamentals of biology including chemical basis of life, cell structure, bioenergetics, plant and animal physiology, and genetics. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Biology and Biochemistry majors and minors, Kinesiology majors, and Environmental Studies: Natural Resources Management and Conservation majors.

name: Advising for Success as a Biology Major
oneLiner: Introduction to the resources and opportunities available to Biology majors at SF State.
description: Introduction to the resources and opportunities available to Biology majors at SF State. Includes meeting with advisors, peer mentors, and instructors to explore what resources are available to achieve learning goals and develop a cohesive plan for completing Biology degrees. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Biology majors.

name: Introductory Biology II
oneLiner: Fundamentals of biology including gene expression, development, evolution, ecology, and…
description: Fundamentals of biology including gene expression, development, evolution, ecology, and the diversity of microbes, plants, and animals. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit; seminar, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230* with a grade of C- or better.

name: Nature Study
oneLiner: Explore the identification, structure, adaptation, life history, habits, habitat…
description: Explore the identification, structure, adaptation, life history, habits, habitat, economic status, and conservation of common plants and animals. Includes two all-day field trips scheduled on two separate weekends. Intended for non-Biology majors. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; a college-level biology course*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Global Politics of Science, Technology, and Health
oneLiner: Examine the cultural, ethical, economic, and political dimensions of science…
description: Examine the cultural, ethical, economic, and political dimensions of science, technology, and health in a global context. Explore how science, technology, and public health both shape politics and are shaped by politics. Consider the role of science in government and society; the dilemmas of international organizations and scientific knowledge; technology and big tech companies in international relations, science and technology policy, and government regulation; global health regimes and institutions; and the implications of social media, artificial intelligence, and cyber-currencies. (This course is offered as I R 305 and BIOL 305. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; I R 104 or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Biology for Today's World
oneLiner: Fundamental concepts and processes in genetics, cell biology, evolution, ecology, and…
description: Fundamental concepts and processes in genetics, cell biology, evolution, ecology, and biodiversity. Scientific inquiry. Application of concepts to current issues in science and society. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; one college-level biology course*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Principles of Ecology
oneLiner: Ecological principles and methods.
description: Ecological principles and methods. Introduction to population, community, and ecosystem ecology. Includes trips to various habitats. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: One college-level biology or environmentally-oriented course. Intended for non-Biology majors.

name: Field Methods in Ecology and Evolution
oneLiner: An introduction to sampling and experimental design for environmental biologists.
description: An introduction to sampling and experimental design for environmental biologists. An overview of methods for sampling a variety of organisms in specific habitats. Principles of design, execution, and interpretation of data derived from field experiments will be explored. Data analysis and visualization will be emphasized. (BIOL 315/BIOL 715 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; BIOL 240* and BIOL 458* with grades of C or better; GPA of 3.0 or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Ecology of California
oneLiner: Examines the ecology and natural history of California, and the impact humans have on…
description: Examines the ecology and natural history of California, and the impact humans have on the environment in perceptual and scientific content. Focus on the principal processes underlying the evolution/diversity of California's terrestrial/aquatic flora/fauna.
prereqNotes: A college-level biology course.

name: Our Endangered Planet
oneLiner: The effect of humans on the ecology of our environment.
description: The effect of humans on the ecology of our environment. Species extinctions, the role of genetics, nature reserves, the biology of small populations, and restoration ecology. Intended for non-Biology majors.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; one college-level biology course*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Disease!
oneLiner: Origin and natural history of selected infectious and non-infectious human diseases…
description: Origin and natural history of selected infectious and non-infectious human diseases, including causal agents, mechanisms, and historical impact. Factors involved in the incidence and distribution of disease. Intended for non-Biology majors.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; BIOL 100 or equivalent*; or permission of the instructor.

name: HIV, AIDS, and the Science to End the Epidemic
oneLiner: Track one of the few modern epidemics to understand how it came about and analyze what…
description: Track one of the few modern epidemics to understand how it came about and analyze what was effective in combating the epidemic, what was less effective, and the lessons that can be learned from this disease and others.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; one college-level Biology course*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Human Anatomy
oneLiner: Gross structures of the human body.
description: Gross structures of the human body. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Biology, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Clinical Science, and Kinesiology majors with sophomore standing or above; BIOL 230* with a grade of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Human Sexuality
oneLiner: Development, structure, function, and dysfunction of reproductive and sexual systems in…
description: Development, structure, function, and dysfunction of reproductive and sexual systems in humans, physiology of sexual response, variations in sexual expression, law, birth control and abortion, sexual health, sexual motivation, love, and sexual values. Intended for B.A. in General Biology and non-Biology majors.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; one college-level Biology course*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Research with Communities
oneLiner: Application of research justice and community-engaged research to CSL.
description: Application of research justice and community-engaged research to CSL. Activities will include improving the well-being of communities by addressing biological and social determinants of health. These will be examined within the context of racial/ethnic health disparities caused by systemic racism and social disadvantage. Local health disparities will be addressed by honing skills and knowledge to meet the needs of communities of color through direct service, community organizing, and transcreation. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as BIOL 331 and RRS 331. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; BIOL 100 or BIOL 230; or permission of the instructor.

name: Health Disparities in Cancer
oneLiner: Major determinants of health disparities in cancer including ethnic differences in…
description: Major determinants of health disparities in cancer including ethnic differences in biology and prevention and treatment of cancer. Strategies to overcome these disparities through research, health education, outreach, advocacy, and policy changes. (BIOL 832/BIOL 332 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and BIOL 355; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Evolution
oneLiner: The principles of evolutionary biology, concentrating on basic population genetic…
description: The principles of evolutionary biology, concentrating on basic population genetic mechanisms and methods of analysis. Intended for biology and non-Biology majors.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230*, BIOL 240*, and BIOL 355*.

name: Bioethics
oneLiner: Human experiments, genetic engineering, in-vitro fertilization, human enhancement…
description: Human experiments, genetic engineering, in-vitro fertilization, human enhancement, cloning, reproductive technology, animal testing, euthanasia, and assisted dying. Emphasis on respectful and reflective discussion.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Cell Biology
oneLiner: Cell structure and function, extracellular matrix interactions, signal transduction…
description: Cell structure and function, extracellular matrix interactions, signal transduction, and regulatory mechanisms in cell growth and differentiation.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing with BIOL 230*, BIOL 240*, and CHEM 115*; or upper-division Chemistry or Biochemistry majors with BIOL 230* and either BIOL 240* or CHEM 340*; all with grades of C- or better.

name: Experiments in Cell and Molecular Biology Discussion
oneLiner: Experiments introducing laboratory techniques including microscopy, cytochemistry…
description: Experiments introducing laboratory techniques including microscopy, cytochemistry, spectrophotometric quantitation of macromolecules, organelle isolation, animal cell culture, gene expression, protein analysis, and recombinant DNA techniques. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Biology and Biochemistry majors; GE Area 1A/A2*, BIOL 350*, and BIOL 355*; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 351GW.

name: Experiments in Cell and Molecular Biology - GWAR
oneLiner: Experiments introducing laboratory techniques including microscopy, cytochemistry…
description: Experiments introducing laboratory techniques including microscopy, cytochemistry, spectrophotometric quantitation of macromolecules, organelle isolation, animal cell culture, gene expression, protein analysis, and recombinant DNA techniques. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Biology and Biochemistry majors; upper-division standing; GE Area 1A/A2*, BIOL 350*, and BIOL 355*; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 351.

name: Genetics
oneLiner: Viral, prokaryotic, and eukaryotic genetics.
description: Viral, prokaryotic, and eukaryotic genetics. Population, human, and molecular genetics.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230*, BIOL 240*, and CHEM 115*; or Chemistry or Biochemistry majors with BIOL 230* and either BIOL 240* or CHEM 340*, all with grades of C- or better.

name: Honors Genetics
oneLiner: Advanced topics, new ideas, unsolved problems, reading of original research, and review…
description: Advanced topics, new ideas, unsolved problems, reading of original research, and review of articles in genetics: Mendelian, molecular, and population. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 355 with a grade of B or better. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Molecular Genetics
oneLiner: Current ideas in molecular biology including the transfer and expression of genetic…
description: Current ideas in molecular biology including the transfer and expression of genetic information, interaction and hybridization of genes, molecular mutagens, and molecular evolution. Ethical questions in molecular genetics. Intended for Biology majors.
prereqNotes: BIOL 355* or equivalent with a grade of C- or better.

name: Forensic Genetics: Math Matters
oneLiner: Statistical forensic genetics with a focus on social impact.
description: Statistical forensic genetics with a focus on social impact. Statistical exploration and analyses in R programming language. Creation of an original scientific research project. Critical analysis of forensics in the media. Completion of a forensic genetics policy proposal project. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Computer Science majors with sophomore standing or above; BIOL 230 with a grade of C- or better and MATH 199; or permission of the instructor.

name: Cancer Biology
oneLiner: The molecular and cellular basis of cancer.
description: The molecular and cellular basis of cancer. Emphasis on potential therapeutic targets, including cell cycle regulators, signal transduction mechanisms, cellular differentiation factors, oncogenes, and tumor suppressors. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (BIOL 760/BIOL 360 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; BIOL 350* and BIOL 355*; GPA of 3.0 or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Evolutionary Developmental Biology
oneLiner: Examine the evolution of animal diversity by evaluating the co-option of developmental…
description: Examine the evolution of animal diversity by evaluating the co-option of developmental mechanisms and comparative embryology from representative taxa spanning ancestral multicellular animals through vertebrates. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 355* with a grade of C- or better. BIOL 337 is highly recommended. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Developmental Biology
oneLiner: Early embryonic development including the exploration of the molecular genetic basis…
description: Early embryonic development including the exploration of the molecular genetic basis for tissue differentiation. Gene regulation, chromatin, sex determination, oncogenesis, aging, and pattern formation. (BIOL 782/BIOL 382 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; BIOL 350 and BIOL 355 with grades of C- or better; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology and Biochemistry majors.

name: General Microbiology
oneLiner: Morphology, physiology, genetics, molecular biology, evolution, and taxonomy of…
description: Morphology, physiology, genetics, molecular biology, evolution, and taxonomy of microorganisms. Bacteria and viruses. The importance of microbes in biotechnology, ecology, and public health.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and either CHEM 130 or CHEM 233 with grades of C- or better. Intended for Biology and Biochemistry majors.

name: General Microbiology Laboratory - GWAR
oneLiner: Laboratory techniques in the isolation, cultivation, and identification of microbes…
description: Laboratory techniques in the isolation, cultivation, and identification of microbes, especially bacteria. Microbial properties including nutrition, gene transfer, enzyme induction, and viral replication. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Biology majors; GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 401 (may be taken concurrently).

name: Environmental Microbiology
oneLiner: Study of microbes and microbial communities using molecular and genomic approaches.
description: Study of microbes and microbial communities using molecular and genomic approaches. Primary research data includes novel microbial genomes and metagenomes. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 355, BIOL 401, and BIOL 402GW; CHEM 340 or CHEM 349. Intended for Biology majors.

name: General Virology
oneLiner: Molecular aspects of virus structure, genetics, reproduction, and infection.
description: Molecular aspects of virus structure, genetics, reproduction, and infection. Virus types include bacterial, animal, and plant. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 401 and BIOL 402GW with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Emerging Diseases
oneLiner: Biology of the emerging diseases that threaten humans and wildlife.
description: Biology of the emerging diseases that threaten humans and wildlife. The molecular biology, genetics, epidemiology, ecology, and economic impact of emerging viruses.
prereqNotes: BIOL 350 or BIOL 355 or BIOL 401; and CHEM 130 or CHEM 233.

name: Medical Microbiology
oneLiner: Principles of infection, immunity, and characterization of medically important…
description: Principles of infection, immunity, and characterization of medically important microbial agents.
prereqNotes: Priority enrollment for graduating senior Biology majors and majors requiring this course; BIOL 401 with a grade of C or better; permission of the instructor.

name: Medical Microbiology Laboratory
oneLiner: Basic principles and current standard diagnostic procedures in medical microbiology.
description: Basic principles and current standard diagnostic procedures in medical microbiology. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Priority enrollment for B.S. Biology majors; BIOL 401, BIOL 402GW with a grade of C- or better, and BIOL 430 (may be taken concurrently); permission of the instructor.

name: Immunology
oneLiner: Innate and acquired immunity.
description: Innate and acquired immunity. Recognition of antigens. Mechanisms of immune responses and their induction. Measurement and variations of immunity as in hypersensitivity and immune suppression and their effects on the host. Intended for Biology majors.
prereqNotes: BIOL 350* or BIOL 401*.

name: Immunology Laboratory
oneLiner: Laboratory illustrating antibody-antigen interactions, the cellular basis of immune…
description: Laboratory illustrating antibody-antigen interactions, the cellular basis of immune responses, and the applications of immune and serological reactions. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 402GW or equivalent; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 435.

name: Microbial Physiology
oneLiner: Function, biosynthesis, structure, and chemistry of cells and viruses.
description: Function, biosynthesis, structure, and chemistry of cells and viruses. Focus on transport, chemotaxis, and energy metabolism, the regulation of growth rate and growth efficiency, and mechanisms of viral and microbial differentiation.
prereqNotes: BIOL 401, BIOL 402GW with a grade of C- or better, and CHEM 349 or equivalent. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Microbial Physiology Laboratory
oneLiner: Experiments in the physiology and metabolism of protists and bacteria including growth…
description: Experiments in the physiology and metabolism of protists and bacteria including growth studies, cell fractionation procedures, enzyme preparations and assays, and analyses of cellular molecules. Incorporates analytical instrumentation and statistical techniques. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 442 (may be taken concurrently). Intended for Biology majors.

name: Microbial Genomics
oneLiner: Techniques in comparative microbial genomics including a class project in analyzing and…
description: Techniques in comparative microbial genomics including a class project in analyzing and annotating a novel microbial genome. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 401, BIOL 402GW, and BIOL 355; permission of the instructor.

name: General Parasitology
oneLiner: Biology of animal parasites including parasite structure/function, cellular…
description: Biology of animal parasites including parasite structure/function, cellular, immunological, biochemical, and molecular parasitology, and control and prevention. Examination of the impact of parasitic infection on human health, culture, and socio-economic welfare.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and BIOL 355. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Parasitology Laboratory
oneLiner: Methods and techniques in the examination, preparation, recognition, and identification…
description: Methods and techniques in the examination, preparation, recognition, and identification of protozoan and metazoan parasites of animal hosts. Human parasites with an orientation toward clinical science. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 453 (may be taken concurrently).

name: Biostatistics
oneLiner: Biological measurements, experimental design, data analysis, and statistical methods as…
description: Biological measurements, experimental design, data analysis, and statistical methods as applied to biological problems and methods of data resolution and presentation. Intended for Biology majors. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: One college-level Biology course*.

name: General Entomology
oneLiner: The insects and their close relatives including physiology, external and internal…
description: The insects and their close relatives including physiology, external and internal structures, life cycles, classification of insects to order, ecology in desert, field, forest, and aquatic habitats, and the economic and medical importance of orders. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Natural History of Vertebrates
oneLiner: Structure, behavior, and distribution of amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals…
description: Structure, behavior, and distribution of amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals, especially those of Central California. One all-day field trip required. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Herpetology - GWAR
oneLiner: Evolution, classification, and distribution of amphibians and reptiles.
description: Evolution, classification, and distribution of amphibians and reptiles. The ecology and behavior of California species. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Ornithology Discussion
oneLiner: Anatomy, physiology, behavior, distribution, classification, and evolution of birds.
description: Anatomy, physiology, behavior, distribution, classification, and evolution of birds. Visits to the San Francisco Zoo, private aviaries, and museums. One weekend field trip required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: Biology majors; GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 478GW; or permission of the instructor.

name: Ornithology - GWAR
oneLiner: Anatomy, physiology, behavior, distribution, classification, and evolution of birds.
description: Anatomy, physiology, behavior, distribution, classification, and evolution of birds. Visits to the San Francisco Zoo, private aviaries, and museums. One weekend field trip required. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 478; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Ecology
oneLiner: Interrelationships between organisms and their environment studied at the individual…
description: Interrelationships between organisms and their environment studied at the individual, population, community, and ecosystem levels.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Ecology Field Research Techniques-GWAR
oneLiner: Hands-on experience with ecological research techniques and emphasizing scientific…
description: Hands-on experience with ecological research techniques and emphasizing scientific writing, data analysis, and field work. Engage in field trips to diverse ecological sites to learn methods used to observe, survey, and sample plants, animals, and ecological processes. Develop and carry out an independent ecological research project and produce a formal research paper. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC grading only; CR/NC not allowed)
prereqNotes: BIOL 230* and BIOL 240* with grades of C- or better; BIOL 482* (may be taken concurrently).

name: Ecology of Infectious Diseases
oneLiner: Examination of ecological and evolutionary processes that govern the transmission of…
description: Examination of ecological and evolutionary processes that govern the transmission of pathogens in animal and plant systems, including factors that lead to disease emergence, the impact of diseases on host populations, and theoretical foundations of disease ecology. Experience with developing a research question, formulating a testable hypothesis, biological data collection, quantitative analysis, and written and oral presentations through a group research project to assess ecology and risk of tick-borne diseases in the San Francisco Bay Area. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230* and BIOL 240* with grades of C- or better.

name: Evolution and Diversity of Plants
oneLiner: Comparative biology and phylogeny of the major lineages of plants.
description: Comparative biology and phylogeny of the major lineages of plants. Evolution and diversification of vegetative and reproductive structures, life histories, and ecological adaptations. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240.

name: Biology of the Algae
oneLiner: Collection, preservation, identification, and culturing of marine and freshwater algae.
description: Collection, preservation, identification, and culturing of marine and freshwater algae. Comparative studies of morphology, life history, and ecology. Field trips. Seminar, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (BIOL 702/BIOL 502 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Plant Structure and Function
oneLiner: Plant cells and tissues, their structure, development, and organization into vegetative…
description: Plant cells and tissues, their structure, development, and organization into vegetative and reproductive structures. Evolutionary and ecological interpretation of tissues of vascular plants. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory; 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Plant Biodiversity and California Field Botany
oneLiner: Examine plant biodiversity through principles of classification, phylogenetic…
description: Examine plant biodiversity through principles of classification, phylogenetic relationships, and global biogeography. Hands-on experience gained through numerous field trips and laboratory exercises with live plant material offers practice in the identification of any plant species, collection of herbarium specimens, and other field botany techniques. Expertise gained of all major native Californian plant lineages and ecosystems, including those used by indigenous peoples. Intended for Biology majors. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 3 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only.) (BIOL 814/BIOL 514 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240*; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Plant Physiology
oneLiner: Plant physiology including photosynthesis, water and mineral uptake and distribution…
description: Plant physiology including photosynthesis, water and mineral uptake and distribution, translocation of organic materials. Environmental and internal plant regulatory factors and their effect on growth and metabolism.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and CHEM 130. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Plant Molecular Physiology Laboratory
oneLiner: Molecular, physiological, and biochemical understanding of plant growth and development.
description: Molecular, physiological, and biochemical understanding of plant growth and development. Focus on plant development, plant-plant and plant-environment interactions, photosynthesis, water balance, mineral nutrition, gene expression, cell imaging, data analyses, and presentations. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Biology majors; BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and CHEM 130.

name: Plants, People, and the Planet
oneLiner: Principles of ecology through the study of plants and plant associations.
description: Principles of ecology through the study of plants and plant associations. Ecological concepts, biotic-environmental dynamics and relationships, and levels of ecological integration. Biotic provinces and plant associations in California. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240 or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Conservation Biology
oneLiner: Principles of nature conservation, preservation, and management.
description: Principles of nature conservation, preservation, and management. Theory, laws, and practice of conservation science.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Restoration Ecology
oneLiner: Focuses on the restoration of degraded habitats with an emphasis on the application of…
description: Focuses on the restoration of degraded habitats with an emphasis on the application of ecological theory to restoration practice. A variety of habitats will be covered especially those common to the Bay Area.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240.

name: Wetland Ecology
oneLiner: Ecology of a variety of wetland types, biotic and abiotic characteristics and…
description: Ecology of a variety of wetland types, biotic and abiotic characteristics and processes, conservation, restoration, and management. Field trips to wetland habitats and participation in field and/or greenhouse experiments. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, and BIOL 240; or permission of the instructor.

name: Marine Invertebrate Zoology
oneLiner: Comparative laboratory and field study of local marine invertebrate animals and…
description: Comparative laboratory and field study of local marine invertebrate animals and evolution and functional morphology. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Biology of Fishes Discussion
oneLiner: Morphology, physiology, behavior, ecology, distribution, classification, and evolution…
description: Morphology, physiology, behavior, ecology, distribution, classification, and evolution of marine and freshwater fishes with a focus on California species. Two-weekend field trips. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2, BIOL 230, and BIOL 240; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 570GW; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Biology of Fishes - GWAR
oneLiner: Morphology, physiology, behavior, ecology, distribution, classification, and evolution…
description: Morphology, physiology, behavior, ecology, distribution, classification, and evolution of marine and freshwater fishes with a focus on California species. Two-weekend field trips. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2, BIOL 230, and BIOL 240; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 570; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Colloquium in Ecology, Evolution, and Conservation
oneLiner: Presentations of student and faculty research, recent journal articles, and by outside…
description: Presentations of student and faculty research, recent journal articles, and by outside speakers. Student speakers receive graduate seminar credit. May be repeated for a total of 8 units. (BIOL 872/BIOL 572 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Climate and Ecological Interactions
oneLiner: Theory, observations, and modeling of the two-way interaction between climate and ecology.
description: Theory, observations, and modeling of the two-way interaction between climate and ecology. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (This course is offered as BIOL 577 and ERTH 577. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: MATH 107 and MATH 108, or MATH 199, or MATH 226; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240 or two 200-level or higher courses in Earth & Climate Sciences; or permission of the instructor.

name: Limnology
oneLiner: Physical, chemical, and biological characteristics of inland waters.
description: Physical, chemical, and biological characteristics of inland waters. Individual field projects. Field trips conducted during class time. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and CHEM 215; an ecology course is recommended. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Biological Oceanography & Limnology
oneLiner: Biological, chemical and physical characteristics of Earth's oceans and freshwaters.
description: Biological, chemical and physical characteristics of Earth's oceans and freshwaters. The biology of plankton, nekton, and benthos, emphasizing production and food webs. Identification, sampling, and productivity measurements of marine organisms. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Marine Ecology
oneLiner: Plant and animal relationships in near-shore marine communities and temperate zone…
description: Plant and animal relationships in near-shore marine communities and temperate zone communities of the central California coast.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Marine Ecology Laboratory Discussion
oneLiner: Laboratory and fieldwork in marine ecology serves as an introduction to…
description: Laboratory and fieldwork in marine ecology serves as an introduction to hypothesis-driven research, research design, sampling methods, laboratory techniques, data collection, and analysis. Fieldwork in a variety of marine field environments. Includes use of primary literature and oral and written presentations. (Plus-minus ABC/NC; CR/NC not allowed)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; Biology majors; GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 586GW; or permission of the instructor.

name: Marine Ecology Laboratory - GWAR
oneLiner: Laboratory and fieldwork in marine ecology serves as an introduction to…
description: Laboratory and fieldwork in marine ecology serves as an introduction to hypothesis-driven research, research design, sampling methods, laboratory techniques, data collection, and analysis. Fieldwork in a variety of marine field environments. Includes use of primary literature and oral and written presentations. Lecture: 1 unit; laboratory: 2 units. (Plus-minus ABC/NC; CR/NC not allowed) Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; Biology majors; GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 586; or permission of the instructor.

name: Animal Behavior
oneLiner: General introduction to animal behavior.
description: General introduction to animal behavior. Mechanisms of behavior including development, hormones, neural processes, and cognition. Evolutionary approaches including foraging, habitat selection, communication, sexual selection, mating systems, parental care, and social behavior. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 230* and BIOL 240*.

name: Conservation and Management of Marine Mammals
oneLiner: Biology and scientific principles involved in the conservation and management of marine…
description: Biology and scientific principles involved in the conservation and management of marine mammals. Current regulations and methodologies are critically reviewed and evaluated. Controversies concerning conservation, ecological balance, and specific governmental constraints in the face of a changing environment will be discussed.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and BIOL 355.

name: Physics in Medicine
oneLiner: Mechanics, thermodynamics, and electricity applied to mechanical properties of tissues…
description: Mechanics, thermodynamics, and electricity applied to mechanical properties of tissues, metabolism, membrane transport, control and regulation of physical parameters. Sonography, electromagnetism and quantum physics applied to medical diagnostic technology and imaging.
prereqNotes: PHYS 121 and BIOL 230 or equivalents; or permission of the instructor.

name: Systems Physiology
oneLiner: Integrative mechanisms and control systems in cardiovascular and respiratory physiology.
description: Integrative mechanisms and control systems in cardiovascular and respiratory physiology. Circulation and the distribution and regulation of body fluids. Digestive systems and metabolism.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, and CHEM 130; or Chemistry and Biochemistry majors with BIOL 230 and CHEM 340.

name: Human Physiology Laboratory - GWAR
oneLiner: Experiments in preparation, recording, and analysis of the functioning of human and…
description: Experiments in preparation, recording, and analysis of the functioning of human and other vertebrate organ systems and tissues. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 612 or BIOL 630 (may be taken concurrently). Intended for Biology majors.

name: Vertebrate Histology
oneLiner: Microscopic anatomy of tissues and organ systems of vertebrates.
description: Microscopic anatomy of tissues and organ systems of vertebrates. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Molecular Pathophysiology
oneLiner: Globally important diseases caused by genetic errors, environmental factors, or parasites.
description: Globally important diseases caused by genetic errors, environmental factors, or parasites. Each disease is studied at the molecular, cellular, and physiological levels.
prereqNotes: BIOL 350, BIOL 355, and BIOL 612. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Cardiorespiratory Physiology
oneLiner: The physiology of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems, and their interrelationship.
description: The physiology of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems, and their interrelationship. Organ function in health and disease. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, BIOL 612 or BIOL 630, and PHYS 121; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Environmental Physiology
oneLiner: The physiological and biochemical mechanisms underlying adaptation of animals to…
description: The physiological and biochemical mechanisms underlying adaptation of animals to diverse environments. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 612 or BIOL 630. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Biology of Aging
oneLiner: Biological processes underlying aging.
description: Biological processes underlying aging. Focus on the molecular mechanisms of aging including specific animal models of aging and age-related changes in the major physiological systems in humans. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Biology majors and minors; BIOL 212 or BIOL 612, BIOL 350, and BIOL 355.

name: Pathophysiology
oneLiner: The processes underlying disease in the major physiological systems.
description: The processes underlying disease in the major physiological systems. Focus on understanding the relationship between changes at the molecular, cellular, and tissue levels and their physiological manifestations at the organ and system levels. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Biology majors and minors; BIOL 212 or BIOL 612.

name: Endocrinology
oneLiner: Introduction to the classes of hormones, sources and synthesis of hormones, endocrine…
description: Introduction to the classes of hormones, sources and synthesis of hormones, endocrine target tissues, signaling pathways, and hormonal regulation within the vertebrate endocrine system. Application to clinical real-world endocrine case studies.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240.

name: Reproductive Physiology
oneLiner: Reproductive morphology and physiology of vertebrates.
description: Reproductive morphology and physiology of vertebrates.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, BIOL 330, and CHEM 130; BIOL 492 or another course in vertebrate anatomy is recommended. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Hormones and Behavior
oneLiner: Effects that hormones exert on behavior.
description: Effects that hormones exert on behavior. Hormonal activation and organization of behavior and the nervous system. Actions of hormones compared in humans and non-human species.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; a course in physiology or endocrinology strongly recommended; or permission of the instructor. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Pharmacology
oneLiner: Pharmacology principles including pharmacokinetics of drug absorption and elimination.
description: Pharmacology principles including pharmacokinetics of drug absorption and elimination. Mechanisms of drug action on the body. Commonly used pharmaceutical drugs. (BIOL 723/BIOL 623 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240 with grades of C- or better, BIOL 612, and CHEM 130; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Hematology
oneLiner: Origin and function of mammalian blood cells and plasma.
description: Origin and function of mammalian blood cells and plasma. Cell variations in health and disease. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: A college-level physiology course. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Biophysics
oneLiner: Physical description of free energies and driving forces, energetic and timescales of…
description: Physical description of free energies and driving forces, energetic and timescales of biological processes, interactions of biomolecules, diffusion transport and signaling, protein DNA and membrane structure, molecular motors, cooperative binding, membrane potentials and excitability, and regulation of gene expression.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, CHEM 115, and PHYS 121 or equivalents; or permission of the instructor.

name: Animal Physiology
oneLiner: Exploration of the biodiversity of animals living across Earth's habitats with varying…
description: Exploration of the biodiversity of animals living across Earth's habitats with varying ecologies and life-histories. Focus on the basic functional systems of animals, including metabolism, digestion, energetics, thermal physiology, neuronal and sensory systems, endocrine systems, muscle systems, respiratory systems, circulatory systems, and osmotic and ionic processes. Intended for Biology majors.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230* and BIOL 240*; CHEM 130* or CHEM 233*.

name: Animal Physiology Laboratory Discussion
oneLiner: Approaches to scientific research on the environmental physiology of marine and…
description: Approaches to scientific research on the environmental physiology of marine and estuarine organisms with a focus on metabolic processes. Emphasis on scientific writing and communication. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: Biology majors; GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 612* or BIOL 630* (may be taken concurrently); concurrent enrollment in BIOL 631GW.

name: Animal Physiology Laboratory - GWAR
oneLiner: Approaches to scientific research on the environmental physiology of marine and…
description: Approaches to scientific research on the environmental physiology of marine and estuarine organisms with a focus on metabolic processes. Emphasis on scientific writing and communication. Intended for Biology majors. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; BIOL 612* or BIOL 630* (may be taken concurrently); concurrent enrollment with BIOL 631.

name: Bioinformatics and Sequence Analysis
oneLiner: Principles and methods of biological analysis using computing, including next-gen…
description: Principles and methods of biological analysis using computing, including next-gen sequencing, phylogenetics, sequence variation, and gene expression analysis. Includes a series of hands-on bioinformatics projects using real biological data. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (BIOL 738/BIOL 638 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; BIOL 230 and BIOL 355*; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 337*; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Cellular Neurosciences
oneLiner: Cellular and molecular analysis of neurons.
description: Cellular and molecular analysis of neurons. Cellular, synaptic, and retinal neurophysiology. Electrical and chemical mechanisms underlying intraneuronal and inter-neuronal signaling.
prereqNotes: BIOL 230, BIOL 240, CHEM 130, and PHYS 121; BIOL 350 and BIOL 612 are recommended. Intended for Biology majors.

name: Neural Systems Physiology
oneLiner: Communication between neural centers controlling sensory and motor systems…
description: Communication between neural centers controlling sensory and motor systems, homeostasis, learning, thought, and affect. Connectivity, neurophysiological regulation, and neuropathology. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 328 or BIOL 612.

name: LEADerS Service Learning Course: Learners Engaged in Advocating for Diversity in Science
oneLiner: Examination of issues involving equity and diversity of scientific teaching with a…
description: Examination of issues involving equity and diversity of scientific teaching with a specific focus on the development of inclusive practices within the upper-division courses in Biology. Students will be involved in developing assessments in their partnerships and either implementing (PALS) or developing (LEADS) active learning exercises. Seminar, 2 units; activity, 2 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; BIOL 230 and BIOL 240; BIOL 350 or BIOL 355 or BIOL 357.

name: Peer Assistants for Learning Science (PALS)
oneLiner: Intended for Biology majors interested in revisiting and applying their science…
description: Intended for Biology majors interested in revisiting and applying their science knowledge, understanding importance of diversity, equity, and inclusion in their discipline, gaining insights into teaching science in the university setting, exploring the field of science teaching as a potential career, and learning science through teaching science. Work with faculty and lecturers who have been trained in scientific teaching and are interested in expanding their capacity for active learning and inclusive teaching practices in their course. Lecture, 2 units; Activity, 2 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: BIOL 230*.

name: Optical Engineering for the Biological Sciences
oneLiner: A hands-on introduction to applying advances in low-cost computers and digital cameras…
description: A hands-on introduction to applying advances in low-cost computers and digital cameras to microscope design. Emphasis on learning the fundamentals of optical engineering and image processing used in digital microscopy, as well as essential skills in optical design, instrumentation, machining, and fabrication. Includes building a lensless microscope capable of capturing and processing images of plankton. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP) (This course is offered as BIOL 667 and CHEM 667. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: MATH 226; BIOL 230 or CHEM 215 with a grade of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Ecology and Evolution of Marine Systems I
oneLiner: Introduces highly motivated students to ecological and evolutionary processes that…
description: Introduces highly motivated students to ecological and evolutionary processes that structure subtidal marine environments from the top down (emphasizing effects of predation). Students conduct independent field research and develop scientific writing skills. Lecture, 4 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: BIOL 240 and BIOL 458 or equivalents with grades of C or better; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 671 and either BIOL 699 or BIOL 897.

name: Ecology and Evolution of Marine Systems II
oneLiner: Introduction to ecological and evolutionary processes that structure subtidal marine…
description: Introduction to ecological and evolutionary processes that structure subtidal marine environments from the bottom up (emphasizing foundational habitats). Lecture, 4 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: BIOL 240 and BIOL 458 with grades of C or better; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 670GW and BIOL 699 or BIOL 897.

name: Climate Action: Applied Learning for Real World Change
oneLiner: Apply an evolving understanding of climate change causes, impacts, and solutions…
description: Apply an evolving understanding of climate change causes, impacts, and solutions towards real-world action. Integrate a climate change component into existing major requirements, internships, service learning, employment, fellowships, and/or faculty-student research collaborations. Share the outcomes with peers and reflect on experiences together, as well as participate in peer-led and instructor-led learning exchanges on Climate Change themes. May be repeated for up to 3 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Two courses in the Climate Change Causes, Impacts, and Solutions Certificate.

name: Cooperative Internship in Biology
oneLiner: Written and oral report of work performed with an outside agency and a requested…
description: Written and oral report of work performed with an outside agency and a requested written report from the agency supervisor. Evaluation of work by a Biology adviser and/or faculty committee. May be repeated for a total of 16 units. (This course is not eligible for certification for enrollment with the VA.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to sophomore standing and above; Biology majors; permission of Biology faculty adviser.

name: Directed Reading in Stem Cells Seminar
oneLiner: This "Direct Reading in Stem Cells Seminar" series provides an overview of stem cell…
description: This "Direct Reading in Stem Cells Seminar" series provides an overview of stem cell research, biomedical science and biotechnology, and regenerative medicine. Through course instructors, guest scientists, SFSU alumni, and current research trends, students will learn about fundamentals of stem cell discoveries, their use as research tools, and regenerative medicines. May be repeated for a total of 4 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Upper-Division standing; Qualified stem cell scholars and biomedical science fellows under training and/or conducting independent projects at host sites with the instructor's permission.

name: Strategies for Successful Graduate Applications in STEM
oneLiner: Introduction to graduate research skills, including written and oral communication…
description: Introduction to graduate research skills, including written and oral communication, equity in science, reading and analyzing research, responsible conduct in research, and rigor and responsibility in STEM. May be repeated for a total of 4 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (This course is offered as BIOL 698 and SCI 698. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Senior standing and permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study in Biology
oneLiner: Special study in the laboratory, field, or library under the direction of a member of…
description: Special study in the laboratory, field, or library under the direction of a member of the department. The student must present a written detailed report of the work accomplished to the staff of the department. May be repeated for credit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Biology majors; permission of the department and instructor.

name: Introduction to Research Skills
oneLiner: Introduction to the theory and practice of skills used by research scientists that…
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of skills used by research scientists that include research literature searches, basic concepts in visualizing and interpreting data, analyzing conclusions of research articles, ethics, and safety. Assignments support completion of the degree requirements, including forming a thesis committee and defining a research objective. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Strategies for Successful PhD Applications in STEM
oneLiner: Introduction to graduate research skills, including written and oral communication…
description: Introduction to graduate research skills, including written and oral communication, equity in science, reading and analyzing research, responsible conduct in research, and rigor and responsibility in STEM. May be repeated for a total of 8 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (This course is offered as BIOL 701 and SCI 701. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing and permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Practice of research methods in criminal justice studies in real-world field settings.
description: Practice of research methods in criminal justice studies in real-world field settings. Activity. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division Criminal Justice majors; GE Area 1A/A2; C J 300 (may be taken concurrently); concurrent enrollment in C J 330GW*.

name: Research Methods in Criminal Justice - GWAR
oneLiner: Heuristics refers to data gathering.
description: Heuristics refers to data gathering. How and by what basic procedures is data gathered in criminal justice? Data gathering strategies and techniques, the nature of data gathered by official, governmental agencies, and alternatives to the present arrangement. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Criminal Justice majors; GE Area 1A/A2*; C J 300* (may be taken concurrently); concurrent enrollment in C J 330*.

name: Legal Writing and Research
oneLiner: The legal brief as the focus of strong inference writing in criminal justice.
description: The legal brief as the focus of strong inference writing in criminal justice. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300 (may be taken concurrently); a GWAR course; or permission of the instructor.

name: Comparative Criminal Justice
oneLiner: Ways in which institutions of criminal justice in one society compare with those in…
description: Ways in which institutions of criminal justice in one society compare with those in other societies. Attention is given to U.S., British, European, Asian, and African systems. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. (This course is offered as C J 340 and I R 341. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Intelligence and Intelligence Agencies
oneLiner: The role of modern intelligence agencies in international politics.
description: The role of modern intelligence agencies in international politics. Areas of study include cyber warfare, intelligence collection, hybrid war, and the comparative structures of different intelligence agencies around the world. (This course is offered as I R 360 and C J 360. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: The Making of US Foreign Policy
oneLiner: The role of domestic and transnational actors in making U.S. foreign policy.
description: The role of domestic and transnational actors in making U.S. foreign policy. Examine American culture, media, interest groups, social movements, corporations, and lobbies on policy outcomes. Analyze domestic factors and constraints on U.S. foreign policy decision-making. Consider global constraints and influences on US foreign policy and the impact of international events on Americans. (This course is offered as I R 362, PLSI 362, and C J 362. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GE Area 1A/A2; C J 200 or I R 310 or PLSI 200; or permission of the instructor.

name: Police and Public Policy
oneLiner: The scope of police activities, police administration, discretion, accountability…
description: The scope of police activities, police administration, discretion, accountability, affirmative action, public relations, new technologies, and changing criminal procedure. Issues that the police can and should accomplish, by what rules, and under whose control.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Criminal Profiling
oneLiner: Analysis of the application of personality studies in homicide, arson, rape, and…
description: Analysis of the application of personality studies in homicide, arson, rape, and terrorist cases.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Organized Crime
oneLiner: Organized criminal enterprise recognizes no geographic, legal, or moral boundaries.
description: Organized criminal enterprise recognizes no geographic, legal, or moral boundaries. Salient characteristics and impact of criminal organizations in various settings and crime control strategies.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Crime Scene Investigation
oneLiner: A critical examination of the myths of CSI and a realistic perspective on the roles and…
description: A critical examination of the myths of CSI and a realistic perspective on the roles and duties of forensic and investigative personnel. Application of the scientific method and logical reasoning to careful analysis of the physical evidence present at crime scenes. Additional topics will include probative value and probability of physical evidence; documenting evidence using photos, diagrams, and reports; collecting and preserving evidence; maintaining the chain of custody; and legal and safety considerations. Emphasis on commonly encountered types of evidence, and writing clear, accurate, and mechanically sound reports for use in court.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Criminal Justice Studies majors and minors.

name: Introduction to Forensic Science
oneLiner: Introduces students to scientific evidence and operations of a crime lab, pure and…
description: Introduces students to scientific evidence and operations of a crime lab, pure and applied science, and the scientific method as applied to evidence analysis. Explores the sub-disciplines of forensic science, characteristics of evidence, methods of laboratory analysis, requirements of courtroom admissibility, expert testimony, and forensic error. Lecture, 2 units; activity 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; C J 300* (may be taken concurrently).

name: Race, Crime, and Justice
oneLiner: Ethnic studies methods and cross-cultural perspectives examine the rise of institutions…
description: Ethnic studies methods and cross-cultural perspectives examine the rise of institutions of law enforcement, juvenile and criminal justice, case studies, life histories, and community service learning internships. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as LTNS 430 and C J 435. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Jails and Prisons
oneLiner: The political economy of the prison industry in the U.S. with a focus on the jail as…
description: The political economy of the prison industry in the U.S. with a focus on the jail as well as the prison. Field study at the San Quentin and San Francisco jails.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: The Architecture of Incarceration
oneLiner: The connections between the architectural design and management of U.S. jails and prisons.
description: The connections between the architectural design and management of U.S. jails and prisons.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Criminological Theory
oneLiner: The social, economic, and political context in which criminological theories (past and…
description: The social, economic, and political context in which criminological theories (past and present) emerged and how they are reflected in legal practices. (This course is offered as SOC 451 and C J 452. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2, 1B/A3, 1C/A1, and 2/B4.

name: Community Corrections and Sentencing
oneLiner: Deinstitutionalization movement within the prison industry in the U.S.
description: Deinstitutionalization movement within the prison industry in the U.S. Development of the scale and reach of the prison industry, incarceration rates relative to violent and non-violent offenses, incarceration rates for drug offenses, development of decentralized, and community-related sentencing.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Terrorism and Covert Political Warfare
oneLiner: Terrorism and covert political warfare as international instruments especially since…
description: Terrorism and covert political warfare as international instruments especially since World War II. The use of terror and covert political warfare and the responses to their use. (This course is offered as C J 461 and I R 361. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Juvenile Justice
oneLiner: Analysis of "delinquency," emergence and administration of juvenile law, and analysis…
description: Analysis of "delinquency," emergence and administration of juvenile law, and analysis of social organizations for youthful offenders. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as SOC 452 and C J 470. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2, 1B/A3, 1C/A1, and 2/B4.

name: Contemporary Issues in Juvenile Justice
oneLiner: Examination of the punitive turn in juvenile justice and the impact on youth.
description: Examination of the punitive turn in juvenile justice and the impact on youth. Consideration of how changing concepts of childhood, criminal behavior, and moral development impacted the juvenile court system. Analysis of how courts have responded to the punitive turn with a focus on reform and decarceration.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Intervention Policies in Juvenile Justice
oneLiner: A critical examination of juvenile justice treatment and intervention policies over the…
description: A critical examination of juvenile justice treatment and intervention policies over the past 200 years. Special emphasis on contemporary systems of care and revolutionizing practices.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: California Corrections System
oneLiner: Development of California's correctional system, among the ten largest in the world.
description: Development of California's correctional system, among the ten largest in the world. Critical junctures, including the introduction of the convict labor system, good time, progressive penology and the prison building boom.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/o Youth, Crime, and Justice
oneLiner: Examination of Latino juvenile justice, the myths and realities, and the…
description: Examination of Latino juvenile justice, the myths and realities, and the over-incarceration of Latino youth: its sources, costs, and consequences; and impact on individuals, families, and communities. Latino experiences with schooling, police, gangs, drugs, "juvie," and caseworkers. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as LTNS 485 and C J 485. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Immigration, Criminalization, and Justice
oneLiner: Survey of dynamics that drive immigration from the Global South, the political…
description: Survey of dynamics that drive immigration from the Global South, the political, cultural and economic, incorporation of immigrants, the criminalization of immigrants, the merger of criminal and immigration law enforcement, the impacts of detention and deportation, and the histories and social change produced by immigrant communities.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Criminal Law
oneLiner: Substantive criminal law: legal adjudication within the criminal justice system and the…
description: Substantive criminal law: legal adjudication within the criminal justice system and the criteria according to which guilt is established. Types of crime: homicide, rape, theft, and business crimes. Disposition of convicted offenders. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300; a GWAR course; or permission of the instructor.

name: Criminal Procedure
oneLiner: The salient norms of criminal adjudication as they have developed in case law…
description: The salient norms of criminal adjudication as they have developed in case law reflecting 4th, 5th, and 6th Amendment issues incorporated via the 14th Amendment. Reasonableness, probable cause, privacy, penumbral rights, the assistance of counsel, and federalism.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300; a GWAR course; or permission of the instructor.

name: Analysis of the Felon in Society
oneLiner: Examination of the process of Re-entry (post-incarceration) from the perspective of…
description: Examination of the process of Re-entry (post-incarceration) from the perspective of individuals who have lived it. Lecture, 1 unit; activity, 2 units. (This course is offered as SOC 510 and C J 510. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2, 1B/A3, 1C/A1, and 2/B4, or permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Analysis of Re-entry and Housing
oneLiner: Examine the strange, tumultuous, and sometimes cruel period of reentry after…
description: Examine the strange, tumultuous, and sometimes cruel period of reentry after incarceration. Explore current approaches to re-entry, focusing on the key element of housing. A critical look at dated and current theories concerning re-integration/integration, examining theories inspired by medical, social, and criminology models. Critically examine current practices of reentry, which tend towards a one size fits all (cookie-cutter) approach. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. (This course is offered as SOC 511, C J 511, and USP 511. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Extremism as Crime
oneLiner: Domestic extremism in the U.S. (militia, hate crimes, terrorism).
description: Domestic extremism in the U.S. (militia, hate crimes, terrorism).

name: Alternatives to Criminalization
oneLiner: Examination of the causes and consequences of criminalization with a focus on…

Engagement with Bay Area organizations working on community organizing and redistributive policies as solutions to the problems of criminalization, incarceration, and harm such as harm reduction, restorative justice, etc. Reflexive, ethical practice of qualitative methods, focused on ethnography and Participatory Action Research.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300.

name: School Violence and Discipline
oneLiner: Examination of the perceptions and realities of contemporary public school violence…

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300 and C J 330GW; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Examination of the role violence plays in the lives of ghetto subjects; conceptual…

prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Youth Gangs in Community Context
oneLiner: Examination of youth gangs in America within their social, economic, and political…
description: Examination of youth gangs in America within their social, economic, and political contexts from their earliest development to the present day; theories of gang formation and stories of the gang experience.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; C J 300 and C J 330GW; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Examination of the criminalization of gender and sexuality utilizing feminist and queer…
description: Examination of the criminalization of gender and sexuality utilizing feminist and queer perspectives on criminality; understanding of how laws, policing practices, courtrooms, and institutions regulate gender and sexuality; and examination of effects on labor market opportunities, life chances, and gendered ideas of protection and punishment.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Capstone in Criminal Justice Studies
oneLiner: Reflection and demonstration of intellectual and scholarly growth while in the Criminal…

name: Criminal Justice Studies Internship
oneLiner: Fieldwork in approved criminal justice studies related public, private, and non-profit…

name: Introduction to Creative Writing
oneLiner: The creative writing process.

oneLiner: Develop a robust writing practice in community with fellow majors.
description: Develop a robust writing practice in community with fellow majors. Introduction to department expectations in the classroom and to faculty members' varying writing practices and creative processes. Training in practical use of advising materials, website information, and resources and opportunities both within the University and in the Bay Area literary community.

prereqNotes: Restricted to Creative Writing majors; GE Area 1A/A2; non-majors admitted with permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Examination of the literary genre of graphic memoir and graphic biography within the…

name: Craft of Poetry - GWAR
oneLiner: Focus on basic craft elements of poetry: diction, imagery, rhythm, voice, and form.

oneLiner: Focus on basic craft elements of fiction: plot, dialogue, character, point of view, and…

oneLiner: Study of techniques and craft in a wide selection of contemporary poetry from various…
