name: Contemporary World Poetry
oneLiner: Study of techniques and craft in a wide selection of contemporary poetry from various…
description: Study of techniques and craft in a wide selection of contemporary poetry from various cultures and nations. (C W 814/C W 514 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Writers on Writing
oneLiner: Faculty and visiting writers representing a range of styles and subjects read from…
description: Faculty and visiting writers representing a range of styles and subjects read from their works and discuss their creative process with students. (C W 820/C W 520 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Playwright's Theatre Workshop
oneLiner: Projects designed to give playwrights opportunities to refine their craft through…
description: Projects designed to give playwrights opportunities to refine their craft through workshops, rehearsals, readings, and dramaturgical assignments. May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Fourteen Hills Literary Magazine
oneLiner: Editing and publishing Fourteen Hills, the graduate literary magazine of the Creative…
description: Editing and publishing Fourteen Hills, the graduate literary magazine of the Creative Writing Department. Selection of material, design, production, and distribution. May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Creative Writing or permission of the instructor.

name: Poetry Center Workshop
oneLiner: A poetry writing and study course aligned with The Poetry Center Reading Series.
description: A poetry writing and study course aligned with The Poetry Center Reading Series. Features guest performances throughout the semester by outstanding local, national, and international poets, writers, musicians, and related artists. (C W 850/C W 550 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Workshop in Creative Nonfiction
oneLiner: Creation and revision of original creative nonfiction to a finished, publishable state.
description: Creation and revision of original creative nonfiction to a finished, publishable state. May be repeated for a maximum of 18 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: M.F.A. Workshop in Fiction
oneLiner: Students are expected to concentrate on the revision of fiction, on bringing work to a…
description: Students are expected to concentrate on the revision of fiction, on bringing work to a finished, publishable state. Emphasizes the short story. May be repeated for a total of 18 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to M.F.A. Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Workshop in Poetry
oneLiner: Students are expected to concentrate on the revision of poetry, on bringing work to a…
description: Students are expected to concentrate on the revision of poetry, on bringing work to a finished, publishable state. May be repeated for a total of 18 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Workshop in Playwriting
oneLiner: Students are expected to concentrate on the revision of a play, on bringing work to a…
description: Students are expected to concentrate on the revision of a play, on bringing work to a finished state, ready for production. May be repeated for a total of 18 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Practicum in Teaching
oneLiner: Put theory into practice by observing and participating in undergraduate courses under…
description: Put theory into practice by observing and participating in undergraduate courses under the supervision of Creative Writing instructors. Engage in a process of discovery of the values, beliefs, ideals, and aesthetics that can inform future Creative Writing pedagogies and the development of Creative Writing syllabi. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Teaching Creative Writing
oneLiner: Theoretical and practical aspects of teaching creative writing. (Plus-minus letter…
description: Theoretical and practical aspects of teaching creative writing. (Plus-minus letter grade only.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Craft of Translation
oneLiner: Literary translation: the art and craft of translation.
description: Literary translation: the art and craft of translation. Students familiarize themselves with the best models and develop skills in their own translation.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: Theory of Translation
oneLiner: Examination of the art of translation from a wide range of theoretical perspectives.
description: Examination of the art of translation from a wide range of theoretical perspectives. Focus on linguistic, literary, political, and philosophical aspects of the transfer of meaning between languages in an era of globalization. Evaluation of contending theories and application to the practice of translation. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students with a working knowledge of a language other than English.

name: Community Projects in Literature
oneLiner: Students exercise their writing skills through internships with community literary…
description: Students exercise their writing skills through internships with community literary organizations. May be repeated for a total of 6 units at one level. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [CSL may be available] (C W 875/C W 675 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: M.F.A. Craft and Process Tutorial in Fiction
oneLiner: Examination of the creative process, emphasizing techniques, style, and structure.
description: Examination of the creative process, emphasizing techniques, style, and structure. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 18 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate M.F.A. in Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: M.F.A. Craft and Process Tutorial in Poetry
oneLiner: Examination of creative process emphasizing techniques, style, and structure.
description: Examination of creative process emphasizing techniques, style, and structure. Topic to be specified in Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 18 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA in Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

name: M.F.A. Craft and Process Tutorial in Playwriting
oneLiner: Examination of creative process emphasizing techniques, style, and structure.
description: Examination of creative process emphasizing techniques, style, and structure. Topics to be specified in Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 18 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to M.F.A. in Creative Writing students or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: (CR/NC grading only)
description: (CR/NC grading only)

ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

oneLiner: (CR/NC grading only)

ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: A special study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a faculty…
description: A special study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a faculty member. Open only to graduate students of demonstrated ability to do independent work. Enrollment by petition (form available in the department office). May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor.

name: Child Development, Social Justice, and Academic Success
oneLiner: Focus on educational and social justice for child and adolescent development.
description: Focus on educational and social justice for child and adolescent development. General education skills, writing, oral communication, critical thinking, and quantitative reasoning are systematically reinforced. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to freshmen.

name: Introduction to Applied Child and Adolescent Development
oneLiner: Study of the growth and development of children from prenatal through adolescence.
description: Study of the growth and development of children from prenatal through adolescence. Physical, cognitive, linguistic, social, moral, and emotional aspects of development with attention to both typical and atypical development in each area are discussed. Focus on the influences of culture, family, environment, and abuse/neglect. Introduction to an application of development knowledge to best inform practices and interactions with infants, children, and adolescents. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

name: Foundations in Early Childhood
oneLiner: Observation of teachers and children under the age of five years in a quality licensed…
description: Observation of teachers and children under the age of five years in a quality licensed center or program. Foundations and best practices in early childhood education. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: ENG 114 or equivalent or permission of instructor. Priority enrollment for freshmen and sophomores.

name: Infants, Toddlers, and Families
oneLiner: Research and theories in developmental science and their application in families and…
description: Research and theories in developmental science and their application in families and communities from conception to age three. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP) [Formerly FCS 223]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors; or permission of the instructor.

name: Principles and Practices in Early Childhood Programs
oneLiner: Historical context and theoretical perspectives in early care and education.
description: Historical context and theoretical perspectives in early care and education. Examination of the role of the early childhood educator, identification of best practices for environmental design, curriculum, and teaching strategies. Exploration of teacher-child relationships, professional ethics, career pathways, and professional standards. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [CSL may be available]

name: Children, Families, and Community: An Ecological Perspective
oneLiner: Understanding children, families, and community from an ecological perspective.
description: Understanding children, families, and community from an ecological perspective. Emphasis on the contribution of basic and applied research to development in relation to family and community.

name: Practicum in Early Childhood Education
oneLiner: Hands-on, supervised practicum experience in licensed preschools or early childhood…
description: Hands-on, supervised practicum experience in licensed preschools or early childhood education centers working directly with children. A minimum of 100 hours is required at approved sites, with regular observation and feedback provided by trained course instructors or designated faculty supervisors. Placement requirements vary based on the type of certification students are pursuing. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CAD 610]
prereqNotes: CAD 210* and CAD 260*; either CAD 215* or CAD 230*; or equivalents.

name: Professional Roles and Careers in Child and Adolescent Development
oneLiner: Overview of the field of child and adolescent development including an introduction to…
description: Overview of the field of child and adolescent development including an introduction to careers providing services to children, youth, and families. Topics include current issues and trends in providing services for children, youth, and families in the United States, and a historical overview of social services, education, and public policies related to children, youth, and families. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors.

name: Developing Language and Literacy Skills in Young Children
oneLiner: Evidence-based theories and application of support for mono- and multi-lingual language…
description: Evidence-based theories and application of support for mono- and multi-lingual language and literacy development in early childhood.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors, and Early Childhood Development minors; CAD 210* and CAD 260*.

name: Curriculum and Development in Early Childhood
oneLiner: Curriculum and environments for young children.
description: Curriculum and environments for young children. Exploration of teaching strategies and curriculum development based on theoretical frameworks, observation, and assessment. Focus on the teacher's role in supporting development and learning across the curriculum, including all content areas. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors.

name: Community Youth Development
oneLiner: Introduction to youth and community development with an emphasis on community supports…
description: Introduction to youth and community development with an emphasis on community supports and opportunities for healthy youth development. Theories and research used to construct a framework for youth development. Program models and legislation are examined. Includes off-campus work with a local youth/community program. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors; upper-division standing; CAD 210 and CAD 260 or equivalents.

name: Applied Developmental Science: Prenatal Through Early Childhood - GWAR
oneLiner: Research and theories in developmental science and their application to practice from…
description: Research and theories in developmental science and their application to practice from prenatal through early childhood (ABC/NC grading only). [Formerly CAD 410]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors; GE Area 1A/A2*; CAD 210 and CAD 260 or equivalents with grades of C or higher.

name: Applied Developmental Science: Middle Childhood through Emerging Adulthood
oneLiner: Research and theories in developmental science and their application to practice from…
description: Research and theories in developmental science and their application to practice from middle childhood through emerging adulthood. (Plus-minus letter grade)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors; GE Area 1A/A2*; CAD 210 and CAD 260 or equivalents with grades of C or higher.

name: Assessment and Observation with Children
oneLiner: Interpretation, evaluation, and practice of measurement and assessment tools used with…
description: Interpretation, evaluation, and practice of measurement and assessment tools used with young children including observation techniques and standardized tests. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP) [Formerly FCS 420]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors; CAD 210 or equivalent.

name: Administration of Programs for Young Children
oneLiner: Organization, administration, development, and evaluation of programs serving young…
description: Organization, administration, development, and evaluation of programs serving young children in group settings. Focus on philosophy, program design, staffing, licensing, housing, equipment, funding, and family/community involvement. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors; CAD 210 and CAD 260.

name: Family Stress, Coping, and Resilience
oneLiner: Family resilience and ways in which diverse families react to and resolve crises with…
description: Family resilience and ways in which diverse families react to and resolve crises with an emphasis on the nature of crises, impact on family functioning, and methods of prevention, management, and intervention. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly FCS 426]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Understanding and Working with Diverse Families
oneLiner: Drawing on a variety of disciplines, examination of experiences of families including…
description: Drawing on a variety of disciplines, examination of experiences of families including family diversity, theories on families, and challenges families face; application in the areas of family engagement, involvement, and support. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors; CAD 210 and CAD 260 or equivalents.

name: Research Methods in Child and Adolescent Development
oneLiner: Scientific analysis, writing, research, and statistical methods in child and adolescent…
description: Scientific analysis, writing, research, and statistical methods in child and adolescent development with a focus on conducting socially, culturally, and/or historically contextualized research.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors; CAD 300* and CAD 410GW* with a grade of C or better.

name: Adult Supervision and Leadership in Early Childhood Programs
oneLiner: Exploration of adult supervision, administration and leadership in early childhood…
description: Exploration of adult supervision, administration and leadership in early childhood programs from theoretical and personal perspectives. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors; CAD 210 and CAD 260 or equivalents with grades of C or higher; CAD 215 or CAD 230 or equivalents with grades of C or higher.

name: Child Life: Theory and Application
oneLiner: Examination of children and their families in a healthcare setting.
description: Examination of children and their families in a healthcare setting. Emphasis on the perspective of a Child Life Specialist with the purpose of developing the skills to aid in minimizing the stress and anxiety experienced during hospitalization. Focus on educational and play components, and the general support and scope of practice unique to the field. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors.

name: Loss and Grief: Children, Youth, Families and Community
oneLiner: Introduction to concepts surrounding the nature of suffering and issues of death and…
description: Introduction to concepts surrounding the nature of suffering and issues of death and dying. Examination of these concepts from a theoretical perspective with attention to ethical and moral issues from a cross-cultural diversity perspective, and the impact of death, dying, and bereavement on a family and community. Identification and utilization of resources that promote positive coping skills and strategies for children and youth. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors and Early Childhood Development minors.

name: Child and Adolescent Development Internship Seminar
oneLiner: Analysis and discussion of agencies that serve children, youth, and families with…
description: Analysis and discussion of agencies that serve children, youth, and families with regard to professional competencies, standards and ethics, leadership, organizational structure, and functioning. Prepares students for professional employment in the field of child and adolescent development. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CAD 210* and CAD 260* or equivalents with a grade of C or higher; CAD 300 (may be taken concurrently); concurrent enrollment in CAD 601.

name: Child and Adolescent Development Internship
oneLiner: Supervised experience in educational institutions, health and human service agencies…
description: Supervised experience in educational institutions, health and human service agencies, and organizations that serve children, youth, and families. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: CAD 210* and CAD 260* or equivalents with a grade of C or higher; CAD 300 (may be taken concurrently); concurrent enrollment in CAD 600.

name: Children, Youth, and Public Policy
oneLiner: Overview of how public policies for services for children and youth are developed…
description: Overview of how public policies for services for children and youth are developed, adopted, and implemented; policy process and historical and current policy issues in areas of education and child care. (Plus-minus letter grade only; CR/NC not allowed)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors; CAD 210 and CAD 260 or equivalents.

name: Applied Advanced Developmental Science in Child and Adolescent Development
oneLiner: Synthesis of research and application in developmental science to promote positive…
description: Synthesis of research and application in developmental science to promote positive development across childhood and adolescence. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors; CAD 210, CAD 260, CAD 300*, and CAD 410GW*.

name: International Field Study in Child and Adolescent Development
oneLiner: Comparison of child development programs and settings in international venues with that…
description: Comparison of child development programs and settings in international venues with that of the U.S. Involves travel as a group for 2 to 3 weeks to selected countries outside the U.S. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2 or permission of the instructor.

name: Projects in the Teaching of CAD
oneLiner: Training and experience in the teaching of child and adolescent development.
description: Training and experience in the teaching of child and adolescent development. Serve as an Instructional Aide to a Child and Adolescent Development instructor and receive training in teaching and learning principles as well as participate in teaching-related activities. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: A grade of B+ or better in the course that the student will be assisting in and permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: An intensive study of a particular issue in child and adolescent development selected…
description: An intensive study of a particular issue in child and adolescent development selected by the student. Enrollment by petition. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; permission of the instructor and major adviser.

name: Preparation for Chemistry
oneLiner: Elementary concepts of chemistry.
description: Elementary concepts of chemistry. Development of skills in applying mathematics to solving problems in chemistry. Preparation for CHEM 115 or CHEM 180. (Plus-minus ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Category I or II QR/Math placement; or Category III or IV placement for QR/Math with GE Area 2/B4 (may be taken concurrently) with a grade of C or better; or MATH 107 or MATH 197 (may be taken concurrently) with a grade of C or better.

name: Survey of Chemistry
oneLiner: Principles of general and organic chemistry and biochemistry.
description: Principles of general and organic chemistry and biochemistry. Suitable for Pre-Nursing, Exercise Science, and Health Science majors. Not preparation for CHEM 115.
prereqNotes: Category I or II QR/Math placement; or Category III or IV QR/Math placement and MATH 197 with a grade of C or better; or GE Area 2/B4 (may be taken concurrently).

name: Survey of Chemistry Laboratory
oneLiner: Laboratory to accompany or follow CHEM 101.
description: Laboratory to accompany or follow CHEM 101. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply)

name: General Chemistry I
oneLiner: The first semester of a two-semester sequence in general chemistry intended for…
description: The first semester of a two-semester sequence in general chemistry intended for Biology, Biochemistry, and Chemistry majors and those interested in pursuing post-baccalaureate work in the health professions. Essential concepts of atomic properties, bonding, intermolecular forces, reaction chemistry, stoichiometry, redox chemistry, and acid-base theory. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: CAT I or II placement for QR/MATH* or CAT III or IV placement for QR/MATH with a grade of C or better in MATH 124* or MATH 197* or MATH 199*. All students will be required to complete an online math review at the start of the semester.

name: General Organic Chemistry
oneLiner: Common organic compounds and basic principles.
description: Common organic compounds and basic principles. For laboratory, see CHEM 234. Cannot be used for the Chemistry or Biochemistry degrees.
prereqNotes: CHEM 115* with a grade of C or better.

name: Chemistry for Energy and the Environment
oneLiner: Study of the fundamental chemical principles that underlie chemical processes in the…
description: Study of the fundamental chemical principles that underlie chemical processes in the environment and the chemical processes that are important to the generation of energy. Suitable for Engineering and Environmental Studies majors. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply)
prereqNotes: Category I or II placement for QR/Math. Category III or IV for QR/Math placement must have completed MATH 197 with a grade of C or better or be enrolled in a GE Area 2/B4 course, or have satisfied the GE Area 2/B4 requirement. High school chemistry is recommended.

name: General Chemistry II
oneLiner: The second semester in a two semester sequence in general chemistry course intended for…
description: The second semester in a two semester sequence in general chemistry course intended for Biology, Biochemistry, and Chemistry majors and those pursuing post-baccalaureate work in the health professions. Chemical equilibria including solubility, acid-base and redox, thermodynamics, kinetics, and electrochemistry. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 115* with a grade of C or better.

name: Organic Chemistry I
oneLiner: Principles of organic chemistry emphasizing the structure, properties, and reactions of…
description: Principles of organic chemistry emphasizing the structure, properties, and reactions of alkanes, cycloalkanes, alkyl, halides, alcohols, ethers, and alkenes. Stereochemistry. Mechanisms of substitution and elimination reactions. Primarily for students majoring in Chemistry and Biochemistry. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Priority enrollment for Chemistry and Biochemistry majors; CHEM 115 and CHEM 215* with grades of C or better; other majors permitted on a space-available basis.

name: Organic Chemistry I Laboratory
oneLiner: Techniques and selected experiments in organic chemistry.
description: Techniques and selected experiments in organic chemistry. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 130 or CHEM 233 with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).

name: Organic Chemistry II
oneLiner: Introduction to NMR as a technique in structure elucidation and continuation of CHEM…
description: Introduction to NMR as a technique in structure elucidation and continuation of CHEM 233 functional group topics including alkynes, simple and complicated aromatic ring systems, ketones, aldehydes, carboxylic acids and their derivatives. Other topics include carbonyl condensations and the chemistry of substituted benzenes. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CHEM 335]
prereqNotes: CHEM 233* with a grade of C or better.

name: Organic Chemistry II Laboratory
oneLiner: Techniques and experiments in organic synthesis, isolation, purification, and…
description: Techniques and experiments in organic synthesis, isolation, purification, and characterization. Intended for science majors. Activity, 1 unit; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CHEM 336]
prereqNotes: CHEM 234* and CHEM 235* (may be taken concurrently) with grades of C or better.

name: Mathematics and Physics for Chemistry
oneLiner: Integrated mathematics and physics for physical chemistry including fluids, wave…
description: Integrated mathematics and physics for physical chemistry including fluids, wave motion, thermodynamics, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, introductory vector calculus, and introductory differential equations and linear algebra. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 215, MATH 227, PHYS 230, and PHYS 232 or (on advisement) PHYS 121 and PHYS 122, all with grades of C or better; or permission of instructor; concurrent enrollment in CHEM 351 is strongly recommended.

name: Physical Chemistry for Life Sciences I
oneLiner: Application of chemical equilibria and thermodynamics, the kinetic theory of gases, and…
description: Application of chemical equilibria and thermodynamics, the kinetic theory of gases, and properties of solutions to biological systems. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. Designed for Biochemistry, pre-professional curricula, Biology, and BA in Chemistry majors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 321 (may be taken concurrently), CHEM 235*, MATH 227*, and one of PHYS 121*, PHYS 230*, or PHYS 240* with grades of C or better; CHEM 340 or CHEM 349 recommended.

name: Physical Chemistry for Life Sciences II
oneLiner: Quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, biophysical spectroscopy, intermolecular forces…
description: Quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, biophysical spectroscopy, intermolecular forces, macromolecules, and statistical thermodynamics. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. Intended for Biochemistry and Biology majors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 235*, CHEM 321 (may be taken concurrently), MATH 227*, and one of PHYS 121*, PHYS 230*, or PHYS 240* all with grades of C or better; CHEM 300 and 340 or CHEM 349 recommended.

name: Quantitative Chemical Analysis
oneLiner: Foundation course in analytical chemistry with a focus on quantitative analysis.
description: Foundation course in analytical chemistry with a focus on quantitative analysis. Topics include uncertainties, statistics, equilibria, titrimetric methods, electrochemistry and potentiometry, molecular and atomic spectroscopy, mass spectroscopy, and chromatography. Intended for Chemistry, Biochemistry, and Biology majors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 215* with a grade of C or better.

name: Quantitative Chemical Analysis Laboratory
oneLiner: Practical experience in performing accurate and precise measurements of chemical…
description: Practical experience in performing accurate and precise measurements of chemical species in a variety of real-world samples using gravimetric, titrimetric, potentiometric, spectroscopic, and chromatographic methods. Intended for Chemistry, Biochemistry, and Biology majors. Laboratory. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 321* with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).

name: Inorganic Chemistry
oneLiner: Theories of chemical bonding and their application to inorganic systems with an…
description: Theories of chemical bonding and their application to inorganic systems with an emphasis on transition metal complexes. Molecular Symmetry. Acid/base, redox, and solid-state chemistry. An introduction to organometallic and bioinorganic chemistry. Intended for Chemistry, Biochemistry, and Biology majors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 215* and CHEM 235* with grades of C or better.

name: Biochemistry I
oneLiner: Introduction to Biochemistry including protein structure and function, carbohydrate…
description: Introduction to Biochemistry including protein structure and function, carbohydrate metabolism, enzyme kinetics and thermodynamics, and electron transport chain. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 215, CHEM 233, and CHEM 235* with grades of C or better. Intended for Chemistry, Biochemistry, and Biology majors.

name: Biochemistry II
oneLiner: Biosynthesis and degradation of lipids, amino acids, and nucleotides.
description: Biosynthesis and degradation of lipids, amino acids, and nucleotides. Protein synthesis, folding, and degradation. DNA and RNA structure. DNA replication and transcription. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 340* with a grade of C or better.

name: Biochemistry I Laboratory
oneLiner: Chemical and enzymatic experiments involving proteins, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids…
description: Chemical and enzymatic experiments involving proteins, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids with emphasis on enzyme kinetics. Utilization of standard and modern biochemical techniques. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Chemistry and Biochemistry majors; CHEM 234*, and CHEM 340* (may be taken concurrently) or CHEM 349* (may be taken concurrently) with grades of C or better; CHEM 321 is recommended.

name: General Biochemistry
oneLiner: Survey of major areas in Biochemistry including enzymology, bioenergetics, and…
description: Survey of major areas in Biochemistry including enzymology, bioenergetics, and carbohydrate, lipid, and nucleic acid metabolism. Not intended for B.S. Biochemistry or Chemistry majors. Students who have completed CHEM 340 may not take CHEM 349 for credit.
prereqNotes: CHEM 215* with a grade of C or better, and CHEM 130* with a grade of C or better or CHEM 235* with a grade of C- or better. Nutrition and Dietetics majors CHEM 130* with a grade of C or better.

name: Physical Chemistry I: Thermodynamics and Kinetics
oneLiner: Thermodynamics and kinetics theory.
description: Thermodynamics and kinetics theory. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; CHEM 233 and CHEM 251 (concurrent enrollment recommended); or MATH 228 and either PHYS 230 and PHYS 232; or (on advisement) PHYS 121, PHYS 122, and CHEM 321 (may be taken concurrently); all with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Physical Chemistry II: Quantum Chemistry and Spectroscopy
oneLiner: Quantum chemistry, spectroscopy of atoms and molecules, and statistical thermodynamics.
description: Quantum chemistry, spectroscopy of atoms and molecules, and statistical thermodynamics. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; CHEM 233 and CHEM 251; or MATH 228 and either PHYS 230 and PHYS 232; or (on advisement) PHYS 121, PHYS 122, and CHEM 321; all with grades of C or better; or permission of instructor.

name: Computer Applications in Chemistry and Biochemistry
oneLiner: Data acquisition, manipulation, and presentation with an emphasis on software used in…
description: Data acquisition, manipulation, and presentation with an emphasis on software used in chemistry and biochemistry laboratories. Computational chemistry and molecular visualization software for small and large molecules. Development of interactive molecular visualization web pages. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 233 and CHEM 321 with grades of C or better.

name: Chemistry Behind Environmental Pollution
oneLiner: Traditional and contemporary topics in environmental chemistry.
description: Traditional and contemporary topics in environmental chemistry. Understanding and appreciation of various chemical processes and principles underlying environmental problems facing society.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; CHEM 115* or CHEM 180* with a grade of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Contemporary Chemistry and Biochemistry Research - GWAR
oneLiner: Improve skills in written and oral communication with an emphasis on the communication…
description: Improve skills in written and oral communication with an emphasis on the communication skills expected of professional chemists and biochemists. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division Chemistry and Biochemistry majors; GE Area 1A/A2; CHEM 215 or CHEM 234 with a grade of C or higher.

name: Environmental Analysis
oneLiner: Practical analysis of real-world samples and environmental pollutants.
description: Practical analysis of real-world samples and environmental pollutants. Statistics, QA/QC, heavy metal analysis via atomic spectroscopy, and organic pollutant analysis via GC/MS. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 321* and CHEM 322* with grades of C or better.

name: Instrumental Analysis
oneLiner: Instrumental methods for chemical and biochemical analysis including basic electronics…
description: Instrumental methods for chemical and biochemical analysis including basic electronics, molecular and atomic spectroscopy, IR and Raman spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and chromatography. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 321* and CHEM 322* with grades of C or better.

name: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry Laboratory
oneLiner: Modern techniques in inorganic chemistry with an emphasis on synthesis…
description: Modern techniques in inorganic chemistry with an emphasis on synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of metals in a variety of materials including biological and environmental samples. Laboratory. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 321, CHEM 322, and CHEM 325* with grades of C or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Advanced Organic Chemistry
oneLiner: Theoretical aspects of organic chemistry, molecular structure, and reaction mechanisms.…
description: Theoretical aspects of organic chemistry, molecular structure, and reaction mechanisms. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 235* with a grade of C or better.

name: Biophysical Chemistry Laboratory
oneLiner: Experiments using modern techniques in biochemistry, bioinformatics, molecular biology…
description: Experiments using modern techniques in biochemistry, bioinformatics, molecular biology, and biophysics for the study of biological macromolecules. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Charges for missing or damaged laboratory locker items apply) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 343 with a grade of C or better and CHEM 301 or CHEM 353 (may be taken concurrently).

name: Experimental Physical Chemistry with Laboratory
oneLiner: Emphasis on molecular spectroscopy, thermodynamics, kinetics, electrochemistry…
description: Emphasis on molecular spectroscopy, thermodynamics, kinetics, electrochemistry, applications of computational chemistry, and error analysis. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 321 and CHEM 322; either CHEM 300 and CHEM 301 or CHEM 351 and CHEM 353 with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Organic Chemistry of Drug Synthesis and Activity
oneLiner: Survey of organic chemistry topics related to modern pharmaceuticals including…
description: Survey of organic chemistry topics related to modern pharmaceuticals including heterocyclic chemistry (synthesis and presence in drugs), metabolism, drug-delivery, an overview of various classes of drugs, and antibody-drug conjugates. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 235* with a grade of C or better; concurrent enrollment in CHEM 340* or CHEM 349*.

name: Research Trends in Chemistry and Biochemistry - GWAR
oneLiner: Self-directed learning experience for undergraduates in modern research topics in…
description: Self-directed learning experience for undergraduates in modern research topics in chemistry and biochemistry. (Plus-minus ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; CHEM 340; GPA of 3.0 or better.

name: Optical Engineering for the Biological Sciences
oneLiner: A hands-on introduction to applying advances in low-cost computers and digital cameras…
description: A hands-on introduction to applying advances in low-cost computers and digital cameras to microscope design. Emphasis on learning the fundamentals of optical engineering and image processing used in digital microscopy, as well as essential skills in optical design, instrumentation, machining, and fabrication. Includes building a lensless microscope capable of capturing and processing images of plankton. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 2 units. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP) (This course is offered as BIOL 667 and CHEM 667. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: MATH 226; BIOL 230 or CHEM 215 with a grade of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Chemical Oceanography
oneLiner: Investigation of the composition and dynamics of the ocean through chemistry.…
description: Investigation of the composition and dynamics of the ocean through chemistry. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CHEM 215 or equivalent.

name: Instructional Methods in Teaching Chemistry and Biochemistry
oneLiner: Introduction to effective teaching strategies in science classrooms grounded in current…
description: Introduction to effective teaching strategies in science classrooms grounded in current science education theory and research. May not be repeated for credit. (Plus-minus ABC/NC; CR/NC not allowed) (CHEM 885/CHEM 685 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; Chemistry majors and minors and Biochemistry majors; GPA of 3.0 or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Experiences in Teaching Chemistry and Biochemistry
oneLiner: Activity practicum for students serving as Learning Assistants (LAs) in STEM courses.
description: Activity practicum for students serving as Learning Assistants (LAs) in STEM courses. LAs will directly assist STEM instructors in facilitating active learning in their classrooms. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus ABC/NC; CR/NC not allowed)
prereqNotes: A grade of B or better in the course in which the student will be instructing; CHEM 685 (may be taken concurrently); or permission of the instructor.

name: Cooperative Education in Chemistry
oneLiner: Supervised chemistry laboratory experience in the industry.
description: Supervised chemistry laboratory experience in the industry. A final written report is required. May be repeated for a total of 3 units. (This course is not eligible for certification for enrollment with the VA.) (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor. Enrollment by prior arrangement with supervising faculty member and industry sponsor. See department adviser for details.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Laboratory or library research work focused on chemistry and biochemistry problems…
description: Laboratory or library research work focused on chemistry and biochemistry problems directed by a department faculty. For advanced, superior students majoring or minoring in Chemistry or Biochemistry. Final written report required. May be repeated. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the department and instructor.

name: Electron Microscopy
oneLiner: Introduction to electron microscopy with a focus on instrumentation, image formation…
description: Introduction to electron microscopy with a focus on instrumentation, image formation and interpretation, x-ray microanalysis, sample preparation, artifacts, and related techniques. Laboratory work includes operation of the electron microscope, x-ray microanalysis, and the preparation of biological and inorganic specimens for scanning and transmission electron microscopy. Seminar, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (This course is offered as BIOL 741, CHEM 741, and ERTH 741. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Graduate or senior standing and permission of the instructor.

name: Special Topics in Chemistry
oneLiner: Advanced and current study in various chemistry and biochemistry specialties.
description: Advanced and current study in various chemistry and biochemistry specialties. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate-level standing in Chemistry or permission of the instructor.

name: Exploratory Data Science for Scientists
oneLiner: Introduction to the fundamentals of data science through its applications in biology…
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of data science through its applications in biology and chemistry research. Exploration of data preparation, analysis, and reporting using real-world scientific datasets. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. (This course is offered as BIOL 806 and CHEM 806. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing; or upper-division standing with permission of the instructor; a college-level computer science course.

name: Coding Community for Data Science Components of Independent Research Projects
oneLiner: Applications of data science principles to independent research for a master's thesis.
description: Applications of data science principles to independent research for a master's thesis. May be repeated for a total of 3 units. (This course is offered as CHEM 807 and BIOL 807. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing; BIOL 806/CHEM 806 or equivalent (concurrent enrollment recommended); or permission of the instructor.

name: Professional Prospects for Quantitative Biologists, Data Scientists, and Bioinformaticians
oneLiner: Connect with data scientists from Bay Area industries, universities, and government…
description: Connect with data scientists from Bay Area industries, universities, and government agencies. Data scientists will be invited to campus to discuss current trends in the industry, specific positions and roles achievable for students post-graduation, CV composition, job interview skills, and professional experiences in a broad set of workplaces. Practice professional communication skills and experience post-graduate workplace culture. (CR/NC grading only) (This course is offered as BIOL 808 and CHEM 808. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: BIOL 806*/CHEM 806*.

name: Mass Spectrometry - Principles and Practice
oneLiner: Fundamental principles and modern practice of mass spectrometry, instrumentation (mass…
description: Fundamental principles and modern practice of mass spectrometry, instrumentation (mass analyzers, ionization modes, sample introduction systems) and applications (qualitative and quantitative analysis, environmental and biomedical applications). (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing in Chemistry or permission of the instructor.

name: Organic Synthesis
oneLiner: Problems relating to current organic synthetic methods.
description: Problems relating to current organic synthetic methods. Synthesis and reactions of the major classes of mono- and polyfunctional compounds.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing in Chemistry or permission of the instructor.

name: Organic Spectroscopic Methods
oneLiner: Relations between molecular structure and spectroscopic behavior.
description: Relations between molecular structure and spectroscopic behavior. Mass spectrometry, infrared, electronic, and magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
prereqNotes: Graduate Chemistry students; CHEM 301 or CHEM 353; or permission of the instructor.

name: Enzymology
oneLiner: The relationships between enzyme structure and catalytic activity, including enzyme…
description: The relationships between enzyme structure and catalytic activity, including enzyme kinetics and mechanisms.
prereqNotes: Graduate Chemistry students; CHEM 341, CHEM 301 or CHEM 353; or consent of the instructor.

name: Bioorganic and Medicinal Chemistry
oneLiner: Molecular recognition, enzymatic reaction mechanisms, catalytic antibodies/polymers…
description: Molecular recognition, enzymatic reaction mechanisms, catalytic antibodies/polymers, enzymes in organic synthesis, pharmacodynamics, and drug action, drug design for pharmacokinetic problems.
prereqNotes: Graduate Chemistry students or consent of the instructor.

name: Biochemical Spectroscopy
oneLiner: Quantum chemistry elements.
description: Quantum chemistry elements. Principles, techniques, and biochemical applications of spectroscopy.
prereqNotes: Graduate chemistry students; passing ACS diagnostic examination in quantum chemistry; a biochemistry course; or consent of the instructor.

name: Computational Methods in Chemistry
oneLiner: Introduction to quantum chemical and classical mechanical methods for the computation…
description: Introduction to quantum chemical and classical mechanical methods for the computation of molecular structure, molecular spectroscopy, liquid state transport properties, and molecular reactivity for small and large molecules, including solids and interactions at surfaces. Hands-on use of four software packages: Gaussian 09, AMBER molecular dynamics, LAMMPS dynamics for mesoscopic systems, and BEST for molecular hydrodynamics. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing; one year of undergraduate physical chemistry.

name: Research Methods I
oneLiner: Development of background, specific research aims, methods, and outcomes.
description: Development of background, specific research aims, methods, and outcomes. Includes literature review, writing assignments, and oral presentations. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Research Methods II
oneLiner: Exploration of current areas and methods of chemical research.
description: Exploration of current areas and methods of chemical research. Scientific writing and presentations emphasizing students' independent research projects. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing; CHEM 879; or permission of the instructor.

name: Instructional Methods in Teaching Chemistry and Biochemistry
oneLiner: Introduction to effective teaching strategies in science classrooms grounded in current…
description: Introduction to effective teaching strategies in science classrooms grounded in current science education theory and research. May not be repeated for credit. (Plus-minus ABC/NC; CR/NC not allowed) (CHEM 885/CHEM 685 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing.

name: Research Project
oneLiner: Supervised independent and original laboratory investigation.
description: Supervised independent and original laboratory investigation. Guidelines are available through the Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Research
oneLiner: Independent and original experimental, computational, or theoretical research under…
description: Independent and original experimental, computational, or theoretical research under faculty supervision. May be repeated for a total of 12 units. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing and permission of the instructor.

name: Master's Thesis
oneLiner: (CR/NC grading only)
description: (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) for the Master of Science in Chemistry and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: First Semester Chinese
oneLiner: Understanding, speaking, reading, and writing modern Mandarin Chinese at the elementary…
description: Understanding, speaking, reading, and writing modern Mandarin Chinese at the elementary level. Emphasis on the spoken language. Laboratory attendance required.

name: Second Semester Chinese
oneLiner: Further study of elementary Mandarin Chinese.
description: Further study of elementary Mandarin Chinese. Laboratory attendance required.
prereqNotes: CHIN 101 or permission of the instructor.

name: Third Semester Chinese
oneLiner: Understanding, speaking, reading, and writing modern Mandarin Chinese at the…
description: Understanding, speaking, reading, and writing modern Mandarin Chinese at the low-intermediate level. Laboratory attendance required.
prereqNotes: CHIN 102 or permission of the instructor.

name: Flagship Preparation I
oneLiner: Augments CHIN 101 and CHIN 102 for preparation for the Chinese Flagship Program.
description: Augments CHIN 101 and CHIN 102 for preparation for the Chinese Flagship Program. Focus on presentational speaking skills and writing skills; practice with traditional and simplified Chinese characters, composition, and use of electronic media for Chinese.
prereqNotes: Concurrent enrollment in CHIN 101 or CHIN 102 or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese Language and Society
oneLiner: Examination of the role of Chinese language in various aspects of social life, such as…
description: Examination of the role of Chinese language in various aspects of social life, such as identity, gender relations, class, kinship, social status, and hierarchies. Topics also include the regional variations of the Chinese language and its relations to culture, education, politics, and technology.

name: Writing China & the West: Written Communication and Cross-Cultural Encounters in Word and Image
oneLiner: Introduction to effective writing, emphasizing clarity, coherence, and the development…
description: Introduction to effective writing, emphasizing clarity, coherence, and the development of a personal voice. Through close reading and analytical writing, explore how China and the West have imagined, represented, and misunderstood each other from the 10th century to the present. Analyze how cultural encounters shape identity, power, and belonging through engaging with travelogues, poetry, letters, paintings, and migration narratives.

name: The Classic Chinese Novel in Contemporary Pop Culture
oneLiner: Explore the legacy of China's four great classic novels in contemporary Chinese popular…
description: Explore the legacy of China's four great classic novels in contemporary Chinese popular culture. Analysis of original works and their adaptation in TV shows and cinema, fiction, computer games, and theme parks. (This course is offered as CHIN 271 and HUM 271. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: Flagship Preparation II
oneLiner: Augments CHIN 102 and CHIN 103 for preparation for the Chinese Flagship Program.
description: Augments CHIN 102 and CHIN 103 for preparation for the Chinese Flagship Program. Focus on writing; practice with traditional and simplified Chinese characters, composition, and use of electronic media for Chinese.
prereqNotes: Concurrent enrollment in CHIN 102 or CHIN 103 or permission of the instructor.

name: Intermediate Chinese
oneLiner: Balanced focus on spoken and written Mandarin Chinese.
description: Balanced focus on spoken and written Mandarin Chinese. Developing students' oral fluency, expanding vocabulary, and correcting pronunciation. Improving skills using basic texts written in Chinese characters and writing sentences in characters. Laboratory attendance required.
prereqNotes: CHIN 103 or permission of the instructor.

name: Conversation and Reading
oneLiner: Developing proficiency in spoken Mandarin and written Chinese.
description: Developing proficiency in spoken Mandarin and written Chinese. Review of basic sentence patterns, vocabulary expansion, and acquisition of Chinese characters.
prereqNotes: CHIN 303 or Chinese Literature and Linguistics majors or minors or Chinese ITEP majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Speech and Writing
oneLiner: Developing proficiency in spoken Mandarin and written Chinese.
description: Developing proficiency in spoken Mandarin and written Chinese. Vocabulary expansion, acquisition, and retention of Chinese characters; speaking and writing skills in interactive context.
prereqNotes: CHIN 311 or consent of the instructor.

name: Flagship Preparation III: Academic Prose
oneLiner: Augments CHIN 103 and 303 for preparation for the Chinese Flagship Program.
description: Augments CHIN 103 and 303 for preparation for the Chinese Flagship Program. Focus on presentational speaking skills and writing skills. Training uses materials from the humanities, social sciences, and professional disciplines.
prereqNotes: Concurrent enrollment in CHIN 103 or CHIN 303 or permission of the instructor.

name: Advanced Chinese
oneLiner: Developing Chinese proficiency at advanced level: vocabulary expansion, acquisition…
description: Developing Chinese proficiency at advanced level: vocabulary expansion, acquisition, and retention of Chinese characters in both full and simplified forms; communicative competence in four skills (listening, speaking, reading, and writing).
prereqNotes: CHIN 312 or Chinese Literature and Linguistics majors or minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Building Chinese Media Literacy
oneLiner: Vocabulary, structures, styles, and topics of contemporary Chinese media.
description: Vocabulary, structures, styles, and topics of contemporary Chinese media. Newspapers, radio and television broadcasts, websites, blogs, and social media of Greater China. Intensive focus on reading and listening, augmented by writing and presentation assignments. (This course is offered as CHIN 410 and JOUR 410, and is taught in Chinese. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: CHIN 401 or consent of the instructor.

name: Media Chinese
oneLiner: Exploration of the role of media in the Chinese-speaking world.
description: Exploration of the role of media in the Chinese-speaking world. Focus is on radio and television; news reports and articles, editorials, interviews, and advertisements. Knowledge of Chinese is not required. (This course is offered as CHIN 411, I R 413, and JOUR 411. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese for Healthcare Professions
oneLiner: Instruction in translation and interpreting between patients and healthcare…
description: Instruction in translation and interpreting between patients and healthcare professionals in a healthcare setting. Introduction to basic medical terminology and their equivalents in Chinese and the analysis and transfer of message meanings necessary to render effective translations and interpretations. Exploration of the knowledge of discourse settings and structures for efficient, effective interpreting and translation practice. Analysis of healthcare disparities affecting Chinese-speaking populations and how to advocate for equitable healthcare practices.
prereqNotes: CHIN 312 or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Flagship Chinese I
oneLiner: Focus on advanced training in all four skills and three modes of language.
description: Focus on advanced training in all four skills and three modes of language. Group study of advanced academic prose; preparation of formal presentations; composition of academic essays.
prereqNotes: Advanced Chinese skills and Flagship student status or permission of the instructor and the Flagship Director.

name: Flagship Chinese II: Domain Training
oneLiner: Focus on advanced training in all four skills and three modes of language.
description: Focus on advanced training in all four skills and three modes of language. Combination of group study of advanced academic prose and individual study of language pertaining to field domains, to prepare students for the Flagship Capstone Year.
prereqNotes: CHIN 475 or equivalent and Flagship student status or permission of the instructor and the Flagship Director. Flagship students may enroll in CHIN 476 before they have completed CHIN 475 upon advisement.

name: Introduction to Classical Chinese
oneLiner: Stylistic and structural characteristics of classical Chinese; problems of…
description: Stylistic and structural characteristics of classical Chinese; problems of interpretation; introduction to literary genres in cultural context.
prereqNotes: CHIN 312 (may be taken concurrently) or Chinese Literature and Linguistics majors or minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Readings in Literary Chinese
oneLiner: Close readings of classical Chinese texts drawn from philosophical, historical, and…
description: Close readings of classical Chinese texts drawn from philosophical, historical, and literary sources, such as the Sishu (the Four Books), the Wujing (Five Confucian Classics), and classical Chinese poetry from the Han to the Tang. Classical Chinese grammar is studied using a hands-on approach; reading of text in original, analyze linguistic features, and socio-historical and literary context.
prereqNotes: CHIN 312 (may be taken concurrently) or Chinese Literature and Linguistics majors or minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese Philosophy and Religion
oneLiner: Major philosophical and religious traditions of China.
description: Major philosophical and religious traditions of China. Topics include the I Ching, Confucianism, Taoism, and Chinese Buddhism. (This course is offered as PHIL 511 and CHIN 511. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese Modern Fiction
oneLiner: Major authors from the May Fourth Movement and subsequent periods.
description: Major authors from the May Fourth Movement and subsequent periods.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Chinese Language and Modern China
oneLiner: Introduction to the linguistic structure, historical development, and present state of…
description: Introduction to the linguistic structure, historical development, and present state of Modern Standard Chinese; its relationship to the major Chinese dialect families; aspects of Chinese sociolinguistics and pragmatics.
prereqNotes: CHIN 311 or CHIN 312 (may be taken concurrently) or Chinese Literature and Linguistics majors or minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Topics in Modern Chinese Language and Literature
oneLiner: Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule.
description: Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary.
prereqNotes: CHIN 311 or CHIN 312 (may be taken concurrently) or Chinese Literature and Linguistics majors or minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Topics in Chinese Language, Literature, and Culture in English
oneLiner: Topic to be specified in the Class Schedule.
description: Topic to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary.
prereqNotes: GE Area E.

name: The Poetic Tradition - GWAR
oneLiner: Major Chinese poets from antiquity to late imperial times, discussed in cultural context.
description: Major Chinese poets from antiquity to late imperial times, discussed in cultural context. Taught in English. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2.

name: The Narrative Tradition
oneLiner: Chinese literary tradition including philosophical essays, historical writings…
description: Chinese literary tradition including philosophical essays, historical writings, fiction, and drama from 500 B.C. to novels of late 19th Century. [Taught in English] (CHIN 802/CHIN 602 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Revolutionary Tradition in Modern Chinese Literature - GWAR
oneLiner: Introduction to 20th-century Chinese literature and thought with particular focus on…
description: Introduction to 20th-century Chinese literature and thought with particular focus on politically motivated writers. Critical engagement with the most important intellectual trends and political movements from the last days of Imperial rule to the present. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GE Area 1A/A2; or permission of the instructor.

name: Negotiating Chineseness in the Late 20th and 21st Centuries - GWAR
oneLiner: Exploration of multiple negotiations of Chineseness through a wide range of texts from…
description: Exploration of multiple negotiations of Chineseness through a wide range of texts from the People's Republic, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and the Chinese Diaspora. Focus on literary, cinematic, and critical works produced between 1970 and present. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division Chinese majors; GE Area 1A/A2; or permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Written projects requiring critical analysis and interpretation of literary…
description: Written projects requiring critical analysis and interpretation of literary, linguistic, or pedagogical problems. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Permission of the department chair and instructor. Open only to undergraduate students who have demonstrated the ability to do independent work.

name: Projects in the Teaching of Chinese
oneLiner: Experience with proficiency-based methods for teaching Chinese.
description: Experience with proficiency-based methods for teaching Chinese. Supervising faculty member offers individual direction and group pedagogy sessions. Enrollment for 1-3 units (1 unit requires 2 hours tutoring and 1 hour preparation weekly). May be repeated for a total of 4 units maximum. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing; tutoring appointment in the Chinese Flagship Program.

name: The Narrative Tradition
oneLiner: Chinese literary tradition including philosophical essays, historical writings…
description: Chinese literary tradition including philosophical essays, historical writings, fiction, and drama from 500 B.C. to novels of late 19th Century. [Taught in English] (CHIN 802/CHIN 602 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: M.A. in Chinese students or permission of the instructor.

name: The Road To Modernity Part I: Chinese Literary Trends of the Late Imperial and Republican Periods
oneLiner: Examination of the most important literary trends and genres (fiction, poetry, drama…
description: Examination of the most important literary trends and genres (fiction, poetry, drama, reportage) that have shaped the development of modern Chinese literature from the 1850s until 1945. Will constitute part 1- of a 2-part survey of modern Chinese literature.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Modern Chinese Literature
oneLiner: Readings by major authors from the May Fourth Movement to the present, as well as…
description: Readings by major authors from the May Fourth Movement to the present, as well as selections from secondary scholarship.
prereqNotes: Admission to Chinese program or permission of the instructor.

name: Classical Chinese Literature
oneLiner: Classical philosophical, historical, and belletristic writings.
description: Classical philosophical, historical, and belletristic writings.
prereqNotes: Admission to Chinese program or permission of the instructor.

name: Applied Linguistics and Teaching Chinese
oneLiner: Investigation of practical issues pertinent to second language acquisition and pedagogy…
description: Investigation of practical issues pertinent to second language acquisition and pedagogy in Teaching Chinese as a Second Language.
prereqNotes: Admission to Chinese program or permission of the instructor.

name: Semantics and Morphology
oneLiner: Introduction to linguistic meaning and word formation in Chinese.
description: Introduction to linguistic meaning and word formation in Chinese. Chinese semantics, pragmatics, morphology in light of recent findings in cognitive science.
prereqNotes: Master of Arts in Chinese students or permission of the instructor.

name: Language Change and Dialect Variation
oneLiner: Introduction to mechanisms of language change and their application to Chinese…
description: Introduction to mechanisms of language change and their application to Chinese historical linguistics and modern dialect classification. Topics include sound change, lexical change, grammaticalization, linguistic reconstruction, language typology, and Chinese philology.
prereqNotes: Master of Arts in Chinese students or permission of the instructor.

name: Materials Development for Teaching Chinese
oneLiner: Strengthening skills in developing teaching materials and level-appropriate thematic…
description: Strengthening skills in developing teaching materials and level-appropriate thematic units, adopted for national foreign language standards and California state-approved curriculum framework. Language learning assessment and student projects. [Online Course]
prereqNotes: Admission to Chinese M.A. program or permission of the instructor.

name: Translation
oneLiner: Translation theory and its application to English and Chinese.
description: Translation theory and its application to English and Chinese. Topics include meaning, levels of equivalence, fidelity and authorship, metaphor and idiomatic language, domesticating and foreignizing strategies, transliteration and romanization, translation of specific genres, Chinese translation theory, and translation research.
prereqNotes: Admission to Chinese M.A. program or permission of the instructor.

name: Consecutive and Simultaneous Interpreting
oneLiner: Seminar focused on general English-Chinese and Chinese-English liaison, consecutive and…
description: Seminar focused on general English-Chinese and Chinese-English liaison, consecutive and simultaneous interpreting. Training in shadowing, note-taking, and effort management, leading to the build-up of skills in consecutive and simultaneous interpreting.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Culminating Experience Examination
oneLiner: Enrollment in 896EXAM required for students whose culminating experience consists of an…
description: Enrollment in 896EXAM required for students whose culminating experience consists of an examination only. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor, committee chair, and approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a member of the…
description: Study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a member of the departmental faculty. Open only to graduate students who have demonstrated the ability to do independent work. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Permission of the graduate major adviser and supervising faculty member. Enrollment by petition.

name: International Relations Through Cinema
oneLiner: Exploration of how key issues and topics in international relations are depicted in…
description: Exploration of how key issues and topics in international relations are depicted in international cinema. Introduction to basic concepts in international relations through a common and highly accessible medium, feature film. (This course is offered as I R 201 and CINE 101. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: Introduction to Contemporary Cinema
oneLiner: Survey of a wide range of topics on contemporary cinema - exploring an array of…
description: Survey of a wide range of topics on contemporary cinema - exploring an array of international and U.S. films, as well as alternative cinematic modes. Open to non-majors.

name: Asian Popular Culture in Global Perspective
oneLiner: Introduction to Asian popular culture from comparative and international perspectives.
description: Introduction to Asian popular culture from comparative and international perspectives. Examine sources, drivers, and impact, focusing on historical, sectoral, and regional trends in the global influence of Asian culture. Cases include entertainment, media, and sports; Chinese, Japanese, and Korean popular culture; and implications for Asian, Western, and non-Western worlds. (This course is offered as I R 202 and CINE 103. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: The Ancient World in Film
oneLiner: Examination of how ancient Greek and Roman myth and history are represented in film…
description: Examination of how ancient Greek and Roman myth and history are represented in film, often as a way of looking critically at modern society and its values. (This course is offered as CLAS 280 and CINE 180. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2.

name: Introduction to Cinema Studies
oneLiner: Introduction to the expressive properties and codes of cinema.
description: Introduction to the expressive properties and codes of cinema. Exposure to diverse cinematic traditions. An emphasis is placed on developing fundamental critical methods and perspectives. A grade of C or better is required for Cinema majors and minors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

name: Introduction to Filmmaking
oneLiner: Introduction to modes of film production.
description: Introduction to modes of film production. Operation, function, and creative use of filmmaking tools common to development, pre-production, production, post-production, and distribution. Exploration of technical considerations, the language of filmmaking, and creating meaning in cinema. A grade of C or better is required for Cinema majors and minors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Concurrent enrollment in CINE 204*.

name: Introduction to Filmmaking Laboratory
oneLiner: Hands-on lab introduces filmmaking tools and techniques.
description: Hands-on lab introduces filmmaking tools and techniques. Development and execution of short group creative film projects. Activity. A grade of C or better is required for Cinema majors. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only).

name: Film History I
oneLiner: Introduction to the history of early cinema through WWII (1895-1945).
description: Introduction to the history of early cinema through WWII (1895-1945). Survey of diverse cinematic traditions, social/national inflections, and forms. A grade of C or better is required for Cinema majors and minors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

name: Film History II
oneLiner: Introduction to the history of post-WWII cinema (since 1945).
description: Introduction to the history of post-WWII cinema (since 1945). Survey of diverse cinematic traditions, social/national inflections, and forms. A grade of C or better is required for Cinema majors and minors. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

name: Writing About Cinema - GWAR
oneLiner: Advanced analysis and persuasive writing on films and cinematic form. (ABC/NC grading…
description: Advanced analysis and persuasive writing on films and cinematic form. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; Cinema majors and minors; GE Area 1A/A2; CINE 200*, CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Gender and Film
oneLiner: Critical examination of issues related to the representation of gender and sexuality in…
description: Critical examination of issues related to the representation of gender and sexuality in cinema. Intermediate-level course. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Film and the Holocaust
oneLiner: The use of film to document and dramatize the Holocaust.
description: The use of film to document and dramatize the Holocaust. Filmmakers who have sought to give expression to its human scale. Significant works which have helped define the issues. (This course is offered as CINE 305 and JS 405. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or consent of the instructor.

name: Chinese Documentary Film
oneLiner: Explore the cultural, social, and aesthetic context of Chinese documentary films.
description: Explore the cultural, social, and aesthetic context of Chinese documentary films. Intermediate-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: National/Regional Cinemas
oneLiner: A critical exploration of a given national or regional cinema, addressing the impact of…
description: A critical exploration of a given national or regional cinema, addressing the impact of cultural specificity on film production and consumption. Intermediate-level course. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 9 units when topics vary.
