prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Third Cinema
oneLiner: Survey of critical perspectives on the aesthetics, cultural underpinnings, and…
description: Survey of critical perspectives on the aesthetics, cultural underpinnings, and political/historical context of films produced within societies formerly called "The Third World." Intermediate-level course. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/o/x Cinema
oneLiner: Examine Latino/a/x history using Latino/a/x-themed and produced films.
description: Examine Latino/a/x history using Latino/a/x-themed and produced films. The power of stereotypes, global dissemination of film, and examples of the ways in which Latin American and U.S. Latina/o/x filmmakers respond to stereotypes by creating cinematic counter-discourses. (This course is offered as LTNS 409 and CINE 309. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Israeli Cinema
oneLiner: Survey of Israeli cinema with critical readings. (This course is offered as JS 408 and…
description: Survey of Israeli cinema with critical readings. (This course is offered as JS 408 and CINE 314. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Iranian Cinema
oneLiner: Examination of Iranian films in English as a lens to understand issues in the broader…
description: Examination of Iranian films in English as a lens to understand issues in the broader world. Exploration and discussion of the historical development of visual arts and cinema in Iranian societies as a form of self-expression and communicative practice. Major themes in contemporary Iranian cultures are examined through critical content, along with modes of humanistic and artistic inquiry, analysis, and interpretation. (This course is offered as PRSN 320 [formerly PRSN 550] and CINE 320. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Focus on Film Topics
oneLiner: Exploration of influential filmmakers, performers, or movements in cinema.
description: Exploration of influential filmmakers, performers, or movements in cinema. Intermediate-level course. Suitable for non-majors. Topics to be specified in Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 4 units in any combination of CINE 325, CINE 326, and CINE 650 and when topics vary. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or consent of the instructor.

name: Festivals, Archives, and Cinematic Movements of the San Francisco Bay Area
oneLiner: Exploration of the rich and diverse film culture of the S.F.
description: Exploration of the rich and diverse film culture of the S.F. Bay Area, including film societies, archives, and established festivals. Course may coordinate with current festival or archive film series. Intermediate-level course. Suitable for non-majors. May be repeated for a total of 4 units in any combination of CINE 325, CINE 326, and CINE 650 when topics vary. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropology and Film
oneLiner: Social and cultural anthropology through films, ethnographies, and popular writings of…
description: Social and cultural anthropology through films, ethnographies, and popular writings of anthropologists. (This course is offered as ANTH 327 and CINE 327. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Art of Directing
oneLiner: Examination of the work and methods of a diverse sampling of fiction film directors.
description: Examination of the work and methods of a diverse sampling of fiction film directors. Exploration of the creative roles and administrative techniques of the film director with a focus on various approaches to authorship, cinematic style, and working with talent.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 202*, CINE 204* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Hollywood Representation of Race and Ethnicity
oneLiner: Examine the representation of race and ethnicity in U.S.
description: Examine the representation of race and ethnicity in U.S. Cinema. Employs critical and cultural theory to uncover the social significance of race as an ideological formation intertwined with the art and industry of American film. Intermediate-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Representation and Narration of Sexuality in Hollywood Cinema
oneLiner: Examination of the representation and narration of sexuality in cinema with an emphasis…
description: Examination of the representation and narration of sexuality in cinema with an emphasis on Hollywood. Employs critical and cultural theory - including critical race, queer, and feminist theories - to unpack the social and political significance of sexuality in cinema. Intermediate-level course. (This course is offered as CINE 332 and SXS 332. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors and Human Sexuality Studies minors; CINE 200*, and CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Race and Independent Cinema
oneLiner: Explore independent feature and short narrative films by and about people of color in…
description: Explore independent feature and short narrative films by and about people of color in the United States to expand existing frameworks that evaluate these works primarily in relation to dominant culture and the dominant industry. Study how a diversity of filmmakers concerned with racial inequality use cinema to narrate and represent the lives and stories of people of color. Explore the racial politics of representation, preservation, distribution, exhibition, and criticism through close readings, comparative approaches, and historically contextualized analysis. (This course is offered as CINE 333 and RRS 333. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors and Race and Resistance Studies minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Art of Cinematography
oneLiner: Focus on the contributions of outstanding cinematographers to world film history.
description: Focus on the contributions of outstanding cinematographers to world film history. Examine the signature visual styles and techniques, as well as the influences of art movements and fine-arts photography, photojournalism, and technological innovation, on the creative use of cinematography. Intermediate-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Video Game Culture
oneLiner: Examine video game culture, focusing on the history of gaming, key industry trends…
description: Examine video game culture, focusing on the history of gaming, key industry trends, video game scholarship, and popular gaming discourse. Explore topics such as (but not limited to) the arcade boom, casual games, gaming conventions, serious games, machinima and mods, the rise of e-sports, video game adaptations, and representations of gaming in pop culture.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors with CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or Video Game Studies majors and minors with VGS 100*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Studies
oneLiner: Explores essential critical approaches for analyzing cinema.
description: Explores essential critical approaches for analyzing cinema. A grade of C or better is required for the Cinema major and minor. Intermediate-level course. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor. Concurrent enrollment in CINE 341*.

name: Critical Studies Discussion Group
oneLiner: Applied critical analysis through writing, media projects, discussion, and research…
description: Applied critical analysis through writing, media projects, discussion, and research about Cinema. A Grade of C or better is required for the Cinema major and minor. Intermediate-level course. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor. Concurrent enrollment in CINE 340*.

name: Documentary Film
oneLiner: Explore the history, aesthetics, voice, and social impact of documentary and…
description: Explore the history, aesthetics, voice, and social impact of documentary and non-fiction media. Intermediate-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Perspectives on Documentary Film - GWAR
oneLiner: Explore focused issues in documentary film with an emphasis on critical writing.
description: Explore focused issues in documentary film with an emphasis on critical writing. Intermediate-level course. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; GE Area 1A/A2*; CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Film Genre
oneLiner: Examine a specific film genre focusing on key historical and theoretical issues.
description: Examine a specific film genre focusing on key historical and theoretical issues. Intermediate-level course. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 9 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Auteur Cinema
oneLiner: Examination of directors, stars, studios, writers, producers, or others who may be the…
description: Examination of directors, stars, studios, writers, producers, or others who may be the creative force behind a given film. Intermediate-level course. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 9 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Signs of Aliens: Semiotics of Film and Popular Culture
oneLiner: Explore the sign of the alien, an element of popular culture that encompasses troubling…
description: Explore the sign of the alien, an element of popular culture that encompasses troubling ideologies such as xenophobia and racism. Through semiotics and cultural film studies, alienation is examined as an aesthetic expression and value system reflected in considerations of immigration, race, sexuality, and more. Intermediate-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: From Ghost Stories to Short Stories: Japanese Fiction in Comparative Contexts
oneLiner: Examine the formal transformations in Japanese prose fiction and other storytelling…
description: Examine the formal transformations in Japanese prose fiction and other storytelling media by comparing them with other traditions; focus on questions of tradition, influence, genre, and translations. (This course is offered as CWL 432, CINE 348, and HUM 532. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: The Art of Short Film - GWAR
oneLiner: Explore the short film as a distinctive form of expression with unique structural…
description: Explore the short film as a distinctive form of expression with unique structural, aesthetic, and rhetorical dimensions, with an emphasis on critical writing. Intermediate-level course. (Plus-minus ABC/NC)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; GE Area 1A/A2*; CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Animation
oneLiner: Overview of global animation history, including crucial developments and historical…
description: Overview of global animation history, including crucial developments and historical trends; key modes, techniques, and traditions; influential state-sponsored studios and institutions; and understudied animation traditions. Analysis of key industrial, aesthetic, and technological developments in animated media and various techniques, including traditional cel animation, 3D digital animation, stop motion, direct animation, and cutout and silhouette animation.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Visual Effects: From Méliès to Marvel
oneLiner: Overview of cinematic visual effects from 19th-century trick films to contemporary…
description: Overview of cinematic visual effects from 19th-century trick films to contemporary virtual productions. Examine the history, theory, and aesthetics of special effects, as well as the technologies behind seminal VFX films. Explore classic works of practical effects pioneers such as Georges Méliès and stop-motion animator Willis O'Brien, as well as the latest innovations by digital visual effects powerhouses such as ILM, Digital Domain, and Weta Digital. Discussions on contemporary trends and recent developments in the global VFX industry.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and Animation minors; CINE 200*; and either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Film and Society
oneLiner: Major social issues as found in cinematic media: race, class, gender, and sexuality.
description: Major social issues as found in cinematic media: race, class, gender, and sexuality. How feminism, ideology, political movements, and social and historical changes impact representations. Intermediate-level course. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Cinema Department Internship
oneLiner: Development of research, writing, and technical skills; training in production…
description: Development of research, writing, and technical skills; training in production practices and technical equipment. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division Cinema majors; permission of the instructor required. Apply at the Cinema Department office.

name: Sound Production for Cinema
oneLiner: The aesthetics of field and studio recording.
description: The aesthetics of field and studio recording. Practice in production recording, sound effects, dialog and voice miking, and foley production. Intermediate-level production course. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Exploring Sound Design for Cinema
oneLiner: Create sound-centered experimental projects that focus on the concept of time, space…
description: Create sound-centered experimental projects that focus on the concept of time, space, identity, culture, environment, and body. Understand the collaborative work process and environment of post-sound production. Examination of sound design for cinema, focusing on computer-based technologies of editing and mixing. Creative exploration of sound/story relationships. Intermediate-level production course. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors, Cinema minors, Video Game Studies minors, and Animation minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require the permission of the instructor.

name: Sound Editing and Mixing
oneLiner: Practice the art and technique of sound design, editing, and mixing for moving images…
description: Practice the art and technique of sound design, editing, and mixing for moving images including sound effects recording and creation. Use best practices for designing multilayered synced soundtracks for cinema and other moving image media. Intermediate-level production course. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors, Cinema minors, and Animation minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Production Design and Art Direction
oneLiner: Development of fundamental hands-on technical skills and aesthetic considerations in…
description: Development of fundamental hands-on technical skills and aesthetic considerations in set design and art direction for film, video, and media production. Incorporates script breakdown and analysis, budgeting, creation of design plans, and stagecraft techniques. Culminates in the presentation of a set design or production design conceptualization. Intermediate-level production course. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Projects in Film Editing
oneLiner: Techniques and aesthetics of film editing through hands-on practice.
description: Techniques and aesthetics of film editing through hands-on practice. Intermediate-level production course. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of instructor.

name: Performing for the Screen
oneLiner: Intermediate-level workshop to practice the rehearsal process and acting for the camera…
description: Intermediate-level workshop to practice the rehearsal process and acting for the camera in conjunction with directing courses and film productions. Instruction and critique for doing auditions, preparing scene work, and acting on-set. Laboratory. May be repeated for a total of 3 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to sophomore standing or above or permission of the instructor.

name: Directing Actors
oneLiner: The creative role of the director with a focus on rehearsing and directing actors for…
description: The creative role of the director with a focus on rehearsing and directing actors for character-driven work. Intermediate-level production course. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: 16mm Cinematography
oneLiner: Exploration of the role of Director of Photography.
description: Exploration of the role of Director of Photography. Practice in camera department responsibilities and crew structure. Study of visual storytelling through technical and aesthetic studio-based projects with 16mm cameras and lighting equipment. Intermediate-level cinematography course. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level production courses per semester. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Digital Cinematography
oneLiner: Focus on image workflow.
description: Focus on image workflow. Practice in image manipulation, including camera settings, shooting techniques for visual effects, and post-production color grading. Explore the craft and visual style of digital capture and display through predominantly location-based technical projects. Intermediate-level cinematography course. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Explorations in XR: Developing Immersive Experiences Through VR, AR, MR, and Beyond
oneLiner: Extended Reality (XR) includes a range of innovative immersive technologies such as…
description: Extended Reality (XR) includes a range of innovative immersive technologies such as Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and Mixed Reality (MR). Explore the potential of XR with a variety of hands-on projects using sound design, virtual production, performance capture, world-building aesthetics, haptics, and interactivity. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema, Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts, Music, Design, Theatre, and Dance majors; Cinema and Animation minors; Video Game Studies minors who have completed CWL 180; or permission of the instructor.

name: Animation and Video Game Pre-Production
oneLiner: Visual planning for animation and video games including story development, character…
description: Visual planning for animation and video games including story development, character design, environment layout, and storyboarding. May be repeated for up to 9 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Drawing for Animation
oneLiner: Explore drawing techniques for animation including gesture and movement, kinetic…
description: Explore drawing techniques for animation including gesture and movement, kinetic volume, and abstraction of motion. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Animation I
oneLiner: Aesthetics, dynamics of movement, and techniques of animation.
description: Aesthetics, dynamics of movement, and techniques of animation. Projects in varied media and methods. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Online portfolio review required. Deadline: April 20th. Enrollment by permission of the instructor only.

name: Animation II
oneLiner: Creating animation to synchronize with various soundtrack designs.
description: Creating animation to synchronize with various soundtrack designs. Learn character animation techniques, effects design, story development, and basic editing. May be repeated for up to 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Animation minors or CINE 444* or permission of the instructor.

name: Stop-Motion Animation
oneLiner: Production of stop-motion and mixed-media animation.
description: Production of stop-motion and mixed-media animation. Practice using traditional and digital animation techniques for creative storytelling. May be repeated for up to 9 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: 2D Visual Effects
oneLiner: Hands-on practice with 2D digital animation and basic visual effects techniques.
description: Hands-on practice with 2D digital animation and basic visual effects techniques. Creative projects explore how digital animation techniques can impact narrative, experimental and documentary storytelling styles. Basic editing skills helpful. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing.

name: Fundamentals of Screenwriting
oneLiner: Introduction to the fundamental principles of screenwriting and historical context for…
description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of screenwriting and historical context for the development of dramatic writing. Introductory-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors and upper-division Theater Arts majors; or permission of the instructor.

name: Screenwriting: Focus on Genre
oneLiner: In-depth understanding and practice of the various conventions and tropes inherent in…
description: In-depth understanding and practice of the various conventions and tropes inherent in writing within specific film genres. Learn skills and strategies to implement this knowledge through exercises, analysis, and the writing of genre scripts. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary. (Plus-minus letter grade/RP grading only).
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, CINE 212*, or equivalents with grades of C or better; CINE 450*; or permission of instructor.

name: Writing Short Films
oneLiner: Screenwriting strategies for the short film in fictional and experimental forms.
description: Screenwriting strategies for the short film in fictional and experimental forms. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary. Intermediate-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200, CINE 202, CINE 204, CINE 211, and CINE 212 or equivalents with grades of C or better; CINE 450* or equivalent; or permission of instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Feature Screenwriting I
oneLiner: Focus on the practice of long-form film writing, emphasizing story and plot dynamics…
description: Focus on the practice of long-form film writing, emphasizing story and plot dynamics, characterization, narration, dialogue, script forms, and alternatives. Analysis of current motion picture scripts. Intermediate-level course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200, CINE 202, CINE 204, CINE 211, and CINE 212 or equivalents with grades of C or better; CINE 450* or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Writing for Documentary and Nonfiction
oneLiner: Writing strategies for development and scripting of documentary film projects.
description: Writing strategies for development and scripting of documentary film projects. Practice in the research process for a documentary concept. Development of techniques for writing treatments and creating visual plans. Exploration of methods of incorporating interviews and other nonfiction devices. Intermediate writing course.
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Independent Filmmaking Practice
oneLiner: Collaborative work as a writer, director, and editor working on short film projects…
description: Collaborative work as a writer, director, and editor working on short film projects with an emphasis on creating independent films in a community setting. Intermediate-level production course. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Documentary Filmmaking Workshop
oneLiner: Exploration of a variety of non-fiction filmmaking techniques and practices.
description: Exploration of a variety of non-fiction filmmaking techniques and practices. Emphasis on socially conscious documentaries. Intermediate-level course. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require the permission of the instructor.

name: Workshop in Fiction Filmmaking
oneLiner: Collaborative work on short fiction film projects with an emphasis on practicing the…
description: Collaborative work on short fiction film projects with an emphasis on practicing the various crew roles in pre-production and production. Intermediate-level production course. Activity. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to junior Cinema majors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Experimental Filmmaking
oneLiner: Experimental film aesthetics, techniques, and practices.
description: Experimental film aesthetics, techniques, and practices. Projects in varied media and methods. Intermediate-level production course. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Exploration in Interactive Cinema
oneLiner: Explore the conceptualization, programming, production, and presentation of cinema…
description: Explore the conceptualization, programming, production, and presentation of cinema using interactive digital tools and processes. Intermediate-level production course. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Material Cinema Workshop
oneLiner: Exploration of the meaning, histories, and strategic use of photographic material in…
description: Exploration of the meaning, histories, and strategic use of photographic material in cinema. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, and CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Queer Cinema Production
oneLiner: Examination and production of films related to the LGBTQ+ experience.
description: Examination and production of films related to the LGBTQ+ experience. Research, discussion, and critique of LGBTQ+ films of various genres, which will be used as the basis of conceptualizing and producing a new piece of work. The films will be screened publicly at the end of the term. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 202* and CINE 204*.

name: Experiments in Cinematic Form
oneLiner: Focus on experimental cinematic forms from radical experimental films to contemporary…
description: Focus on experimental cinematic forms from radical experimental films to contemporary explorations of forms outside the conventional cinematic structure. Particular emphasis on social and historical context, aesthetic modes, movements, and artists. Advanced-level course. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, CINE 204*, CINE 211*, CINE 212*, CINE 340, and CINE 341 or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Topics in Film History
oneLiner: Examine historical events as they are presented in the cinematic form or as they…
description: Examine historical events as they are presented in the cinematic form or as they influence the emergence of particular aesthetics, film cycles, or representational patterns. Explore the histories of cinemas as they evolved from different cultures and regions in the world. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Issues in Film Theory
oneLiner: Study of a selected method or issue in film theory.
description: Study of a selected method or issue in film theory. Advanced-level course. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units as topics vary. Topics include Documentary Form, Sound and Voice in Cinema, Classical Film Theory, Post-Modernism and Film, and Feminism and Film. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Race, Sex, and Identity Online
oneLiner: Analysis of the relationship between race, sexuality, and social identity online.
description: Analysis of the relationship between race, sexuality, and social identity online. Examine how capitalism and the politics of social resistance are manifested in online media. Advanced-level course.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Practices
oneLiner: Examine the relationship between critical theory and digital media practices.
description: Examine the relationship between critical theory and digital media practices. Familiarization with the emerging possibilities for "creative" or unconventionally presented critical work made possible by digital media: digital video, online, and other new technologies. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Digital Domains: History and Aesthetics of Computer Animation
oneLiner: Artistic and cultural significance of global contemporary computer animation in…
description: Artistic and cultural significance of global contemporary computer animation in animated films, live-action cinema, television, and video games. Analysis of historical, aesthetic, and technological developments of digital imagery, situating computer animation within larger debates in film and media studies. Topics may include film and media theory, industry and production studies, cultural studies, digital realism, acting in a digital environment, digital production/labor politics, digital media convergence, and animation viewership and fan communities. Critical analysis of computer-generated imagery.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Film Theory
oneLiner: Advanced seminar in cinematic and media theory.
description: Advanced seminar in cinematic and media theory.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Film Programming and Exhibitions Management
oneLiner: Overview and practice of curation and programming skills involved in the creation and…
description: Overview and practice of curation and programming skills involved in the creation and presentation of film and video programs. Prepares and manages the School of Cinema's Film Finals Program at semester end. Program planning; promotion and publicity; house management and public relations. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Exhibition, Distribution, and Festivals - Film Marketing
oneLiner: Overview of the strategies, options, and practicalities of film exhibition…
description: Overview of the strategies, options, and practicalities of film exhibition, distribution, and archives, within both an industry and independent filmmaking context. Emphasis on film curation, archives, and digital distribution modes and venues.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Directing Cinematic Style
oneLiner: Explore the creative role of directors of fiction films, including manipulation of…
description: Explore the creative role of directors of fiction films, including manipulation of space and time, dealing with continuity, script planning, blocking, visual style, sound design aesthetics, and/or authorship. Advanced production course. Activity. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception.

name: Advanced Lighting Techniques
oneLiner: Advanced cinematography course focused on lighting.
description: Advanced cinematography course focused on lighting. Exploration of the creative possibilities of soundstage and location lighting as part of a storytelling process. Lectures and practical demonstrations in technical considerations of light fixtures, electrical safety, and crew structure. Collaborative projects include lighting for fiction, visual effects, and emerging technologies. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Immersive Storytelling Through Virtual Reality
oneLiner: Focus on exploring the art and techniques of immersive storytelling through creative…
description: Focus on exploring the art and techniques of immersive storytelling through creative technology in virtual reality. Explore the imaginative and emotional storytelling techniques through a range of innovative immersive technologies focusing on Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR). Creation of an immersive and imaginative experience that connects with audiences through a variety of hands-on projects. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Advanced Projects in Fiction Filmmaking
oneLiner: Creation of a short fiction film.
description: Creation of a short fiction film. Advanced production course fosters the development, scriptwriting, pre-production, shooting, and editing of the film project. Senior capstone class. Activity. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors; CINE 424* or CINE 474* or CINE 612* or permission of the instructor. Students who have taken CINE 620 cannot take CINE 618 for credit.

name: Advanced Fiction Filmmaking I
oneLiner: Advanced production course fosters the development, scriptwriting, pre-production, and…
description: Advanced production course fosters the development, scriptwriting, pre-production, and shooting of a short senior thesis fiction film. First of two-semester sequence, followed by CINE 622. Serves as a culminating experience for fiction-oriented students. Activity. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors; portfolio application required; two or more of the following courses strongly recommended: CINE 350GW, CINE 424, CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 470, CINE 474, or CINE 612; permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. May not be taken concurrently with CINE 627*.

name: Advanced Fiction Filmmaking II
oneLiner: Post-production phase (editing, sound design, grading, mixing) of senior thesis fiction…
description: Post-production phase (editing, sound design, grading, mixing) of senior thesis fiction film. Activity. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors; CINE 620*; portfolio required; permission of the instructor.

name: Exploration in Cinema as an Online Medium
oneLiner: Advanced production course that explores the conceptualization, programming…
description: Advanced production course that explores the conceptualization, programming, production, and presentation of cinema on the Internet, using digital tools and processes. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Advanced Pre-Production Lab
oneLiner: Development of creative and technical aspects of fiction capstone film.
description: Development of creative and technical aspects of fiction capstone film. Use of filmmaking equipment and materials. Laboratory. (Plus-minus letter grade)
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors; concurrent enrollment in CINE 620*.

name: Advanced Post-Production Lab
oneLiner: Focused workshopping of editing and post sound work for fiction capstone film.
description: Focused workshopping of editing and post sound work for fiction capstone film. Laboratory. (Plus-minus letter grade)
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors; CINE 620*; concurrent enrollment in CINE 622*.

name: Explorations in Documentary Production
oneLiner: Examination and production of a particular genre, form, or theme in documentary…
description: Examination and production of a particular genre, form, or theme in documentary, resulting in the creation of short, non-fiction films. Based on a variable topic, students research and critique documentaries and use their findings as the basis of conceptualizing and producing their work. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Producing and Financing Films I
oneLiner: The economics of production including budgeting, breakdowns, financing and contracts…
description: The economics of production including budgeting, breakdowns, financing and contracts, distribution and exhibition, censorship, copyright, libel and slander, and laws of privacy. Hands-on producing of a senior thesis film project. The first part of a two-semester sequence followed by CINE 628. The culminating experience for producing-oriented students. Advanced Production Course. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Producing and Financing Films II
oneLiner: Examine the economics of post-production, marketing, distribution, and exhibition of…
description: Examine the economics of post-production, marketing, distribution, and exhibition of independent films. Explores the role of the producer during the post-production stage of independent filmmaking. Hands-on experience with senior thesis film. Part two of a two-semester sequence, following CINE 627. Advanced production course. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Workshop in Experimental Documentary
oneLiner: Advanced production course exploring experimental film practices in nonfiction.
description: Advanced production course exploring experimental film practices in nonfiction. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Media Archaeology in Cinema
oneLiner: Explore the meaning, histories, strategies, and techniques of the creative re-use of…
description: Explore the meaning, histories, strategies, and techniques of the creative re-use of media in cinema. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, and either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: International Documentary Workshop
oneLiner: A cross-cultural student program with the collaboration of film, cultural, or academic…
description: A cross-cultural student program with the collaboration of film, cultural, or academic programs or established community organizations in other countries. Students will broaden their cultural vision and develop their cinematic techniques in a global context. Documentary production experience course. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 3 units. May be repeated for a total of 12 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing and permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require both the permission of the instructor and approval by the Director of the School of Cinema.

name: Anthropological Filmmaking I
oneLiner: Introduction to ethnographic digital video production, including methods of…
description: Introduction to ethnographic digital video production, including methods of ethnographic fieldwork, the creation of field notes and research design. The basics of digital video planning, production, and editing. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as ANTH 595 and CINE 635. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Anthropology and Cinema majors, minors or ethnography certificate students; ANTH 120 and ANTH 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Anthropological Filmmaking II
oneLiner: Advanced filmmaking-based applied anthropological fieldwork, collaboration, and digital…
description: Advanced filmmaking-based applied anthropological fieldwork, collaboration, and digital post-production techniques. Students complete a video for which they conducted research during the previous semester. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as ANTH 596 and CINE 636. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Anthropology and Cinema majors, minors, and ethnography certificate Students; ANTH 595* or CINE 635*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Filmmaking in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
oneLiner: Advanced production course focused on the art and techniques of integrating artificial…
description: Advanced production course focused on the art and techniques of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into filmmaking practices. Practice creating AI-generated media culminating in a short film project. Explore the ever-evolving landscape of AI technology. Consideration of ethics in using AI tools for creative work. Senior capstone.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Advanced Documentary Production
oneLiner: Advanced production course that fosters the development, pre-production, production…
description: Advanced production course that fosters the development, pre-production, production, and post-production of a senior thesis nonfiction filmmaking project. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Episodic Screenwriting
oneLiner: Advanced screenwriting that explores extended narrative series storytelling structure…
description: Advanced screenwriting that explores extended narrative series storytelling structure and format. Analyze models of long-form narrative, and hone screenwriting skills through concept development, treatment preparation, and writing of a pilot for a webcast or episodic series. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Feature Screenwriting II
oneLiner: Advanced writing workshop focused on conceptualizing and writing long-form screenplays.
description: Advanced writing workshop focused on conceptualizing and writing long-form screenplays.
prereqNotes: CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212* or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Screenplay Revising
oneLiner: Restructure and revise a screenplay written in a previous class at the 400- or…
description: Restructure and revise a screenplay written in a previous class at the 400- or 600-level (after taking and passing CINE 450). Enhance story craft, acquire strategies for rewriting, and refining the clarity of script premise, characters, etc. Production of a polished work that can be submitted to competitions and serve as a writing portfolio upon graduation. Advanced writing course. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; CINE 450* and one additional screenwriting course at the 400 or 600 level; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception.

name: Filmmaking Master Class
oneLiner: An advanced workshop exploring and conceptualizing a select dimension within the craft…
description: An advanced workshop exploring and conceptualizing a select dimension within the craft of filmmaking (pre-production, production, or post-production) as a professional endeavor. Stresses the collaboration of filmmaking. May feature guest filmmakers and opportunities for students to receive critique and feedback on current work. May be repeated for a total of 4 units in any combination of CINE 325, CINE 326, and CINE 650 as topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors and permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception. Exceptions to this limit require the permission of the instructor.

name: Experimental Animation & Visual Effects
oneLiner: Hands-on practice with experimental animation techniques such as painting, clay and…
description: Hands-on practice with experimental animation techniques such as painting, clay and sand on glass; charcoal erasure; collage and mixed media stop motion. Learn to blend animation techniques with digital visual effects. Basic editing skills helpful and no animation or drawing experience required. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior or graduate standing or Animation minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Documentary Animation Methods
oneLiner: Explore and practice fantastical visual representation used in documentary storytelling.
description: Explore and practice fantastical visual representation used in documentary storytelling. Screen global stories and explainer videos. Learn archive research methods and how to make digital assets. Make short fact-based projects using digital tools like collage, puppets, track mattes, rotopaint, green screen and masking techniques. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Writing and Performing in Film and Theatre
oneLiner: Advanced course pairs screenwriting students (Cinema majors) with performing students…
description: Advanced course pairs screenwriting students (Cinema majors) with performing students (Theatre majors) to workshop original scripts through performance. (This course is offered as CINE 654 and TH A 558. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division students; CINE 450* or CINE 454* or CINE 456* or TH A 130* or equivalent; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level or two 600-level CINE courses per semester. CINE 450, CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception.

name: Screenwriting Workshop: Special Topics
oneLiner: Advanced screenwriting workshop that examines advanced projects in film writing.
description: Advanced screenwriting workshop that examines advanced projects in film writing. Special topics to coincide with instructor specialization and to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 6 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors and minors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better; CINE 450* or equivalent; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception.

name: Creating Story Worlds
oneLiner: Advanced writing course focuses on the development of creative intellectual properties…
description: Advanced writing course focuses on the development of creative intellectual properties for screenwriting, video games, and other media to produce deep, coherent, and flexible story worlds that can generate successful narratives across platforms.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Video Game Studies minors or senior Cinema majors and minors with CINE 200, CINE 202, CINE 204, CINE 211, CINE 212, CINE 340*, and CINE 341* or equivalents with grades of C or better; CINE 450* or equivalent; or permission of the instructor. Students are restricted to a maximum of two 400-level OR two 600-level courses per semester. CINE 454, CINE 458, or CINE 601 may be taken concurrently without a formal exception.

name: 3D Computer Animation
oneLiner: Develop technical and conceptual skills related to modeling, rendering, and animation…
description: Develop technical and conceptual skills related to modeling, rendering, and animation related to 3D movies and video games. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Animation III
oneLiner: Designing and animating short films.
description: Designing and animating short films. Learn research methods, dynamic storytelling, animation design principles, sound design techniques, and editing. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Animation minors or CINE 445* or permission of the instructor.

name: Animation IV
oneLiner: Workshop producing a thesis animated film.
description: Workshop producing a thesis animated film. Focus on research, animation, and sound design for creative storytelling. May be repeated for up to 9 units. Extra fee required. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Animation Minor students or students who have experience producing animated films with permission of the instructor.

name: Preparing Career Portfolios
oneLiner: Create a professional portfolio including: a resume, cover letter, demo reel, online…
description: Create a professional portfolio including: a resume, cover letter, demo reel, online portfolio and press kit. Learn job interview strategies and get professional advice on how to prepare for a career in animation and other media arts professions. Use social media to plan and prepare the end of semester screening of Animation Finals. Visiting industry professionals TBA. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. Extra fee required.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors or animation minors with permission of the instructor.

name: Projects in Teaching in Cinema
oneLiner: Teaching experiences in cinema in production, animation, studies and/or history…
description: Teaching experiences in cinema in production, animation, studies and/or history, through assigned instructional projects as classroom aides. (Students may earn a maximum of 6 units toward the baccalaureate degree for any course(s) numbered 685 regardless of discipline.)
prereqNotes: Cinema major; permission of the instructor.

name: Production Independent Study
oneLiner: Independent practice course allows students to propose and carry out individual projects.
description: Independent practice course allows students to propose and carry out individual projects. Students act in a major crew role such as screenwriter, director, editor, production designer, and producer. Does not include Cinema equipment checkout privileges. Open to students who have demonstrated the ability to work independently, have a cumulative grade point average of at least 3.0 (undergraduate), and approval of an instructor. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Cinema majors; CINE 340* and CINE 341*; a CINE GWAR course; GPA minimum of 3.0*; and permission of the instructor.

name: Internship
oneLiner: Experience in a special field. 100+ hours of field experience in cinema-related…
description: Experience in a special field. 100+ hours of field experience in cinema-related activities under the supervision of professionals. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior standing and permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Critical Studies
oneLiner: Independent studies for qualified students who wish to pursue research and scholarly…
description: Independent studies for qualified students who wish to pursue research and scholarly work under faculty supervision. May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: CINE 340 and CINE 341; or permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Selected projects in cinema studies or production.
description: Selected projects in cinema studies or production. Does not include Cinema equipment checkout privileges. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Cinema majors; CINE 200*, CINE 202*, and CINE 204*; either CINE 211* or CINE 212*; or equivalents with grades of C or better. Open to students who have demonstrated the ability to work independently, have a cumulative grade point average of at least 3.0 (undergraduate), and approval of an instructor.

name: Cinema Theory I
oneLiner: Orientation to graduate study.
description: Orientation to graduate study. Introduction to the professional standards and practices of cinema discipline. Survey of film, media and cultural theory from the late 1880s to the 1970s. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to MA Cinema Studies and MFA Cinema students.

name: Fiction Writing & Producing
oneLiner: Fundamentals of writing and producing for short fiction film: conceptualization, idea…
description: Fundamentals of writing and producing for short fiction film: conceptualization, idea development, screenwriting, and pre-production. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema students; concurrent enrollment in CINE 702.

name: Fiction Directing
oneLiner: Fundamentals of directing for short fiction film: casting, working with actors…
description: Fundamentals of directing for short fiction film: casting, working with actors, composing/staging for the camera, and shooting. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema students; concurrent enrollment in CINE 701.

name: Cinematography & Lighting
oneLiner: Fundamentals of cinematography and lighting.
description: Fundamentals of cinematography and lighting. Use of cameras, lenses, filters, light meters, and lights as well as screen direction, camera composition, and movement. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CINE 710]
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema students.

name: Documentary Writing & Producing
oneLiner: Fundamentals of writing and producing for short documentary film: conceptualization…
description: Fundamentals of writing and producing for short documentary film: conceptualization, research and development, treatment writing, and pre-production. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CINE 711]
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema students; concurrent enrollment in CINE 705.

name: Documentary Directing
oneLiner: Hands-on skills and guidance in documentary directing.
description: Hands-on skills and guidance in documentary directing. Direct and produce a documentary film as well as serve as crew on others. Technical production skills, critical analysis of non-fiction films, and documentary voice for creative expression. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CINE 740]
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema students; concurrent enrollment in CINE 704.

name: Cinema Theory II
oneLiner: Focus on contemporary film and media theory from the 1980s to the present. (Plus-minus…
description: Focus on contemporary film and media theory from the 1980s to the present. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CINE 726]
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema and MA Cinema students.

name: Advanced Directing
oneLiner: Advanced directing course that emphasizes individual ideas, how to put them into moving…
description: Advanced directing course that emphasizes individual ideas, how to put them into moving images/sound/text and how/why these inform evolving creative work. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CINE 761]
prereqNotes: Restricted to 2nd Year MFA Cinema students.

name: Advanced Editing
oneLiner: Advance graduate course in film editing.
description: Advance graduate course in film editing. Focus on intricate art and technical precision required to shape narrative, rhythm, and emotional impact in cinema. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CINE 712]
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema students.

name: Experimental Cinema
oneLiner: Aesthetics of avant-garde cinema and production of a short film using experimental…
description: Aesthetics of avant-garde cinema and production of a short film using experimental techniques. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly CINE 730]
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Visual Effects Workshop
oneLiner: Screen films that use a variety of visual effects.
description: Screen films that use a variety of visual effects. Practice using digital visual effects techniques like the ones used in media industries. Design effects for short projects to create impactful stories. Basic digital editing skills are helpful. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Graduate students or Cinema majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Cinematography Workshop
oneLiner: Exploration and achievement of the next level of aesthetics and techniques in…
description: Exploration and achievement of the next level of aesthetics and techniques in cinematography and lighting through a series of masterpiece examinations, hands-on production workshops, cinematography master classes, and industry practices. Projects in up-to-date digital technology. Activity. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students; CINE 710*; or consent of the instructor.

name: Critical Paradigms and the Cinematic
oneLiner: Approaches to the cinematic form through critical paradigms such as theories of the…
description: Approaches to the cinematic form through critical paradigms such as theories of the postmodern, post-colonial theory, structuralism/post-structuralism, systems theory, posthumanist theories. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Cinematic Documentary
oneLiner: Issues and concepts related to non-fiction cinematic forms such as documentary, or…
description: Issues and concepts related to non-fiction cinematic forms such as documentary, or ethnographic film. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate Cinema students.

name: Cinema Forms and Aesthetics
oneLiner: Theoretical and critical perspectives on dominant traditions and major modes of cinema…
description: Theoretical and critical perspectives on dominant traditions and major modes of cinema and/or media: classical, film narrative, documentary; avant-garde cinema and media. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Cinematic Styles, Forms and Movements
oneLiner: Examination of established cinematic styles, forms and movements such as how does style…
description: Examination of established cinematic styles, forms and movements such as how does style affect content? How do movements emerge? How do forms change over time? What relationship does a particular movement bear to narrative storytelling, documentary expression or avant-garde practice? May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema and Women and Gender Studies students.

name: Cinema Histories
oneLiner: Examination of cinematic traditions through historical methods with an emphasis…
description: Examination of cinematic traditions through historical methods with an emphasis historiographic research, modes of argumentation, principles of causality, narrative, and rhetoric. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Experimental Sound for Film
oneLiner: Introduction to a basic set of skills and techniques for creating experimental sound…
description: Introduction to a basic set of skills and techniques for creating experimental sound for film, video, documentary, and animation. Development of an in-depth understanding of contemporary methods of sound design, and incorporation of digital/new media in the compositional processes. Gain practical knowledge about computer-based programming systems for sound design and algorithmic approaches to music composition.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students or permission of the instructor.

name: Cinema and the City
oneLiner: Issues of the representation of the city in cinema, urban space has proven crucial to…
description: Issues of the representation of the city in cinema, urban space has proven crucial to genre films, as well as documentaries and the avant-garde. Utopic and dystopic elements of urban life receive close scrutiny. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Sexuality in the Cinema
oneLiner: Theories and representations of sexualities in cinema from various contexts…
description: Theories and representations of sexualities in cinema from various contexts, traditions, and histories such as queer and LGBTQ subjectivities, practices such as asexuality, BDSM and polyamory, and the study of cinema as an apparatus for the production of intimacy. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Cinema and Cultural Studies
oneLiner: Examination of the field of Cultural Studies and its influence on cinema and media…
description: Examination of the field of Cultural Studies and its influence on cinema and media studies. Students will read both founding theoretical texts and contemporaneous scholarship. Emphasis on intersecting structures of power, including class, nation, gender, race, and sexuality. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Critical Practices
oneLiner: Exploration of the relationship between critical theory/practice and digital media…
description: Exploration of the relationship between critical theory/practice and digital media practices; familiarization with the emerging possibilities for critical work made possible by digital media. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Production Workshop Intensive
oneLiner: Aesthetic and technical aspects of editing and post-production in diverse cinema genres.
description: Aesthetic and technical aspects of editing and post-production in diverse cinema genres. Current technical strategies for editing picture and sound applied to original film or video designed by students. May be repeated for up to 6 units. Activity. (CR/NC grading only) [Formerly CINE 763]
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students or permission of the instructor.

name: Feature Screenwriting
oneLiner: Advanced screenwriting leading to the completion of a feature-length original script.
description: Advanced screenwriting leading to the completion of a feature-length original script. The development of ideas, premise pitching, and disciplined writing practice. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students; introductory screenwriting; permission of the instructor.

name: Grant Writing, Development, and Distribution for Cinema
oneLiner: Learn the art of grant writing, develop a grant proposal for an independent film, and…
description: Learn the art of grant writing, develop a grant proposal for an independent film, and prepare a film for commercial distribution. Explore the different types of fundraising strategies and cultivate relationships with foundations, non-profits, and corporations to finance and distribute original work. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to MFA Cinema students.

name: Internship
oneLiner: Field experience with production entities and organizations within the cinema industry.
description: Field experience with production entities and organizations within the cinema industry. May be repeated once with the permission of the instructor.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Thesis Development
oneLiner: Focus on the development of individual vision and aesthetics and its realization…
description: Focus on the development of individual vision and aesthetics and its realization through research, theoretical orientation, script development, and production planning for the thesis film. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Cinema MFA students.

name: Animation Production Practice
oneLiner: Independent practice exploring animation and visual effects techniques.
description: Independent practice exploring animation and visual effects techniques. May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: Graduate students or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Critical Theory
oneLiner: Advanced study of critical theory specific to the cinematic form usually featuring a…
description: Advanced study of critical theory specific to the cinematic form usually featuring a single theorist such as Bazin, Deleuze, Metz, Mulvey, and Zizek, or a single theme such as Reception, Modernity, Performance, and Realism. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Cinema students.

name: Directed Experience in Film Education
oneLiner: Introduction to basic elements in course preparation, teaching, and assessment in the…
description: Introduction to basic elements in course preparation, teaching, and assessment in the field of cinema. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate Cinema students and permission of the instructor.

name: Creative Work Project
oneLiner: Advancement to Candidacy and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must…
description: Advancement to Candidacy and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: CINE 770, approval of thesis project proposal, permission of instructor, approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC), and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Research Projects in Cinema Studies
oneLiner: Methods of research for individual graduate projects in cinema studies.
description: Methods of research for individual graduate projects in cinema studies. Development of a problem of interest to the student. (Plus-minus letter grade, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to M.A. Cinema students; CINE 700; and permission of the instructor.

name: Master's Thesis
oneLiner: Advancement to Candidacy and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must…
description: Advancement to Candidacy and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor and department chair or graduate coordinator, approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) for Master of Arts in Cinema and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Supervised individual projects in various aspects of the motion picture field.
description: Supervised individual projects in various aspects of the motion picture field. Does not include Cinema equipment checkout privileges. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Permission of the supervising instructor and department chair or graduate coordinator.

name: Archaeology of the Ancient World
oneLiner: Archaeology of the ancient world.
description: Archaeology of the ancient world. Artistic and cultural achievements of Egypt, the Ancient Near East, Greece and Rome, and interaction of the art with society. (This course is offered as CLAR 250, ARTH 250, JS 250, and M S 250. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2.

name: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Greece
oneLiner: Survey of Greek material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the…
description: Survey of Greek material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the Bronze Age to the second century CE. (This course is offered as CLAR 420, ANTH 424, ARTH 401, and M S 420. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Rome
oneLiner: Survey of Roman material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the…
description: Survey of Roman material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the foundation of Rome to the reign of Justinian. (This course is offered as CLAR 425, ANTH 425, ARTH 402, and M S 425. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Video Games and the Archaeology of the Ancient Mediterranean
oneLiner: Explore the reciprocal relationship between video games and archaeological research on…
description: Explore the reciprocal relationship between video games and archaeological research on the ancient Mediterranean, from material culture, history, art, and architecture in games to the use of video games in primary archaeological research. (This course is offered as CLAR 440, HUM 461, and VGS 440. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2, 1B/A3, 1C/A1, and 2/B4 all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Egypt
oneLiner: Ancient Egyptian civilization from Pre-dynastic through Ptolemaic times: art…
description: Ancient Egyptian civilization from Pre-dynastic through Ptolemaic times: art, archaeology, literature, and religion with research use of Sutro Egyptian Collection. (This course is offered as CLAR 500, M S 500, and ARTH 407. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Ancient Egyptian Language and Literature
oneLiner: Introduction to signs, vocabulary, grammar, and syntax of Middle Egyptian language.
description: Introduction to signs, vocabulary, grammar, and syntax of Middle Egyptian language. Learn to read texts from funerary stelae, coffins, and short stories.
