description: Development of competencies around the theme of gender in the African past by working with a variety of texts and sources and the scholarship of leading researchers in this field.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Tales from Ancient India: Hinduism and Buddhism
oneLiner: Study of ancient Indian (Hindu and Buddhist) culture, religion, and literature.
description: Study of ancient Indian (Hindu and Buddhist) culture, religion, and literature. Examination of epics, plays, devotional, and love poetry from Sanskrit and other Indian languages. Examination of family, gender, and patriarchy, kingship and power, heroism, love, war, and ethics, and devotion. (This course is offered as HIST 370, HUM 582, and CLAS 582. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor. or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: India and the British Empire
oneLiner: History of civilization of the Indian subcontinent to the present.
description: History of civilization of the Indian subcontinent to the present. Addresses political, economic, social, ethnic, and linguistic factors that shaped regional development.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Contemporary India
oneLiner: Introduction to themes in the political culture of contemporary India.
description: Introduction to themes in the political culture of contemporary India. Examine the legacy of colonialism and nationalism; digital, film, literary, and popular cultures; the challenges of caste, ethnicity, and gender in a multicultural society; rising global India; Climate and Environmental policies; and foreign policy.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Bollywood and Beyond: Indian History Through Film
oneLiner: Examine Indian history since 1947 through Indian film.
description: Examine Indian history since 1947 through Indian film. Introduction to modern Indian culture and society. Explore films produced in each of the decades since 1947 to explore the changing political and social dynamics of India. The stories that are told through film capture everything from the dreams, desires, and fantasies of Indians to their complex political and social locations in an ever-changing society. (This course is offered as HIST 374 and HUM 586. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Southeast Asia
oneLiner: Transnational history of Southeast Asia from the first century CE to the present.
description: Transnational history of Southeast Asia from the first century CE to the present. Provides a broad understanding of the region's history by focusing on major themes such as social and political organization, cross-cultural interactions and influences, religion and society, colonialism, and national revolutions.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Islamic World I: 500-1500
oneLiner: Islamic civilization, culture, and history from 500 to 1500.
description: Islamic civilization, culture, and history from 500 to 1500.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Islamic World II: 1500 - Present
oneLiner: Islamic civilization, culture, and history from 1500 to the present.
description: Islamic civilization, culture, and history from 1500 to the present.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Iran and Afghanistan 1500 - Present
oneLiner: History of Iran from the rise of the Safavid Empire to the present.
description: History of Iran from the rise of the Safavid Empire to the present. Beginning with a historical background, the course moves on to examine the history of Iran in a period of colonialism, revolution, and the rise of Islam.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Modern Korea
oneLiner: Situate the current geopolitical landscape of Korea within the peninsula's broader…
description: Situate the current geopolitical landscape of Korea within the peninsula's broader historical context. Examine the major political, social, and economic shifts that shaped modern Korea, paying particular attention to the Japanese colonial era, the liberation period after WWII, the Korean War, the mid-twentieth century rapid industrialization, democratization and social movements in the south, and the nature of the state and society in the north. Treatment of Korea's historical past will create a nuanced framework to critically evaluate the contemporary moment and place the peninsula in today's changing global environment.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: The Russian Revolution
oneLiner: The crisis and collapse of Imperial Russia, traditions of the Russian revolutionaries…
description: The crisis and collapse of Imperial Russia, traditions of the Russian revolutionaries, and rise of the Soviet Union of Stalin.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: International History 1814-1918
oneLiner: Over the 19th century, the system of states faced challenges such as the turmoil from…
description: Over the 19th century, the system of states faced challenges such as the turmoil from the Napoleonic Wars, industrialization, global integration, the rise of nationalism, and the spread of empires. Explore the choices made by the individuals and countries involved and how they affected strategy, personalities, popular interests, and contingency. Primary actors are states, empires, nations, and those that would become such. Focused not on one particular national history, but considering the system as a whole. (This course is offered as HIST 395/I R 395. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Modern European Imperialism
oneLiner: Theories and ideologies of imperialism, experiences of colonial rule, and interaction…
description: Theories and ideologies of imperialism, experiences of colonial rule, and interaction within and between empires.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: A Cultural History of American Technology
oneLiner: Introduction to the history of American technology from the Colonial period to the 21st…
description: Introduction to the history of American technology from the Colonial period to the 21st century. Explore the impact of technological advancements on American culture and thought, and, inversely, the degree to which historical circumstances and events unique to America have affected technological innovations. This interplay between context and innovation highlights a central theme of this course that pragmatic applications and the commercial development of new technologies have been a defining characteristic of American history since its inception.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Maritime History
oneLiner: Investigate the ocean as an important site of historical change from 1500 to the…
description: Investigate the ocean as an important site of historical change from 1500 to the present, including the political, economic, cultural, and environmental factors. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: The Jewish Sixties: A Journey Through The Social Protest Movements of the 1960s
oneLiner: Explores the Jewish Sixties through the thematic lens of religion, history, and sociology.
description: Explores the Jewish Sixties through the thematic lens of religion, history, and sociology. Divides "the Sixties" into two historical epochs: 1954-1964 and 1965-1980. The first period examines consensus-based race relations with attention to the modern struggle for racial equality as well as leftist critics of Cold War America. The second period explores the radicalization of social reform efforts with careful attention to the rise of the New Left, Vietnam protests, and counterculture. (This course is offered as JS 548 and HIST 416. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Society and Politics in American History
oneLiner: Changing nature of political patterns from the American Revolution to the present.
description: Changing nature of political patterns from the American Revolution to the present. Focus on parties, elections, and policy-making at the national level including the ideological, social, and economic bases of politics.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: American Colonial History
oneLiner: History of Native American communities, borderlands, and European colonies to 1760s.
description: History of Native American communities, borderlands, and European colonies to 1760s. Primary topics include settler colonialism and the origins of slavery, including how both impacted debates about democracy and freedom. Explore the changing nature of the natural and built environment, capitalism, religion, and war with an emphasis on changing ideas about indigeneity, race, gender, sexuality, class, and ability/disability. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Food Fights: The Politics of American Jewish Consumption from 1654 to the Present
oneLiner: Exploration of the politics of religion, food, and eating among Jews in the US from the…
description: Exploration of the politics of religion, food, and eating among Jews in the US from the late 19th century to the present. Focus on American Jewish foodways including cultural, social, historical, political, and economic practices of food production and consumption that have sustained and demarcated Jewish communities. (This course is offered as JS 421 and HIST 421. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: The American Revolution
oneLiner: Causes of the American Revolution, the War for Independence, including social and…
description: Causes of the American Revolution, the War for Independence, including social and cultural change regarding gender, race, and class.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: History of the United States: Civil War and Reconstruction
oneLiner: Internal development and expansion of the American people and the rise of sectional…
description: Internal development and expansion of the American people and the rise of sectional conflict, culminating in the Civil War and Reconstruction era.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: U.S. History in the Gilded Age, 1877-1916
oneLiner: Explore the Gilded Age -- a period like no other in American history, marked by…
description: Explore the Gilded Age -- a period like no other in American history, marked by unprecedented wealth and inequality, robber barons and labor strikes, innovation and corruption. Examine America's rapid transformation into a modern industrialized nation and a global power, tracing especially the human social and cultural experiences in response to economic, political, legal, ideological, and environmental changes. Topics will include urban life, rural change, immigration, race relations, gender and sexuality, popular entertainment, work and leisure, reform, and nationalism.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division or graduate standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: History of the United States 1916-1945
oneLiner: U.S. history from 1916 to 1945 including politics of the New Era and New Deal…
description: U.S. history from 1916 to 1945 including politics of the New Era and New Deal, involvement in two world wars and its domestic impact, and changing social, economic, and intellectual patterns.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: U.S. History in the Civil Rights Era, 1945-1980
oneLiner: U.S. history from the end of World War Two to the election of Ronald Reagan, addressing…
description: U.S. history from the end of World War Two to the election of Ronald Reagan, addressing topics such as the Cold War and Vietnam War; the Red and Lavender Scares; struggles for racial justice, women's empowerment, reproductive freedom, and gay liberation; the New Left and student activism; the counterculture and the sexual revolution; popular culture during the television age; liberal reform and conservative backlash; the Great Society and Silent Majority; immigration reform and restriction; urban crises, suburban growth, and deindustrialization; Watergate and the Nixon era; and the New Right and Reagan Revolution.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: U.S. History: The Recent Past, 1980 to the Present
oneLiner: U.S. history from 1980 - present, focusing on political developments, social and…
description: U.S. history from 1980 - present, focusing on political developments, social and cultural change, and the defining social movements of the recent past. Emphasis on problems of race, class, gender, and sexuality. Examination of political conflict from Jimmy Carter and the post-Watergate crisis to Donald Trump and the conservative politics of backlash; economic and social transformations from the rise of Wal-Mart and mass incarceration to the Great Recession and the crisis of inequality; and social movements from the Nuclear Freeze, ActUp!, and the Moral Majority to Occupy Wall Street, the Tea Party, and Black Lives Matter.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Rising Powers
oneLiner: Exploration of the rise of Brazil, Russia, India, China, and others.
description: Exploration of the rise of Brazil, Russia, India, China, and others. The capacities for domestic power accumulation, national identities, military capabilities, Western and non-Western responses, and emerging global order. (This course is offered as I R 460 and HIST 430. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; I R 104; or permission of the instructor.

name: American Jews and Popular Culture
oneLiner: Examination of presentation and participation of Jews in American popular culture of…
description: Examination of presentation and participation of Jews in American popular culture of the 20th and 21st centuries. Focused on the representation of Jews and Judaism in film, television, and media. Representation of Jews and Judaism in literature, athletics, food, museums, and consumer culture also addressed. (This course is offered as JS 441, HIST 441, and HUM 441. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2.

name: American Jewish History
oneLiner: American Jewish History from 1654 to the present tracing the social, political…
description: American Jewish History from 1654 to the present tracing the social, political, religious, and economic history of Jews in colonial America and the United States. Topics include the influence of government, immigration, religion, anti-Semitism, regionalism, and acculturation. (This course is offered as JS 449 and HIST 449. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: History of California
oneLiner: California from its Indigenous origins to the 21st century.
description: California from its Indigenous origins to the 21st century. Topics include the diverse and complex cultures of California's Native peoples; European exploration and conquest; Mexican independence and Californio societies; war and statehood; migration and immigration; industry and labor; race, ethnicity, class, gender, and sexuality; cities and suburbs; political cultures and trends; student movements and social justice activism; the environment; popular culture; and the contours of the so-called "California Dream."
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Bay Area History and Society
oneLiner: Exploration of the Bay Area, specifically San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, and San…
description: Exploration of the Bay Area, specifically San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, and San Jose, from a socio-historical and global perspective. Exploration of various dimensions of the Bay Area's human and environmental composition and history, paying special attention to the built environment, immigration, globalization, race, and class.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: The United States and the World Before 1913
oneLiner: Examine American involvement in the world and international relations from the…
description: Examine American involvement in the world and international relations from the Revolutionary Period until the eve of World War I. Topics will include territorial expansion to the Pacific Ocean; American relations with European powers; U.S. involvement in Latin America, Asia, and Africa; cultural and economic diplomacy; and creating an overseas empire. Emphasis on unofficial cultural interactions and the role of non-state actors in international relations as well as more traditional high-level diplomacy.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor; or permission of the instructor.

name: The United States and the World after 1913
oneLiner: Examination of the history of US involvement in the world and international relations…
description: Examination of the history of US involvement in the world and international relations from 1913 to the present. Topics include the creation and maintenance of the American empire; the emergence of the U.S. as a superpower; America's involvement in the instigation, perpetuation and conclusion of the Cold War; cultural, economic, and educational exchange between the U.S. and other nations; and American participation in the international community.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: American Ethnic and Racial Relations to 1890
oneLiner: How ideas and practices of race and ethnicity developed and changed in colonial North…
description: How ideas and practices of race and ethnicity developed and changed in colonial North America and the U.S. from the 1600s to the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: American Ethnic and Racial Relations II: 1890-Present
oneLiner: The effects of ethnic and race relations on American life from the closing of the…
description: The effects of ethnic and race relations on American life from the closing of the frontier to the present including Russian Jews, American Irish, Mexican Americans, Japanese, and African-Americans.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: History of People of Color in the U.S.
oneLiner: History of the U.S. people of color, their experience in the development of American…
description: History of the U.S. people of color, their experience in the development of American society, from the 1600s to the present. Consequences of domination and racism in thwarting economic interests, and responses to limiting institutional arrangements. (This course is offered as RRS 600 and HIST 466. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Women in the U.S. to 1890
oneLiner: The history of the changing social, economic, political, and intellectual life of women…
description: The history of the changing social, economic, political, and intellectual life of women in the U.S. from colonization to 1890.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division or graduate standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Women in the U.S.: 1890-Present
oneLiner: The history of the changing social, economic, political, and intellectual life of women…
description: The history of the changing social, economic, political, and intellectual life of women in the U.S. from 1890 to the present.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: American Childhoods: Past and Present
oneLiner: American childhoods through time and across cultures since the 17th century.
description: American childhoods through time and across cultures since the 17th century.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or graduate standing; or permission of the instructor.

name: The U.S. Constitution to 1896
oneLiner: History of the U.S.
description: History of the U.S. Constitution from its origins in the late 1700s to the landmark Plessy v. Ferguson decision in 1896. Special attention to the changing structures of governance, powers of the courts, debates about African American slavery and Native American sovereignty, the struggles of women and minority groups for equal rights and social justice, and the reconstruction of the Constitution after the Civil War.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: The U.S. Constitution Since 1896
oneLiner: History of the U.S.
description: History of the U.S. Constitution from the late 19th century to the present with special attention to new constitutional amendments, shifts in the politics and powers of the Supreme Court, debates about racial segregation and immigration restriction, controversies about civil liberties and civil rights, and discussions about citizenship rules and voting rights. The struggles of Native Americans, racialized minorities, immigrants, women, gender and sexual minorities, and people with disabilities are emphasized.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Supreme Court and Social Change in U.S. History
oneLiner: Examination of major US Supreme Court decisions and their relationships to social…
description: Examination of major US Supreme Court decisions and their relationships to social change in the 19th, 20th, and early 21st centuries, with special attention to cases related to equal rights in general and the histories of Native Americans, people of color, immigrants, poor people, people with disabilities, women, and LGBT people in particular.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Slavery and Antislavery in the United States
oneLiner: History of slavery and antislavery in the US from the colonial period through the Civil…
description: History of slavery and antislavery in the US from the colonial period through the Civil War, with a focus on the ideologies, economics, and social relations that supported slavery and those that motivated antislavery and free-labor movements. Examination of experiences of enslavement and liberation. (This course is offered as HIST 473, RRS 473, and LABR 473. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GE Areas A1*, A2*, A3*, and B4*, all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Labor in the United States
oneLiner: Development of the workforce and organized labor in the U.S. with an emphasis on the…
description: Development of the workforce and organized labor in the U.S. with an emphasis on the social and economic characteristics of work and the workforce and characteristics of labor organizations at different times. (This course is offered as HIST 474, ECON 474, and LABR 474. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; GE Areas A1*, A2*, A3*, and B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Sexuality in the United States Before 1900
oneLiner: Examination of the history of sexuality in colonial America and the United States…
description: Examination of the history of sexuality in colonial America and the United States before 1900 with an emphasis on the sexual dimensions of capitalism, colonialism, conquest, immigration, imperialism, industrialization, racism, slavery, segregation, and urbanization. Same-sex, cross-sex, monoracial, and interracial relationships will be explored, as will courtship, marriage, and family life. Abortion, birth control, fertility, and reproduction; sex work and commercialized sex; free love, monogamy, and polygamy; obscenity, pornography, and sexual representation; sexual health, disease, ability, and disability; sex education and sexual knowledge; sexual consent and violence; and the regulation and production of sexuality in society, culture, economy, politics, and law.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: American Popular Culture History: Barnum to Reality TV
oneLiner: A social and cultural approach to United States history focused on pop culture…
description: A social and cultural approach to United States history focused on pop culture, including mass communication, consumer trends, technological innovation, and various forms of entertainment. Examine the role of pop culture in American history, especially as related to small-'r' republicanism, the ethics of individualism, identity formation, and community.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: The History of Baseball
oneLiner: Examine the origins of baseball and the way that it often reflects and sometimes shapes…
description: Examine the origins of baseball and the way that it often reflects and sometimes shapes American culture and history. Explore this history through literature, first-hand accounts, film, and experiences, which includes attending a game.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Thought and Culture in America to 1880
oneLiner: American thought and culture from colonial times to the 1880s including intellectual…
description: American thought and culture from colonial times to the 1880s including intellectual movements and influential texts. (This course is offered as HIST 480 and HUM 480. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Thought and Culture in America: 1880 to the Present
oneLiner: American thought and culture from the 1880s to the present including intellectual…
description: American thought and culture from the 1880s to the present including intellectual movements and influential texts. (This course is offered as HIST 481 and HUM 481. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Religion in America
oneLiner: The social history of religion in the United States from contact to the present.
description: The social history of religion in the United States from contact to the present. Changing relations between religious thought and institutions. The range and variety of forms of religious expression in an increasingly urbanized, industrialized, and globalized society. A particular focus on the relationship between religion, science, and modernity. (This course is offered as HIST 482 and RELS 482. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Horror Land: Monsters, Haunts, and Horror in American History
oneLiner: Examine the history of horror and fear in America since the colonial era, covering a…
description: Examine the history of horror and fear in America since the colonial era, covering a variety of phenomena, including folklore, Gothic literature, early crime journalism, religious fervor, monster fiction, horror films, urban legends, popular panics, Halloween, and haunted houses. Emphasis on the social, cultural, economic, ideological, and political contexts in which the horrifying and hideous were conceptualized, created, and consumed.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Disability and Culture in the U.S.
oneLiner: Major topics in U.S. history (industrialization, Civil War, eugenics, immigration…
description: Major topics in U.S. history (industrialization, Civil War, eugenics, immigration, Great Depression, social policies, etc.) through the lens of "disability."
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Sexuality in the United States Since 1900
oneLiner: Examination of the history of sexuality in the United States since 1900 with emphasis…
description: Examination of the history of sexuality in the United States since 1900 with emphasis on "sexual revolutions" and the influences and implications of capitalism, colonialism, immigration, imperialism, industrialization, racism, segregation, urbanization, and war. Same-sex, cross-sex, monoracial, and interracial relationships will be explored, as will courtship, marriage, and family life. Abortion, birth control, fertility, and reproduction; sex work and commercialized sex; free love, monogamy, and polygamy; obscenity, pornography, and sexual representation; sexual health, disease, ability, and disability; sex education and sexual knowledge; sexual consent and violence; and the regulation and production of sexuality in society, culture, economy, politics, and law.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Dynamics of the American City
oneLiner: Historical development and contemporary condition of urban America, city planning, and…
description: Historical development and contemporary condition of urban America, city planning, and federal-city relations. Discussion of the dynamics of urban policy-making and class, gender, race, and ethnicity in urban America. (This course is offered as USP 400 and HIST 489. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4*, all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Topics in American History
oneLiner: Topics course covering the history and historiography of a particular theme, event, or…
description: Topics course covering the history and historiography of a particular theme, event, or problem in U.S. History. Topics to be specified in the class schedule. May be repeated when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Political Violence and Terrorism in German History, Film, and Visual Media
oneLiner: Examination of the history of political violence and terrorism - its history, its…
description: Examination of the history of political violence and terrorism - its history, its causes, aims, and forms in Germany. Multidisciplinary approach to develop the knowledge and skills needed to examine the particularities of political violence and terrorism in Germany in the 20th and 21st century as seen in political manifestos, history, films, modern technology, and caricatures. Taught in English. All materials are available in English. (This course is offered as GER 514, HIST 514, I R 514, and PLSI 514. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Archives or Historical Agency Internship
oneLiner: Internship with an archive or other historical agency.
description: Internship with an archive or other historical agency. Development of knowledge, experience, and training in archival or historical agency work. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Upper-division History majors or permission of the instructor; permission of the department chair.

name: Editing and Publishing the History Journal
oneLiner: Supervised experience in editing and production of an annual journal of research.
description: Supervised experience in editing and production of an annual journal of research. Not applicable to major or minor fields in history. May be taken for a total of 4 units. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; HIST 300GW; or permission of the instructor.

name: Proseminar in History
oneLiner: Seminar-style culminating experience for the Bachelor of Arts in History, focused…
description: Seminar-style culminating experience for the Bachelor of Arts in History, focused principally on a range of historical topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary.

name: Honors Thesis

Introduction to basic concepts in international relations through a common and highly accessible medium, feature film. (This course is offered as I R 201 and CINE 101.
