oneLiner: Background in Latina/x/o literature within its historical framework, with an emphasis…
description: Background in Latina/x/o literature within its historical framework, with an emphasis on culture, politics, and identity, as seen through fiction, poetry, essays, and plays.

name: Topics in Latina/o/x History
oneLiner: Introduction to the history of Latinas/os/x in the U.S.
description: Introduction to the history of Latinas/os/x in the U.S. Analysis of the social, political, and economic conditions that give rise to multiple migrations. [CSL may be available]

name: Latina/o/x Murals, Memes, Music, and More: Latina/o/x Arts & Humanities
oneLiner: U.S.
description: U.S. Latina/o/x cultural experiences documented through music, visual culture, and oral history. Focus on the historical, social, political, and economic forces that inform the activist orientation of Latina/o/x music, public art, visual culture, and the humanities.
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2.

name: Latina/o, U.S. Government, and Constitutional Ideals
oneLiner: Basic governmental and political institutions and underlying socio-political ideals.
description: Basic governmental and political institutions and underlying socio-political ideals. Raza impact on legal-constitutional America and countervailing impact of political-legal structures imposed on Raza. [CSL may be available]

name: History of Latinas/Latinos in the U.S.
oneLiner: Examination of the social-cultural, economic, and political foundations of Latina/o…
description: Examination of the social-cultural, economic, and political foundations of Latina/o history from the Spanish colonial period to the present. (This course is offered as LTNS 278 and HIST 278. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: Latina/o Communities and the Environment
oneLiner: Introduction to the ways in which issues within Latinx communities and environmental…
description: Introduction to the ways in which issues within Latinx communities and environmental resources and conditions intersect. Using historical analysis and contemporary case studies, examine how conflicts around natural resources, urban and rural planning, and inter-generational practices inform Latinx experiences with the environment. (Plus-minus ABC/NC, CR/NC allowed)

name: Latin American and Latino/a/x Art, 1492 to the Present
oneLiner: Survey of Latin American and Latino/a/x artistic practices and architecture from 1492…
description: Survey of Latin American and Latino/a/x artistic practices and architecture from 1492 to the present. Focus on cross-cultural exchange with East and South East Asia, Europe, and West Africa. Emphasis on the impact of socio-political contexts on the production of art and architecture. (This course is offered as ARTH 301 and LTNS 301. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Art majors and minors with sophomore standing or above or LTNS 222* or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/o Studies Creative Writing Workshop
oneLiner: Explore Latina/x literature that covers a diverse range of geographies, genres, and…
description: Explore Latina/x literature that covers a diverse range of geographies, genres, and themes. Instruction and practice in creative writing with an emphasis on poetry, short fiction, and creative nonfiction. Opportunities to create works in Spanish, English, or Spanglish.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/os in California
oneLiner: Overview of the Latina/Latino experience in California from the Mexican-American War to…
description: Overview of the Latina/Latino experience in California from the Mexican-American War to contemporary times. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Latinx Youth Subcultures
oneLiner: Interdisciplinary analysis of Latinx Youth Cultures in the United States.
description: Interdisciplinary analysis of Latinx Youth Cultures in the United States. Discussion of how subcultures provide working-class youth one kind of strategy for negotiating their concrete collective existence.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Gender, Latina/x, and Women of Color Feminisms
oneLiner: An introduction to gender theory, women of color feminisms, and the ways queer Latinx…
description: An introduction to gender theory, women of color feminisms, and the ways queer Latinx communities disrupt heteronormative understandings of gender. [Formerly LTNS 410] [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Black Indians in the Americas
oneLiner: Examines factors impacting on multiracial identity formation among Native communities…
description: Examines factors impacting on multiracial identity formation among Native communities throughout the Americas with a specific focus on Black Indians. Explores concepts and theories regarding blood quantum, sovereignty, and land rights, and the social, legal, and political understanding of mixed-race Native Americans. (This course is offered as AIS 350, AFRS 350, and LTNS 355. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Afro/Latina/o Diasporas
oneLiner: Examine the history and experiences of Afro/Latina/o diasporic communities in the U.S.…
description: Examine the history and experiences of Afro/Latina/o diasporic communities in the U.S. and the history of African peoples in Latin America and the Caribbean.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Afro-Latina Experiences
oneLiner: Examination of Afro-Latina scholarship, experiences, knowledge, and narratives within…
description: Examination of Afro-Latina scholarship, experiences, knowledge, and narratives within the always-evolving racial discourse in the U.S. Through the exploration of scholarship, literary texts, and cultural productions of these women, concepts such as blackness and Latinidad, mestizaje, ethnicity, culture, and nationality will be discussed. Focus on Afro-Latinas' involvement in U.S. academia, identity formation processes, Afro-feminist movements, and artistic and cultural expressions as a means of resistance and survival.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/Latino Studies Knowledge Production
oneLiner: Become an active knowledge producer who can apply Latina/Latino Studies frameworks to…
description: Become an active knowledge producer who can apply Latina/Latino Studies frameworks to experiences both inside and beyond the university. Examine Latina/Latino Studies research methods, methodologies, and theories that challenge oppressive structures and identify the relationships between power, truth, and knowledge. Explore thematic sections that question how capitalism, colonialism, white supremacy, and heteropatriarchy shape the knowledge production process. Knowledge production has been historically central to movements for social change, and students will be empowered to contribute to the ongoing struggle for liberation.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; LTNS 215* or LTNS 278* or LTNS 350*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina Girlhood
oneLiner: Interdisciplinary and intersectional approach to understanding how Latina girlhood is…
description: Interdisciplinary and intersectional approach to understanding how Latina girlhood is shaped by historical, political, cultural, and economic domains of power. Examine how gender, race/ethnicity, sexuality, nationality, citizenship, ability, and space/place shape how people experience and articulate girlhood in similar and divergent ways across time and locations.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/o/x Cinema
oneLiner: Examine Latino/a/x history using Latino/a/x-themed and produced films.
description: Examine Latino/a/x history using Latino/a/x-themed and produced films. The power of stereotypes, global dissemination of film, and examples of the ways in which Latin American and U.S. Latina/o/x filmmakers respond to stereotypes by creating cinematic counter-discourses. (This course is offered as LTNS 409 and CINE 309. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/o Economic Empowerment
oneLiner: Critical analysis of the changing political and economic experiences of Latinas/os in…
description: Critical analysis of the changing political and economic experiences of Latinas/os in the US. Focus on three parts: Latinas/os are not a minority; ideology, policy, and the economy; and the Latina/o economic experience in the US. Examine institutionalized racism, equity, ethnocentrism, and how it relates to policy and Latina/o economic opportunities. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Popular and Traditional Music of the Latinx U.S.
oneLiner: Survey of Latina/o music in the United States from 1850 until the current day in a…
description: Survey of Latina/o music in the United States from 1850 until the current day in a chronological and categorical manner. Exploration and understanding of the main Latina/o/x/Caribbean music genres that were a base for Latinx music-making and its narrative in the US, including Mexican regional, Cuban, Puerto Rican, and music of Central America. Examine the culture, politics, and other social phenomena associated with specific Latinx music styles and time periods. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Race, Crime, and Justice
oneLiner: Ethnic studies methods and cross-cultural perspectives examine the rise of institutions…
description: Ethnic studies methods and cross-cultural perspectives examine the rise of institutions of law enforcement, juvenile and criminal justice, case studies, life histories, and community service learning internships. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as LTNS 430 and C J 435. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Exploration of the histories and contemporary experiences of Latina/x/o communities in…
description: Exploration of the histories and contemporary experiences of Latina/x/o communities in San Francisco and beyond to understand the role oral histories play in representing Latina/x/o culture and experiences. Focus on the theories, practices, and ethics involved in oral history and reading texts that use personal narrative in a variety of ways. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Gendered Borders: Latinas and Globalization
oneLiner: Gender and globalization: moving society toward borderless economies with barricaded…
description: Gender and globalization: moving society toward borderless economies with barricaded borders. Latinas struggle for fair wages, self-determination, and healthy families. Women living in the U.S. and Latin America adjusting to transnational reality. (This course is offered as LTNS 445 and WGS 445. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Latinx Indigeneities
oneLiner: An examination of how Indigenous migrants from Latin America transform notions of…
description: An examination of how Indigenous migrants from Latin America transform notions of Latinidad and indigeneity in the US. Emphasis on place-based knowledges, decolonial feminisms, sovereignty, and systems of healing.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Resistance Literature of the Americas
oneLiner: Examine the historical development of a literary genre that mobilizes literature as a…
description: Examine the historical development of a literary genre that mobilizes literature as a tool of liberation. Survey of precolonial and contemporary texts spanning the Caribbean, Central and South American diasporas, Mexico, and the United States. Explore how "Third World" liberation movements contest dominant cultural narratives, politicize literary poetics, and deploy creative practices to resist colonialism, imperialism, heteropatriarchy, canonical exclusion, and censorship.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Central Americans of the U.S.: History and Heritage
oneLiner: Developmental relationship between U.S. communities of Central American origin and…
description: Developmental relationship between U.S. communities of Central American origin and historical, socio-economic, and cultural factors of contemporary Central America; nationalistic movements, migrations to the U.S., economic dependence, social change, art, and society.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Mexican American and Chicana/x/o History
oneLiner: Examine key historical processes that have shaped the racial and political formations…

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Examine the history of Caribbean migration to the United States since the nineteenth…
description: Examine the history of Caribbean migration to the United States since the nineteenth century, focusing in particular on migrations from Cuba, Puerto Rico, Haiti, Panama, and the Dominican Republic.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

Focus on several different Nahautl and Mayan groups throughout Mexico and Central America. Readings will include ancient codices, literary texts and translations, and historical and contemporary studies.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Examination of Latino juvenile justice, the myths and realities, and the…

Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Creative Writing in Spanish: Poetry, Fiction, and Drama

description: Reading and analysis of literary texts from Spain and Latin America. Practice in writing poetry, fiction, and plays in Spanish. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: SPAN 301 or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Women in Latin America
oneLiner: History of the changing roles of women in Latin America from the colonial period to the…
description: History of the changing roles of women in Latin America from the colonial period to the present. (This course is offered as HIST 355, WGS 355, and LTNS 533. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Central Americans Writing in the United States
oneLiner: Investigation of Central American immigrant experiences and their cultural and…
description: Investigation of Central American immigrant experiences and their cultural and political impact on the artistic and academic sectors. Exploration of the various stages of this evolving literature, including a range of undocumented, queer, Afro, and Indigenous Central American voices.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing, GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better, or permission of the instructor.

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Sociology of Latina/x/o Experiences
oneLiner: A comprehensive introduction to sociological perspectives on Latina/x/o experiences in…

prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

description: Introduction to Latino politics focusing on equity, labor, immigrant rights, and voter-based movement. prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; LTNS 276*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Mexican Politics and Society
oneLiner: Peoples, politics, and cultures of Mexico.
description: Peoples, politics, and cultures of Mexico. The implications of rapid change in Mexico for California and the U.S. [CSL may be available] (This course is offered as LTNS 670 and PLSI 408. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Central American literature, from earliest indigenous manuscripts, such as the Popol…

prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Latina/o/x Community Organizing and Career Futures

description: Latinx community organizing including mobilization and action toward the resolution of community problems, elements and techniques of organizing, development of leadership and community resources, acquisition and direction of power, and analysis of the existing social, political, and economic context. name: Projects in the Teaching of Latina/o Studies

name: Community Fieldwork in Latina/o Studies

name: Archaeology of the Ancient World

oneLiner: Introduction to the important role museums play in society including preservation and…

(Plus-minus letter grade only)

name: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Greece
oneLiner: Survey of Greek material culture (art, architecture, city planning, etc.) from the…

name: Art and Archaeology of Ancient Egypt
oneLiner: Ancient Egyptian civilization from Pre-dynastic through Ptolemaic times: art…
description: Ancient Egyptian civilization from Pre-dynastic through Ptolemaic times: art, archaeology, literature, and religion with research use of Sutro Egyptian Collection. (This course is offered as CLAR 500, M S 500, and ARTH 407. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

description: Introduction to signs, vocabulary, grammar, and syntax of Middle Egyptian language. Learn to read texts from funerary stelae, coffins, and short stories. name: Educational Programming and Interpretation Practicum
oneLiner: Work on educational programming and interpretation tasks in the Global Museum…
description: Work on educational programming and interpretation tasks in the Global Museum, including engagement specialist training, school field trips, tours, and the development and implementation of museum exhibition interpretation. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Museum Studies minors; M S 201 and M S 202 with grades of C or better; concurrent enrollment in M S 681. May not be taken concurrently with M S 683.

name: History and Organization of Museums
oneLiner: Major museology facets, including analysis of diverse museums, career options, ethics…
description: Major museology facets, including analysis of diverse museums, career options, ethics, laws, funding, and literature. Museum operation and community-museum relationships through on-site observations, interviews, and research.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Museum Studies students and/or permission of the instructor.

name: San Francisco Bay Area Museums: Behind the Scenes
oneLiner: Study of San Francisco Bay Area museums: their history, organization, collections…
description: Study of San Francisco Bay Area museums: their history, organization, collections stewardship, exhibits, public programs, and mission. Includes structured "behind-the-scenes" tours of local museums.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Museum Studies students, declared upper-division Museum Studies minors, or permission of the instructor.

name: Perspectives on Museums: A Professional Forum
oneLiner: Guest speakers from the museum community to provide graduate students with perspectives…
description: Guest speakers from the museum community to provide graduate students with perspectives and discussion on current practices and trends in the museum workplace. May be repeated for a total of 3 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate Museum Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Museum Education and Public Outreach
oneLiner: Overview and evaluation of educational services in museums including the planning and…
description: Overview and evaluation of educational services in museums including the planning and implementation of educational programs and establishing a liaison with public schools. Designed for graduate students, museum professionals, and public school teachers. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Graduate standing and permission of the instructor.

name: Museum Curatorship and Collecting
oneLiner: Analysis of the duties of museum curators, including academic research, collections…
description: Analysis of the duties of museum curators, including academic research, collections documentation, collections development, donor cultivation, ethical collection practices, exhibition concept development, and the curator's position within the institution and community. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Museum Studies students.

name: Museum Exhibition Development
oneLiner: Theory and practical experience in the development and installation of exhibitions in…
description: Theory and practical experience in the development and installation of exhibitions in museums and related exhibition spaces in libraries or similar institutions, including collaborations between such entities. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing.

name: Museum Conservation and Restoration
oneLiner: Theory and practice in museum conservation and restoration, using the Sutro Egyptian…
description: Theory and practice in museum conservation and restoration, using the Sutro Egyptian and permanent collections. Analysis of museum artifacts.
prereqNotes: Graduate Museum Studies students.

name: Preservation of Natural History and Cultural Collections
oneLiner: Analysis of major types of natural history specimens, their properties, potential…
description: Analysis of major types of natural history specimens, their properties, potential hazards facing them, and appropriate conservation techniques.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or senior standing with the permission of the instructor.

name: Cultural Heritage Preservation
oneLiner: Archaeological and architectural conservation: history of U.S. legislation and…
description: Archaeological and architectural conservation: history of U.S. legislation and implementation, international organizations, major national and international projects, philosophy of preservation strategies, conservation ethic.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division or graduate standing.

name: Archives Management and Preservation
oneLiner: History, principles, methodologies, and practical administration of non-electronic…
description: History, principles, methodologies, and practical administration of non-electronic archives (original documents, maps, photographic materials, manuscripts, diaries, albums, government records); practical, hands-on experience with preservation methods. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or senior standing with the permission of the instructor.

name: Museum Collections Management and Registration
oneLiner: Tasks performed by museum registrars: documentation of collections, loan procedures…
description: Tasks performed by museum registrars: documentation of collections, loan procedures, collections storage, museum security, disaster preparedness, traveling exhibitions and customs, insurance, and development of collections management policies.
prereqNotes: Graduate Museum Studies students.

name: Museum Management, Law, and Ethics
oneLiner: Legal issues of concern to museum professionals and artists; laws governing the…
description: Legal issues of concern to museum professionals and artists; laws governing the acquisition of art objects, authentication, taxes, liability, censorship, artists' rights, copyright, museum organization, and labor relations. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate Museum Studies students, MFA Art students, or permission of the instructor.

name: Museums in the Digital Age
oneLiner: Use and role of digital media and information technology in museums.
description: Use and role of digital media and information technology in museums. Development of practical and theoretical skill set for the management of digital assets for exhibit development, education, public relations and marketing, collections preservation, and digitally-mediated outreach.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Digital Preservation for Museums and Cultural Heritage Institutions
oneLiner: Survey and applied practicum of digital technologies used in museums and cultural…
description: Survey and applied practicum of digital technologies used in museums and cultural heritage institutions. Exploration of the relationship between computation and the humanities; and issues facing cultural institutions in the 21st century, such as open-source programs, the organization and preservation of existing collections, and real-world examples in the field of digital cultural management. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Museum Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Museum Governance
oneLiner: Analysis of governance in museums, including trusteeship, board issues, roles of…
description: Analysis of governance in museums, including trusteeship, board issues, roles of director and senior management, governance conflicts, mission statements, use of advisory committees and support groups, collections issues, planning, and recent controversies. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Museums and Cultural Property
oneLiner: Examination of legal and ethical issues concerning cultural property in museums: museum…
description: Examination of legal and ethical issues concerning cultural property in museums: museum acquisition policies; international art/antiquities trade; auction houses; WWII-era looting; repatriation; ownership dispute resolution; relationships with descendant communities. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Fundraising in Museums
oneLiner: Examination of fundraising in museums, budget building, budget cycle, legal and tax…
description: Examination of fundraising in museums, budget building, budget cycle, legal and tax issues of fundraising, as well as specific fundraising methods (gifts, planned giving, bequests, endowments, e-commerce, grants, contracts). (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Museum Studies students or permission of the instructor.

name: Museum Audiences, Visitors, and Communities
oneLiner: Analysis of museum visitors (visitor studies) and non-visitors (audience research) in…
description: Analysis of museum visitors (visitor studies) and non-visitors (audience research) in the context of museum communities. Methodology and applications of visitor/audience research to improve museum operations and exhibitions.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing and permission of the instructor.

name: Museum Internship
oneLiner: Practicum in collections management, exhibition design, fundraising management…
description: Practicum in collections management, exhibition design, fundraising management, publishing, curation, educational programming, conservation under the supervision of a professional museum employee and SF State instructor. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Graduate Museum Studies students and M S 700.

name: Professional Conferences and Workshops
oneLiner: Attendance, participation, and evaluation at professional conferences, workshops, or…
description: Attendance, participation, and evaluation at professional conferences, workshops, or short courses offered by museums, professional associations, or other recognized institutions. Prior approval by the Museum Studies Program is mandatory. May be repeated for a total of 3 units. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor.

name: Project Management for Museums
oneLiner: Under faculty guidance, development, logistics, budgeting, and time management for…
description: Under faculty guidance, development, logistics, budgeting, and time management for museum exhibits, catalogue publishing, conferences/sessions for museum professionals, or special events for schools/general public. May be repeated for a total of 3 units for the degree credit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Museum Studies students; M S 720 and M S 850; or permission of the instructor.

name: Creative Work Project
oneLiner: Original creative work project which must be developed with the approval of the Museum…
description: Original creative work project which must be developed with the approval of the Museum Studies program. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration. (CR/NC; RP grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor and approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Preparation for Written Comprehensive Examination
oneLiner: Preparation for Written Comprehensive Examination in Museum Studies for graduate…
description: Preparation for Written Comprehensive Examination in Museum Studies for graduate students who have been advanced to candidacy for the M.A. degree in Museum Studies. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies; and recommendation of major adviser. Concurrently enrollment in M S 896EXM.

name: Written Comprehensive Examination
oneLiner: Written Comprehensive Examination in Museum Studies for graduate students who have been…
description: Written Comprehensive Examination in Museum Studies for graduate students who have been advanced to candidacy for the M.A. degree in Museum Studies. May be repeated a total of 3 times. (CR/NR, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Museum Studies students; permission of the instructor; recommendation of major adviser; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies. Concurrent enrollment in M S 896.

name: Directed Thesis Advising and Support
oneLiner: Directed advising and support for students writing theses or creative works.
description: Directed advising and support for students writing theses or creative works. May be taken before enrollment in M S 894 or M S 898. Once students have taken M S 894 or M S 898 they must take M S 897 every Spring semester until they finish the degree. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing.

name: Master's Thesis
oneLiner: (CR/NC grading only)
description: (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor; approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies; and recommendation of major adviser. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Professional-level, independent study of a particular aspect of museum work under the…
description: Professional-level, independent study of a particular aspect of museum work under the guidance of a faculty member in the Museum Studies Program. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Museum Studies students; permission of the program director.

name: Mathematics for Business Calculus I
oneLiner: Introduction of the necessary business vocabulary.
description: Introduction of the necessary business vocabulary. Review of numbers and operations, exponents and radicals, functions in general, and linear, quadratic, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions in particular, in the context of business, finance, and economy. Introduction to the mathematics of finance: simple and compound interest, annuities, amortization.
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module; Category III* or IV* placement for QR/Math.

name: Mathematics for Business Calculus II
oneLiner: Derivatives and integrals.
description: Derivatives and integrals. Applications of differentiation and integration, including optimization. Problems involving business, finance, and economics. (Note: Successful completion of MATH 107 and MATH 108 will culminate in satisfying the Quantitative Reasoning requirement (GE Area 2/B4). For this course to satisfy General Education, students must earn a grade of C- or CR or higher.)
prereqNotes: MATH 107 with a grade of C or better.

name: Business Calculus
oneLiner: Functions, derivatives, and integrals.
description: Functions, derivatives, and integrals. Applications of differentiation and integration, including optimization and moving averages. Problems involving business, finance, and economics. Elements of basic calculus. (Note: In order for this course to satisfy General Education, students must earn a C- or CR or higher grade if taken fall 2014 or later.)
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module. For students who wish to take business calculus in one semester.

name: Support for College Mathematics
oneLiner: Review of numbers and operations, exponents, and radicals.
description: Review of numbers and operations, exponents, and radicals. Linear, quadratic, polynomial, and rational functions. Exponential and logarithmic functions as needed. Develop and practice strategies for proficiency in quantitative reasoning through problem-solving, communication, and interpretation of data and graphs. [Formerly MATH 112]
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module. Concurrent enrollment in PHIL 111* or CSC 110*.

name: Quantitative Reasoning for Civic Engagement
oneLiner: Participation in civic society requires not only understanding principles of…
description: Participation in civic society requires not only understanding principles of governance, but also problem-solving. Develop the mathematical concepts and skills relevant to the challenges and issues facing individuals and societies. Enables both quantitative understanding and decision-making about aspects of work, life, and civic participation. (Plus-minus ABC/NC, CR/NC allowed) (Note: For this course to satisfy General Education, students must earn a grade of C- or CR or better.) (This course is offered as LCA 112/PHIL 112/PLSI 112/HIST 112/I R 112/MATH 112. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module.

name: Mathematics for Statistical Quantitative Reasoning
oneLiner: Review of mathematics in the context of elementary statistics: numbers, fractions…
description: Review of mathematics in the context of elementary statistics: numbers, fractions, decimals, percentages; units; rounding; formulas and scientific notation; order of operations; algebra of equations; graphs and plots; sets; principals of counting.
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module. Concurrent enrollment in ISED 160* or PSY 171 required.

name: Mathematics for Elementary Statistics
oneLiner: Support development of quantitative reasoning at the college level in the context of…
description: Support development of quantitative reasoning at the college level in the context of data visualization, data analysis, probability theory, and statistics. Development of sense-making skills and computational understanding. Activity. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: First-year math advising module. Concurrent enrollment in MATH 124*, PSY 171* or ISED 160*.

name: Elementary Statistics
oneLiner: Data analysis, probability, and statistical inference.
description: Data analysis, probability, and statistical inference. For students in any field where statistics is a means of communication and a tool for decision making.
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module. Students who elect to take additional support should concurrently enroll in MATH 123.

name: Concepts of the Number System
oneLiner: Designed for prospective multiple subjects credential candidates.
description: Designed for prospective multiple subjects credential candidates. Understanding operations with whole numbers, fractions and decimals. Problem-solving strategies, numeration systems and elementary number theory.

name: Prelude to Calculus I
oneLiner: Review of numbers and operations, exponents, and radicals.
description: Review of numbers and operations, exponents, and radicals. Linear, quadratic, polynomial, and rational functions. Exponential growth and exponential functions. Logarithmic functions. The transcendental number e and natural logarithms. The first semester of a year-long stretch pre-calculus course.
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module; Category III* and IV* placement for QR/Math. Also required: Category III/IV QR placement

name: Prelude to Calculus II
oneLiner: Trigonometry, trigonometric identities, trigonometric and inverse trigonometric…
description: Trigonometry, trigonometric identities, trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions, sequences and series, and limits. (Note: Successful completion of MATH 197 and MATH 198 will culminate in satisfying the Quantitative Reasoning requirement (GE Area 2/B4). For this course to satisfy General Education, students must earn a grade of C- or CR or higher.)
prereqNotes: MATH 197 with a grade of C or better.

name: Pre-Calculus
oneLiner: Functions, graphing techniques, exponentials and logarithms, trigonometry.
description: Functions, graphing techniques, exponentials and logarithms, trigonometry.
prereqNotes: First-Year Math Advising Module. For students who want to take pre-calculus in one semester. Also required: First-Year Math Advising Module

name: Mathematical Computing
oneLiner: Introduces basic sequential programming constructs in scientific computing using the…
description: Introduces basic sequential programming constructs in scientific computing using the Python Language. Uses programming projects to review and reinforce material from Calculus and Linear Algebra. Introduces essential modeling and programming concepts. [Formerly MATH 309]
prereqNotes: MATH 226 with a grade of C or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Linear Algebra
oneLiner: Introduction to the solution to system of linear equations using Gaussian elimination…
description: Introduction to the solution to system of linear equations using Gaussian elimination, matrix algebra, subspaces of R^n and their bases, matrix transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization and applications, dot product, orthogonality, orthogonal bases, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, and using MATLAB to solve linear algebra problems.
prereqNotes: MATH 198* or MATH 199* or MATH 226* with a grade of C or better.

name: Calculus I
oneLiner: Graphs.
description: Graphs. Differentiation: theory, techniques, and applications. Integration: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and applications. Transcendental functions. Lecture, 3 units; laboratory, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: One of the following: MATH 198 or MATH 199 or equivalent with a grade of C or better; or MATH 226 or equivalent with a grade of C- or lower; or high school pre-calculus with B or better; or high school calculus with a grade of C or better.

name: Calculus II
oneLiner: Techniques of integration, analytic geometry, polar coordinates, vectors, improper…
description: Techniques of integration, analytic geometry, polar coordinates, vectors, improper integrals, and sequences and series.
prereqNotes: MATH 226* with a grade of C or better.

name: Calculus III
oneLiner: Three-dimensional analytic geometry, partial differentiation, multiple integrals, and…
description: Three-dimensional analytic geometry, partial differentiation, multiple integrals, and vector calculus. Lecture, 3 units; lab, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: MATH 227* with a grade of C or better.

name: Elementary Differential Equations and Linear Algebra
oneLiner: First and second order linear differential equations, Laplace transform methods, matrix…
description: First and second order linear differential equations, Laplace transform methods, matrix algebra.
prereqNotes: MATH 227* with a grade of C or better.

name: Advanced Number Systems
oneLiner: Designed for prospective multiple subject credential candidates, continues work done in…
description: Designed for prospective multiple subject credential candidates, continues work done in MATH 165 with decimals and percents. Introduces operations with negative numbers. Additional topics include problem-solving and elementary number theory.
prereqNotes: MATH 165 with a grade of C or better.

name: History of Mathematics - GWAR
oneLiner: Survey of the history of mathematics focusing on topics of interest to secondary…
description: Survey of the history of mathematics focusing on topics of interest to secondary mathematics teachers. Emphasis on telling the story of mathematics through research and writing an expository paper. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; MATH 227 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher.

name: Exploration and Proof - GWAR
oneLiner: Informal exploration and proofs in mathematics.
description: Informal exploration and proofs in mathematics. Basic concepts of advanced mathematics courses. Exploratory thinking, elementary logic, sets, mathematical induction, the integers, relations, and functions. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2; MATH 226* with a grade of C or higher.

name: Elementary Number Theory
oneLiner: Divisibility, congruencies, power residues, quadratic reciprocity, diophantine equations.
description: Divisibility, congruencies, power residues, quadratic reciprocity, diophantine equations. Number theoretic functions, continued fractions and rational approximation, partitions.
prereqNotes: MATH 227 and MATH 301GW with grades of C or better.

name: Probability and Statistics with Computing
oneLiner: Data analysis, probability distributions, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing.
description: Data analysis, probability distributions, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing. Students use computer software to do statistical analyses.
prereqNotes: MATH 227* with a grade of C or better; computer experience that meets the approval of the instructor; basic concepts of probability and statistics. Also required: computer experience approved by instructor

name: Linear Algebra
oneLiner: Examination of the solution of systems of linear equations, Gaussian elimination…
description: Examination of the solution of systems of linear equations, Gaussian elimination, matrix algebra, vector spaces, bases, linear transformations, inner products, orthogonal bases, orthogonalization, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization and spectral factorization of symmetric matrices, and singular value decomposition.
prereqNotes: MATH 226* with a grade of C or better; concurrent enrollment in MATH 301GW recommended.

name: Modern Algebra
oneLiner: Introduction to groups, rings, integral domains, fields, and ordering.
description: Introduction to groups, rings, integral domains, fields, and ordering.
prereqNotes: MATH 301GW and either MATH 225 or MATH 325 all with a grade of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to SAS
oneLiner: Using SAS software for data management, presentation of data using graphs and reports…
description: Using SAS software for data management, presentation of data using graphs and reports, calculation of basic statistics such as mean, standard error, percentiles. Analysis of data using t-test, Chi-square test, regression, and analysis of variance.
prereqNotes: MATH 209* or MATH 309* or CSC 210* or CSC 215* or CSC 309* with a grade of C or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Geometry
oneLiner: Introduction to the origin and foundations of geometry: Euclidean, non-Euclidean…
description: Introduction to the origin and foundations of geometry: Euclidean, non-Euclidean geometries, more recent approaches. Quick survey of high school geometry. Classification and representation of motions and similarities. Projections, homogeneous coordinates.
prereqNotes: MATH 228 and MATH 301GW with grades of C or better.

name: Real Analysis I
oneLiner: Critical development of analysis: Bolzano-Weierstrass and Heine-Borel theorems; limits…
description: Critical development of analysis: Bolzano-Weierstrass and Heine-Borel theorems; limits, continuity, differentiability, integrability.
prereqNotes: MATH 227 and MATH 301GW* with grades of C or better.

name: Field Study for Secondary Teachers
oneLiner: Completion of tuberculosis test and fingerprinting for work in the public schools.
description: Completion of tuberculosis test and fingerprinting for work in the public schools. Opportunity for students to relate the mathematics they are learning to the teaching and learning of mathematics at the middle and high school levels; at the same time, fulfill the 45-hour field experience requirement for prospective teachers.
prereqNotes: MATH 301GW with a grade of C or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Ordinary Differential Equations I
oneLiner: First-order differential equations, second-order linear equations with constant…
description: First-order differential equations, second-order linear equations with constant coefficients, graphical and numerical methods, systems of differential equations and phase-plane analysis, existence and uniqueness theorems.
prereqNotes: MATH 228; MATH 225 or MATH 325; MATH 209 or CSC 309 or equivalent, all with grades of C or better.

name: Introduction to Complex Analysis
oneLiner: Analytic functions of a complex variable.
description: Analytic functions of a complex variable. Cauchy's theorem, power series, Laurent series, singularities, residue theorem with applications to definite integrals.
prereqNotes: MATH 228 and MATH 301GW* with grades of C or better.

name: Numerical Analysis
oneLiner: Numerical solution of algebra and calculus problems.
description: Numerical solution of algebra and calculus problems. Interpolation and approximations; direct and iterative methods for solutions of linear equations. Gaussian elimination. Numerical differentiation and integration; solution of ordinary differential equations.
prereqNotes: MATH 228; MATH 225 or MATH 325; and CSC 210 or CSC 215 or MATH 209 or MATH 309, all with grades of C or better.

name: Combinatorics
oneLiner: An introduction to fundamental combinatorial objects, their uses in other fields of…
description: An introduction to fundamental combinatorial objects, their uses in other fields of mathematics and its applications, and their analysis. Does an object with certain prescribed properties exist? How many of them are there? What structure do they have? (MATH 720/MATH 420 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; MATH 301GW; CSC 230 or MATH 310 or MATH 325; all with grades of C or better; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Linear Models
oneLiner: Theory and applications of Linear Models, Multiple Regression, Analysis of Variance for…
description: Theory and applications of Linear Models, Multiple Regression, Analysis of Variance for Fixed and Random Effects, Nested and Crossed Treatments, and Experimental Design. (MATH 724/MATH 424 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; MATH 228*, MATH 325*, and MATH 440* all with grades of C or better; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Applied and Computational Linear Algebra
oneLiner: Explore techniques for solving huge linear systems, covering both the theory behind the…
description: Explore techniques for solving huge linear systems, covering both the theory behind the techniques and the computation. Review and further develop earlier concepts and use them to efficiently solve problems across the natural and social sciences. Problems are drawn from numerical analysis, mathematical biology, data analysis and machine learning, imaging and signal processing, chemistry, physics, economics, computer science, engineering, and other disciplines.
prereqNotes: MATH 225 or MATH 325; and MATH 209 or MATH 309 or CSC 210 or CSC 215; all with grades of C or better.

name: Mathematics of Optimization
oneLiner: Modeling and solution of optimization problems as linear, semidefinite, nonlinear, or…
description: Modeling and solution of optimization problems as linear, semidefinite, nonlinear, or integer programming problems. Analysis and interpretations of solutions to these problems.
prereqNotes: MATH 325 with a grade of C or better.

name: Modern Algebra II
oneLiner: Group actions, conjugacy classes, and Sylow's Theorem.
description: Group actions, conjugacy classes, and Sylow's Theorem. Rings, modules, vector spaces, and finitely generated modules over PIDs. Field extensions and finite fields. (MATH 735/MATH 435 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; MATH 335 with a grade of C or better; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Probability and Statistics I
oneLiner: Probability spaces, elementary combinatorics, random variables, independence, expected…
description: Probability spaces, elementary combinatorics, random variables, independence, expected values, moment generating functions, selected probability distributions, limit theorems, and applications.
prereqNotes: MATH 228* with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently); or permission of the instructor.

name: Probability and Statistics II
oneLiner: Sampling distributions, estimation of parameters, hypothesis testing, goodness-of-fit…
description: Sampling distributions, estimation of parameters, hypothesis testing, goodness-of-fit tests, linear regression, and selected non-parametric methods. (MATH 741/MATH 441 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; MATH 228*, MATH 325*, and MATH 440* all with grades of C or better; GPA of 3.0 or higher; or permission of the instructor.

name: Probability Models
oneLiner: Advanced topics in probability theory: discrete and continuous-time Markov chains…
description: Advanced topics in probability theory: discrete and continuous-time Markov chains, Poisson process, queuing systems, and applications.
prereqNotes: MATH 228*, MATH 325*, and MATH 440* all with grades of C or better, or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Time Series Analysis
oneLiner: Introduction to the theory and practice of time series analysis.
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of time series analysis. Topics include time series regression and exploratory data analysis, stationary processes, ARMA/ARIMA models, Spectral analysis, and Multivariate time series analysis: Multivariate ARMA. The analyses will be performed using R/Python software.
prereqNotes: MATH 228*, MATH 325*, and MATH 440* all with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Design and Analysis of Experiments
oneLiner: Learn how to plan, design, and conduct experiments and analyze the resulting data.…
description: Learn how to plan, design, and conduct experiments and analyze the resulting data. (MATH 747/MATH 447 is a paired course offering. Students who complete the course at one level may not repeat the course at the other level.)
prereqNotes: MATH 228*, MATH 325*, and MATH 440* all with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Statistical Learning and Data Mining
oneLiner: Modern techniques in the statistical analysis of data, including regression…
description: Modern techniques in the statistical analysis of data, including regression, classification, regularization methods, model selection, non-parametric methods, dimensionality reduction, and clustering; employ statistical software to analyze real data using advanced methods from statistics, machine learning, data mining, and pattern recognition.
prereqNotes: MATH 228*, MATH 325*, and MATH 440* all with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Categorical Data Analysis
oneLiner: Exploration of descriptive and inferential methods for contingency tables, generalized…
description: Exploration of descriptive and inferential methods for contingency tables, generalized linear models for discrete data, logistic regression for binary responses, multi-category logistic models for nominal and ordinal responses, log-linear models, and inference for matched-pairs and correlated clustered data.
prereqNotes: MATH 228*, MATH 325*, and MATH 440* all with grades of C or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Topology
oneLiner: Rigorous development of the theory of metric spaces and topological spaces.
description: Rigorous development of the theory of metric spaces and topological spaces. Concepts covered include open, closed sets, interior, closure, boundary of sets; connects sets, compact sets, continuous functions defined on metric and topological spaces.
prereqNotes: MATH 370 with a grade of C or better.

name: Introduction to Differential Geometry
oneLiner: Study of intrinsic surface along with a topological invariant known as the Euler…
description: Study of intrinsic surface along with a topological invariant known as the Euler characteristic. The aim is to prove that the Euler characteristic of a compact orientated surface is numerically equal to the total index of any vector field with isolated zeroes (Poincare-Hopf Index theorem), the total Gaussian curvature (Gauss-Bonnet-Chern theorem), and the algebraic total of the number of non-degenerate critical points (Morse theorem).
prereqNotes: MATH 228 and MATH 325 with grades of C or better; MATH 370 or MATH 450; or permission of the instructor.

name: Mathematical Modeling
oneLiner: Deterministic and stochastic techniques used in mathematical modeling, illustrated and…
description: Deterministic and stochastic techniques used in mathematical modeling, illustrated and developed through problems originating in industry and applied research.
prereqNotes: MATH 225 or MATH 325; MATH 245 or MATH 376; all with grades of C or better.

name: Dynamical Systems with Applications
oneLiner: An introduction to the study of iterations (repeated composition) of a function in most…
description: An introduction to the study of iterations (repeated composition) of a function in most basic contexts, including linear and continuous functions of one variable, number-theoretic functions, geometric functions, and Markov chains. Using mathematical software as an investigative tool, explore applications chosen from piecewise linear systems, fractals, chaos, number theory, cryptography, complex networks, and mathematical modeling.

All sections require enrollment in live ACT class and online LEC. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit.

name: Basic Music I: Piano
oneLiner: Development of basic skills in music fundamentals and piano.
description: Development of basic skills in music fundamentals and piano. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. Extra fee required. Open to all students. (This course is offered as MUS 122 and TH A 122. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: The Foundations of Music Theory
oneLiner: Comprehensive introduction to music fundamentals and development of aural skills.…
description: Comprehensive introduction to music fundamentals and development of aural skills. (Plus-minus letter grade only) (This course is offered as MUS 130 and TH A 131. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors or minors or permission of the instructor.

name: Appreciation of Diverse Music
oneLiner: Survey of a diverse selection of musical traditions and practices, from ancient to…
description: Survey of a diverse selection of musical traditions and practices, from ancient to modern times, aimed at expanding the student's knowledge of and appreciation for music beyond what is easily accessible and heavily marketed. Emphasis on appreciating the aesthetic value of representative works within their cultural contexts. Includes folk and popular music of Europe and the Americas, music of the African diaspora, and western "classical" music from Ancient Greek to modern experimentalism.

name: Survey of Music for Film, TV, and Games
oneLiner: Survey of music used to develop, transform, and underscore emotion in visual media such…
description: Survey of music used to develop, transform, and underscore emotion in visual media such as film, video games, virtual reality, TV, animation, and more. Discussion and analysis of theoretical topics related to the experience and development of music for visual media. Through the use of specific exceptional pieces of media, integration of topics related to social justice, racial minorities, global perspectives.

name: Survey of the History of Electronic Music
oneLiner: Survey of the styles, methods, and technologies of electronic music as a contemporary…
description: Survey of the styles, methods, and technologies of electronic music as a contemporary art form and their impact on modern global culture. Examination of the work of experimental pioneers whose music stems from the classical tradition but whose methods and tools give rise to all forms of electronic music. Exploration of dance music and other popular styles originating in disco and house which have expanded to multitudinous genres and sub-genres.

name: Fundamentals of Modern Musicianship
oneLiner: Explore music notation, terminology, rhythm, scales and modes, key signatures and the…
description: Explore music notation, terminology, rhythm, scales and modes, key signatures and the circle of fifths, intervals, transposition, chords and chord progressions, figured bass, lead sheet notation, Roman numeral analysis, and basic structures integrating the active performance of all concepts. (This course is offered as MUS 200 [formerly MUS 234] and TH A 234. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: MUS 130 or permission of the instructor.

name: Class Piano I
oneLiner: Instruction includes techniques, repertoire, and keyboard harmony. (Plus-minus letter…
description: Instruction includes techniques, repertoire, and keyboard harmony. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Satisfactory performance audition; ability to read treble and bass clefs, Music majors or minors; priority given to Music majors, others by approval of department.

name: Class Piano II

description: Laboratory. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

description: Contrapuntal form and procedures through written exercises, analysis, and composition in two to four parts based upon examples from the literature. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors and minors; MUS 130 or examination; concurrent enrollment in MUS 221 and either MUS 201 or MUS 202 recommended; non-majors with permission of the instructor.

name: Diatonic Harmony
oneLiner: Common practice in harmonic and formal procedures through written exercises, analysis…
description: Common practice in harmonic and formal procedures through written exercises, analysis, and composition: triads, inversions, cadences, seventh chords, binary, ternary, and rondo forms based upon the literature. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: MUS 130 or permission of instructor.

name: Modern Musicianship: Theory, Application, and Ear Training II
oneLiner: Examine non-diatonic scales, advanced chords, chord inversions and voicings, chord…
description: Examine non-diatonic scales, advanced chords, chord inversions and voicings, chord substitutions, nonharmonic tones, lead sheet notation, Roman numeral analysis, and basic structures. Focus on the integration of written notation and active performance. (This course is offered as MUS 235 and TH A 235. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: MUS 130.

name: Introduction to Music Technology
oneLiner: Training in the creative use of a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) including the use of…
description: Training in the creative use of a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) including the use of basic recording and audio manipulation, MIDI, and synthesis. Training in basic acoustics and the evolution of electronic music technologies. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly MUS 433]

name: Composition Workshop
oneLiner: Free compositional work under the supervision of an instructor.
description: Free compositional work under the supervision of an instructor. Analytical presentations of original works. May be repeated for a total of 5 units; only 1 unit may count towards the total required for the major. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: MUS 200 or MUS 232.

name: Applied Music Lessons
oneLiner: An in-depth survey of repertoire and technique for one instrument or voice.
description: An in-depth survey of repertoire and technique for one instrument or voice. May be repeated for a total of 8 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors; audition; and permission of the department.

name: Improvisation Techniques
oneLiner: Beginning musical improvisation for instrumentalists or vocalists in all styles and…
description: Beginning musical improvisation for instrumentalists or vocalists in all styles and genres. May be repeated for a total of 12 units.

name: Traditions and Current Practices of Music and Sound for Healing
oneLiner: Introduction to the history and traditions of music and sound for healing purposes.
description: Introduction to the history and traditions of music and sound for healing purposes. The role of music as healing will be examined as an artistic endeavor and a social phenomenon. Contemporary techniques such as sonic neuro-technologies, singing bowls, and tuning forks will be explored through direct experiences and journal reflections.

name: The American Musical Experience
oneLiner: Exploration of American music through a socio-cultural lens.
description: Exploration of American music through a socio-cultural lens. The development of popular music in the United States will be surveyed relative to the history and sociology of the last two hundred years. Various regional, racial, ethnic, sacred, and secular music will be examined in light of their aesthetic and socially significant contexts.

name: Advanced Class Piano
oneLiner: Intermediate/Advanced class piano for voice, composition, instrumental, and music…
description: Intermediate/Advanced class piano for voice, composition, instrumental, and music history majors. Laboratory. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

oneLiner: Advanced individual projects in performance and literature for piano, harpsichord…
description: Advanced individual projects in performance and literature for piano, harpsichord, organ, and fortepiano. May be repeated for a total of 8 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors; audition; concurrent enrollment in MUS 360.

name: Applied Music Study: Vocals
oneLiner: Vocal study for the Music and Theater Arts degrees.
description: Vocal study for the Music and Theater Arts degrees. May be repeated for a total of 8 units for music performance majors; for other majors, may be repeated for a total of 2 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music and Theatre Art majors; audition; MUS majors must have approval of the department.

name: Rehearsal and Performance Technique
oneLiner: In depth exploration of character psychology, social political context and musical…
description: In depth exploration of character psychology, social political context and musical theatrical detail necessary for a successful opera production. Principally devoted to staging and advancement of student stagecraft. May be repeated for a total of 4 units.(CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: By audition.

name: Class Orchestral and Band Instruments I
oneLiner: Fundamentals in embouchure, fingering, articulation, breath control, and hand position.
description: Fundamentals in embouchure, fingering, articulation, breath control, and hand position. Topics to be specified in Class Schedule. May be repeated with varying content.
prereqNotes: Music majors and minors; ability to read music; others by permission of the department.

name: K-Pop: Performance and Pop Culture
oneLiner: Examination of the social-political, cultural, and aesthetic contexts of K-Pop as a…
description: Examination of the social-political, cultural, and aesthetic contexts of K-Pop as a transnational performance practice. Topics include K-Pop in the context of Korean history; colonization and empire, militarization, dance, music, and theatre history; globalization and popular culture, transmedia, aesthetic innovations, and major artists. (This course is offered as DANC 352/MUS 352/TH A 352. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better.

oneLiner: Training in chamber music, accompaniment, sight reading, keyboard literature, keyboard…
description: Training in chamber music, accompaniment, sight reading, keyboard literature, keyboard harmony, and solo performance with practicum performance opportunities. May be repeated for a total of 16 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division Music majors or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Open to all musical backgrounds and levels of experience to create and perform in the…

With a focus on using the studio as an instrument, perform, record, and live-stream stylistically diverse works, from popular to experimental, and create new works in a collaborative, exploratory, and improvisational environment using traditional acoustic instruments, any vocal style, or rap -- with or without live electronic processing -- as well as electronic instruments including gestural MIDI controllers, analog synthesizers, Ableton Push, theremin, etc. May be repeated for a total of 16 units. Activity.
prereqNotes: Audition.

description: Large performing ensemble focusing on repertoire and instruments of various world cultures and practices. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 16 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)

description: Small conducted ensemble focusing on European sacred choral music written before 1600. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 16 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Audition.

description: Large jazz ensemble, divided into small groups of 2-5 players. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 16 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Audition.

description: Performance and lecture-based introduction to the cultural traditions, concepts, and techniques of regional musical styles and genres of Mexico, including son jarocho, son huasteco, mariachi, marimba music from Chiapas region, as well as select indigenous musical practices. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 8 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Audition.

prereqNotes: Upper-division Music majors or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Music performance in a MUS ensemble (wind, orchestra, university chorus, jazz band…
description: Music performance in a MUS ensemble (wind, orchestra, university chorus, jazz band, etc.) practice as it relates to a variety of genres, styles, settings, historical periods, and instrumentations. Additional written assignments via online coursework. Lecture, 1 unit; activity, 2 units.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; audition; or permission of the instructor. Auditions are held during the first week of each semester.

name: Chromatic Harmony
oneLiner: Procedures found in chromatic music through written exercises, analysis, and…
description: Procedures found in chromatic music through written exercises, analysis, and composition, including secondary dominants, modulation, altered chords, theme-and-variations, and sonata forms based upon the literature. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly MUS 233]
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors and minors; MUS 200 or MUS 232; non-majors with permission of the instructor.

name: Tonal Counterpoint
oneLiner: Contrapuntal practices of the 18th century through written exercises in two- and…
description: Contrapuntal practices of the 18th century through written exercises in two- and three-parts based on analysis of examples from the literature. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Song Writing Workshop
oneLiner: Exploration of the songwriting process through both analytical and creative windows…
description: Exploration of the songwriting process through both analytical and creative windows with an emphasis on group sharing and feedback. Examination of music theory, notation, musicianship, music recording software, and performing. Includes the production of a portfolio of songs that are recorded, formatted, and notated in an accessible and professional manner. [Formerly MUS 238]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Electronic Music Production
oneLiner: Instruction in electronic music production in popular styles such as EDM, hip-hop, pop…
description: Instruction in electronic music production in popular styles such as EDM, hip-hop, pop, etc. Guidance from an established producer on the business of artist and band promotion. Activity. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly MUS 236, 436]
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; MUS 237*; or permission of the instructor.

name: Orchestration
oneLiner: Characteristics of modern orchestral instruments and the orchestrational styles and…
description: Characteristics of modern orchestral instruments and the orchestrational styles and techniques of the 18th, 19th, and 20th centuries. Representative scores from the literature and assignments in scoring for various instrumental ensembles. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: MUS 233.

oneLiner: Advanced training in computer-based production, live performance techniques…
description: Advanced training in computer-based production, live performance techniques, integration of modular and other hardware, and overview of finishing techniques for professional releases. Activity.
prereqNotes: MUS 408* or permission of the instructor.

name: 20th Century Techniques
oneLiner: Compositional procedures and musical structures of the 20th century through studies of…
description: Compositional procedures and musical structures of the 20th century through studies of the literature and composition. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: MUS 403 or MUS 440; or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Examination of the music industry and associated laws including contracts…
description: Examination of the music industry and associated laws including contracts, negotiations, career opportunities, intellectual property rights, and building professional contact networks. Activity.
prereqNotes: MUS 408 or permission of the instructor.

name: Jazz Improvisation
oneLiner: Study and application of jazz improvisation concepts such as extended harmonic…
description: Study and application of jazz improvisation concepts such as extended harmonic approaches, quartalism, linear chromaticism, and advanced cross-rhythm sensibility. Structures used are primarily the blues and standard tunes. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: MUS 270 with a grade of C or higher, or permission of the instructor.

name: Jazz Improvisation II
oneLiner: Review and application of jazz improvisation concepts utilizing extended harmonic…
description: Review and application of jazz improvisation concepts utilizing extended harmonic approaches, quartalism, linear chromaticism, and advanced cross-rhythm sensibility. Structures used are modern jazz standards. May be repeated for a total of 4 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: MUS 431.

name: Introduction to Sound for Games
oneLiner: Training in state of the art techniques used in designing sound for various types of…
description: Training in state of the art techniques used in designing sound for various types of video games and immersive environments. Analysis of theoretical topics in the history and development of modern video game and virtual reality audio design. (This course is offered as MUS 434 and BECA 434. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division and graduate Broadcast & Electronic Communication Arts and Music majors; or Video Game Studies minors who have completed CWL 180; demonstrated familiarity with any digital audio workstation.

name: Music and Middleware for Games

description: Learn implementation of music in a game engine via middleware. May be repeated for a total of 4 units. Activity.
prereqNotes: MUS 434/BECA 434 or permission of the instructor.

oneLiner: Theories and issues in software-based digital audio signal analysis, processing, and…
description: Theories and issues in software-based digital audio signal analysis, processing, and synthesis using Max MSP. Software synthesis and control techniques in creating original musical compositions. Activity. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: MUS 433.

name: Jazz Harmony
oneLiner: Notation and realization of harmony within the jazz musical idiom.
description: Notation and realization of harmony within the jazz musical idiom. Standard chord progressions, nomenclature, and lead sheet symbols, analyzed and applied. Recognition of African American musical culture and aesthetics within historical development of jazz harmony.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors and minors; MUS 200 or MUS 232; non-majors with permission of the instructor.

name: Jazz Composition and Arranging
oneLiner: Major jazz compositional practices, including review and application of form, harmonic…
description: Major jazz compositional practices, including review and application of form, harmonic and linear progression as developed through jazz masterworks of the 20th century. Composers' scores and transcribed improvisations, as well as student works. (Plus-minus letter grade only.)
prereqNotes: MUS 440.

name: Composition Studio Seminar
oneLiner: Exploration and application of composition studio activities.
description: Exploration and application of composition studio activities. Focus on sharing and critiquing work, as well as presentations from invited guests. Activity.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Creative Concepts in Music
oneLiner: The role of musical creativity in cognitive, cultural, political and socio-historical…
description: The role of musical creativity in cognitive, cultural, political and socio-historical terms, is examined in relation to the imaginative, original, eclectic, experimental, and innovative, as expressed by a number of select musical artists, their times, and masterworks.
prereqNotes: MUS 431; or permission of the instructor.

name: Scoring for Games I
oneLiner: Composition of music for a variety of gameplay styles and forms using digital audio…
description: Composition of music for a variety of gameplay styles and forms using digital audio workstations, audio middleware, and game engines as well as recordings of live performers. Training in the form and structure of music scoring for video games and immersive environments. Examination of theoretical distinctions between games and linear media. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing; MUS 237 and MUS 434 recommended; or permission of the instructor.

name: Scoring for Games II
oneLiner: Advanced training in the form and structure of music scoring for video games and…
description: Advanced training in the form and structure of music scoring for video games and immersive environments. Composition for and recording, mixing, and editing of large live performance ensemble for integration within a game. Co-lab with game design students. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors; MUS 237, MUS 415, MUS 434, and MUS 451; or permission of the instructor.

name: Scoring for Film I
oneLiner: Training in scoring for film.
description: Training in scoring for film. Under the supervision of an instructor, gain experience by scoring pre-existing scenes. Analysis of film scores. Preparation in self-promotion and the business of film scoring. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Upper-division standing.

name: Scoring for Film II
oneLiner: Training in scoring for film through collaboration and scoring for live ensembles.
description: Training in scoring for film through collaboration and scoring for live ensembles. Preparation in self-promotion and the business of film scoring. Activity. May be repeated for a total of 8 units.
prereqNotes: MUS 455 or permission of the instructor.

name: Repertoire for Composers
oneLiner: Literature associated with the study of MUS 450 as required for the Bachelor of Music.
description: Literature associated with the study of MUS 450 as required for the Bachelor of Music. May be repeated for a total of 4 units. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Music majors; Junior standing; MUS 420; must be taken concurrently with MUS 425 and MUS 450; or permission of the instructor.

name: Scoring for Virtual Reality
