description: Examination of Latin America political thought from the 16th century to the present. Focus on arguments about Spanish colonialism and Latin American independence and identity, the value of European thought and other sources of knowledge, and the nature of populism and revolution.
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Political Theories of Colonialism and Anti-Colonialism
oneLiner: Explores political theories of colonialism and anti-colonialism from a variety of time…
description: Explores political theories of colonialism and anti-colonialism from a variety of time periods, geographic spaces and ideologies. Analyzes how these theories have traveled and been appropriated. (Plus-minus AB/NC/RP grading only)
prereqNotes: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Culminating Experience Design and Prep
oneLiner: Project design and preparation for graduate culminating experience course (e.g.…
description: Project design and preparation for graduate culminating experience course (e.g. comprehensive exams, thesis, supervised internship). Working with faculty supervisor, develop applicable knowledge and relevant theories for culminating experience project. (CR/NC only)
prereqNotes: Graduate students in Political Science.

name: Supervised Field Internship in Political Science
oneLiner: Culminating Experience field internship in politics, government, community…
description: Culminating Experience field internship in politics, government, community organization, or other relevant politics-oriented organization. Includes written or portfolio project analyzing internship. Not open to Master of Arts students who choose to write a thesis or take comprehensive exams. (CR/NC/RP grading only)
prereqNotes: Advancement to candidacy (ATC) for the master's degree and permission of the candidate's committee chair, and approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Preparation for Written Comprehensive Examination
oneLiner: Directed reading in two subfields of Political Science, based upon a standard…
description: Directed reading in two subfields of Political Science, based upon a standard bibliography and consultation with departmental specialists in that field. Not open to Master of Arts candidates who choose to write a thesis. (CR/NC, RP grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Graduate Political Science students with approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Culminating Experience Examination
oneLiner: Enrollment in 896EXAM required for students whose culminating experience consists of an…
description: Enrollment in 896EXAM required for students whose culminating experience consists of an examination only. Not for students enrolled in a culminating experience course numbered PLSI 898. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor, committee chair, and approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

name: Master's Thesis
oneLiner: (CR/NC, RP grading only)
description: (CR/NC, RP grading only)
prereqNotes: Advancement to candidacy (ATC) for the master's degree and permission of the candidate's committee chair, and approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a member of the…
description: Study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a member of the departmental faculty. Open only to graduate students who have demonstrated the ability to do independent work. Enrollment by petition.
prereqNotes: Permission of the graduate major adviser, supervising faculty member, and department chair.

name: Internship: Aspects of Working in Reentry Services
oneLiner: Internship at a reentry service organization, related government agency, or reentry…
description: Internship at a reentry service organization, related government agency, or reentry scholar. Internship placement will be monitored by Project Rebound staff. Lecture, 1 unit; Activity, 2 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Prison Reentry Studies minors; C J 450*.

name: Persian Language Immersion
oneLiner: Proficiency in the skills of listening, writing, reading, and speaking the Persian…
description: Proficiency in the skills of listening, writing, reading, and speaking the Persian language. Exploration of the geography and culture of the Persian-speaking countries.

name: First Semester Persian
oneLiner: Develop listening, reading, and writing proficiency.
description: Develop listening, reading, and writing proficiency. Explore the Persian-speaking world's geography, history, culture, and religion.

name: Second Semester Persian
oneLiner: Continue to develop listening, reading, writing, and speaking proficiency.
description: Continue to develop listening, reading, writing, and speaking proficiency. Explore the Persian-speaking world's geography, history, culture, and religion.
prereqNotes: PRSN 101 or equivalent.

name: History and Cultures of Iran
oneLiner: Exploration of the major themes and key historical moments in the development of…
description: Exploration of the major themes and key historical moments in the development of cultures and civilizations of Iran from ancient times to present over the span of three millennia including historic, linguistic, ethnic, religious, artistic, and literary developments of the Greater Iranian nations. Significant shared terms such as Persia and Persian are critically explored and evaluated through an examination of the historical development of Iranian civilization through the late antique, medieval, and modern epochs. (This course is offered as PRSN 260 and I R 260. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: Persianate Literatures in Translation
oneLiner: Introduction to the historical development of oral and written literature amongst the…
description: Introduction to the historical development of oral and written literature amongst the peoples of Greater Iran. Exploration of various languages and literatures from the first millennium BCE until the New Persian language became the established and most influential Iranian language in the Medieval and Modern world. Examination of the histories, peoples, languages, and practices as key themes in the major ancient, medieval, and early modern texts through literary developments throughout the Persianate Societies.

name: Iranian Cinema
oneLiner: Examination of Iranian films in English as a lens to understand issues in the broader…
description: Examination of Iranian films in English as a lens to understand issues in the broader world. Exploration and discussion of the historical development of visual arts and cinema in Iranian societies as a form of self-expression and communicative practice. Major themes in contemporary Iranian cultures are examined through critical content, along with modes of humanistic and artistic inquiry, analysis, and interpretation. (This course is offered as PRSN 320 [formerly PRSN 550] and CINE 320. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Iranian Media in English
oneLiner: Development of critical thinking, reading, and writing skills for understanding Iranian…
description: Development of critical thinking, reading, and writing skills for understanding Iranian socio-politics and culture through global media. Access, interpret, and develop a practical understanding of contemporary media, including social media. Understand the Iranian world in the future through techniques for media literacy. (This course is offered as PRSN 411 and I R 415. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: World Religions
oneLiner: Major religions of humanity, their history, and teachings: Hinduism, Buddhism…
description: Major religions of humanity, their history, and teachings: Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism, Christianity, Judaism, and Islam. (This course is offered as PHIL 502 and PRSN 502. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Religions in Iran
oneLiner: Exploration of the major religious traditions of Iran from its inception to the present…
description: Exploration of the major religious traditions of Iran from its inception to the present day over the span of three millennia including Judaism, Zoroastrianism, Mithraism, Mandaeism, Christianity, Manichaeism, Mazdakism, Islam (Sunni and Shia), Sufism, Yarsanism, and Bahai faith. Insight into not only Iranian identity, but also the way in which religious traditions grow, change, and influence one another through the spectrum of Greater Iranian history. (This course is offered as PRSN 503 [formerly PRSN 450], PHIL 503, and RELS 503. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: The Buddhist Tradition
oneLiner: An introduction to the basic teachings of Buddhism and the major Buddhist traditions in…
description: An introduction to the basic teachings of Buddhism and the major Buddhist traditions in Asia. Among the topics to be discussed are ignorance, paths to enlightenment, meditation, morality, faith, and wisdom. (This course is offered as PHIL 509 and PRSN 509. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Written projects in English or Persian that require critical analysis and…
description: Written projects in English or Persian that require critical analysis and interpretation of cultural or literary issues. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: PRSN 102 or equivalent.

name: Psychology of Personal Development
oneLiner: Basic concepts in psychology are used to foster the student's understanding of his/her…
description: Basic concepts in psychology are used to foster the student's understanding of his/her own personal development and life endeavor.

name: The Logic and Psychology of Critical Thinking
oneLiner: Designed to improve students' skills in understanding/criticizing arguments, theories…
description: Designed to improve students' skills in understanding/criticizing arguments, theories, and their reasoning process. Apply an analytic approach to the evaluation of oral and written communication and problem-solving activities.

name: Quantitative Reasoning in Psychology
oneLiner: Psychological statistics and measurement essential to understanding statistical and…
description: Psychological statistics and measurement essential to understanding statistical and quantitative arguments. Lecture, 2 units; activity,1 unit. (Note: For this course to satisfy General Education, students must earn a grade of C- or CR or higher.)
prereqNotes: First-year math advising module. Students who elect to take additional support should concurrently enroll in MATH 122 or MATH 123.

name: General Psychology
oneLiner: Basic methods and concepts of psychology which have broad academic relevance and can be…
description: Basic methods and concepts of psychology which have broad academic relevance and can be applied to the study of psychology as well as other academic disciplines. Psychology majors must take for a letter grade and earn a C or better to continue in the major. [CSL may be available]

name: First Year Experience: Translating Personal Experiences to a Science of Mind and Behavior
oneLiner: First-year experience that provides a synthesis of personal interests and background…
description: First-year experience that provides a synthesis of personal interests and background with the empirical psychological literature.
prereqNotes: GE Area 1A/A2* with a grade of CR or C- or better.

name: Current Issues in Psychology
oneLiner: Selected issues and controversies of current scientific and professional importance in…
description: Selected issues and controversies of current scientific and professional importance in psychology. Advanced study of behavior as a personal, social, and biological phenomenon. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for up to 9 units when topics vary. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200 or equivalent.

name: Psychology: The Major and the Profession
oneLiner: Overview of the psychology major and the field of psychology. (CR/NC grading only)
description: Overview of the psychology major and the field of psychology. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; must be taken in the first semester of the major.

name: Writing in Psychology - GWAR
oneLiner: Writing techniques and practices appropriate for the field of psychology.
description: Writing techniques and practices appropriate for the field of psychology. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated when topics vary. No more than 3 units may be applied toward the Psychology major. (ABC/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Psychology majors; GE Area 1A/A2; PSY 371 with a grade of C or better; completion of 60 units.

name: Sex and Relationships
oneLiner: Explore the role of sexuality in traditional and emerging forms of intimate…
description: Explore the role of sexuality in traditional and emerging forms of intimate relationships. (This course is offered as PSY 320 and SXS 320. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Child Development
oneLiner: The development of the child from conception to adolescence.
description: The development of the child from conception to adolescence. Intended for non-psychology majors.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; PSY 200* or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Psychological Statistics
oneLiner: Statistical theory and techniques appropriate to psychology and related fields…
description: Statistical theory and techniques appropriate to psychology and related fields; statistical inference and the testing of hypotheses. Psychology majors must take for a letter grade and earn a C or better. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology, Child and Adolescent Development, and Liberal Studies majors; PSY 171 and PSY 200 or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Introduction to Research in Psychology
oneLiner: Integrates psychological research methods with statistical techniques.
description: Integrates psychological research methods with statistical techniques. Theoretical, empirical, and interpretive issues are examined within the fundamental methods of inquiry: observation, measurement of individual differences, surveys, and experiments.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology, Child and Adolescent Development, and Liberal Studies majors; PSY 200 and PSY 371 or equivalents with grades of C or better.

name: Adolescent Psychology
oneLiner: The physical, intellectual, emotional, and social development during adolescence.
description: The physical, intellectual, emotional, and social development during adolescence.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors with PSY 200 or equivalent and PSY 330 or PSY 431; or Child and Adolescent Development majors with CAD 210 and CAD 410; or permission of the instructor.

name: Developmental Psychology
oneLiner: Fundamental principles of developmental psychology; origin and development of behavior.
description: Fundamental principles of developmental psychology; origin and development of behavior.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology and Child and Adolescent Development majors; PSY 200 or equivalent.

name: Cognitive Development: Language, Thinking, and Perception
oneLiner: Cognitive development is studied from two dominant approaches--Piagetian and…
description: Cognitive development is studied from two dominant approaches--Piagetian and information processing. The textbooks used are collections of articles by leading theoreticians and researchers in the areas of perception, attention, mental representation (episodic and semantic), and problem-solving.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Psychology and Child and Adolescent Development majors; PSY 431; or permission of the instructor.

name: Social, Emotional, and Personality Development
oneLiner: Advanced course in developmental psychology covering theory and data in the areas of…
description: Advanced course in developmental psychology covering theory and data in the areas of emotional, social, and personality development over the life span.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Psychology and Child and Adolescent Development and Early Childhood Studies majors; PSY 431 or CAD 210 and CAD 410GW; or permission of the instructor.

name: Developmental Psychopathology
oneLiner: Interrelationship of typical and atypical development among children and emerging…
description: Interrelationship of typical and atypical development among children and emerging adults, patterns of adaptation and maladaptation throughout the lifespan with a focus on risk and protective factors.
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; PSY 330 or PSY 431 or CAD 210 or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Development of Gender Identities
oneLiner: Integration of biological, psychological, social, and cultural knowledge toward an…
description: Integration of biological, psychological, social, and cultural knowledge toward an understanding of the development of gender and sex in all their meanings and facets. A critical look at theories of gender, sex, and gender/sex in psychological science with attention to stereotypes and social issues within the United States, and considering both cisgender and transgender experiences. (This course is offered as PSY 436 and SXS 436. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; PSY 371; or permission of the instructor.

name: Social Psychology
oneLiner: Survey of theories, research and applications in major areas of social psychology…
description: Survey of theories, research and applications in major areas of social psychology, including communication and social influence processes in interaction, group dynamics, attitudes, stereotyping and prejudice, altruism and aggression, person perception and social cognition, sex roles and sex differences, crowds and social movements.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors and students in the Conflict Resolution Certificate Program and PSY 200 or equivalent.

name: The Psychology of the Family
oneLiner: Exploration of the family as a psychological group, parental relationships with special…
description: Exploration of the family as a psychological group, parental relationships with special attention to the dynamics of pairs, and the impact of the family on personality and mental health.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors and Conflict Resolution Certificate students; PSY 200 and PSY 371 or equivalent.

name: Health Psychology
oneLiner: A critical review of the relationships between psychological variables and both…
description: A critical review of the relationships between psychological variables and both physical and mental health. Combination of lectures, tests, reading of original research, and conducting an actual study in the field. Students gain knowledge of the relationships between health and psychology and become critical readers of literature relating the two.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200 and PSY 371 or equivalents.

name: The Science of Happiness
oneLiner: Conceptual, experiential, and applied introduction to positive psychology.
description: Conceptual, experiential, and applied introduction to positive psychology.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing Psychology majors; PSY 200 and PSY 371.

name: Variations in Human Sexuality
oneLiner: Variations in sexuality: sexual identity, relationships, behavior, and fantasy…
description: Variations in sexuality: sexual identity, relationships, behavior, and fantasy; identification of personal and social problems associated with varied sexual lifestyles. (This course is offered as SXS 400, PSY 450, and SOC 400. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: Theories of Personality
oneLiner: Survey of the major contemporary theories of personality.
description: Survey of the major contemporary theories of personality. Theoretical positions are compared and critically examined along various significant dimensions, including their relationships to the total field of psychology. Methods of personality assessment as related in theory construction.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200 and PSY 371 or equivalents; or permission of the instructor.

name: Psychopathology (Abnormal Psychology)
oneLiner: An overview of the different theoretical models of psychopathology and the factors that…
description: An overview of the different theoretical models of psychopathology and the factors that can contribute to psychological dysfunction; emphasis will be placed on exploring the major categories of psychological disorders, their causes, and treatments.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200.

name: Psychology of Death and Dying
oneLiner: Exploration of the psychological impact of mortality, grief, loss, and meaning making.
description: Exploration of the psychological impact of mortality, grief, loss, and meaning making. Focus on the current psychological theories and research of death and dying from both a Western and non-Western perspective. Examine the current understanding of the psychology of death and dying.
prereqNotes: PSY 200* or permission of the instructor.

name: Cross-Cultural Perspectives in Psychology
oneLiner: Cross-cultural behavioral, developmental, cognitive, and social data and research of…
description: Cross-cultural behavioral, developmental, cognitive, and social data and research of psychological phenomena as they are differentially affected by culture and subculture. Emphasis on the diversity of parent-child relationships, role of women and men, adult personality and beliefs, attitudes, and values.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors and students enrolled in the Conflict Resolution Certificate Program; PSY 200 or equivalent.

name: Psychology of Human Sexual Behavior
oneLiner: Psychological aspects of human sexual functioning particularly pertaining to gender…
description: Psychological aspects of human sexual functioning particularly pertaining to gender identity, pairing, sexual orientation, sexual intercourse, self-stimulation, reproduction, contraception and abortion. Related social issues such as alternative lifestyles, changing sex roles and recreational sex. (This course is offered as PSY 456 and SXS 456. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing.

name: Introduction to Industrial/Organizational Psychology
oneLiner: Application of psychological principles and methods in understanding human behavior at…
description: Application of psychological principles and methods in understanding human behavior at work, and to approach and solve problems in business and industry. Addresses such issues as: employee selection, training, and evaluation; working conditions; motivation, leadership, and organizational theory.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors and Conflict Resolution Certificate students; PSY 200 and PSY 371 or equivalents.

name: Personnel Psychology
oneLiner: The application of psychological principles to personnel selection and related…
description: The application of psychological principles to personnel selection and related practices in organizations. Designed for the psychology major interested in developing proficiency in personnel techniques.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Human Factors in Technology
oneLiner: A survey of methods and research in the study of the interface between human operators…
description: A survey of methods and research in the study of the interface between human operators and machines. Applications include equipment design for computers, aircraft, automobiles, household appliances, and similar systems.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors or permission of the instructor.

name: Psychology of Career Pursuit
oneLiner: Evaluation and application of psychology theories to foster greater career success and…
description: Evaluation and application of psychology theories to foster greater career success and address social inequities prevalent within career pursuit. Development of professional skills, such as job searching, communication, goal setting, networking, and fostering healthy and equitable work environments. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.

name: The Psychology of Work-Life Stress
oneLiner: General understanding of basic concepts, mechanisms, and issues related to stress…
description: General understanding of basic concepts, mechanisms, and issues related to stress; examines basic factors in context of business organizations. Topics include employees' cognitive appraisal of organizational stressors; physiological, psychological, and behavioral outcomes; and individual differences and long-term consequences.
prereqNotes: PSY 200 or equivalent.

name: Training and Development in Organizations
oneLiner: Application of principles of psychology in the development, delivery, and evaluation of…
description: Application of principles of psychology in the development, delivery, and evaluation of training and development programs in work organizations.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Introduction to Legal Psychology
oneLiner: Topics include laws and the ethics of therapy, alternative dispute resolution, mental…
description: Topics include laws and the ethics of therapy, alternative dispute resolution, mental health aspects of criminology, police psychology, the insanity defense, treatment of prisoners, the psychological forces toward crime and delinquency, expert mental health testimony, eyewitness testimony, and jury behavior.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors, Criminal Justice Studies majors, and Prison Reentry Studies minors; PSY 200 or C J 300; or permission of the instructor.

name: Psychology of Social Justice
oneLiner: Psychological explanations for structural barriers to equality and social justice…
description: Psychological explanations for structural barriers to equality and social justice through an exploration of the mainstream psychological literatures of procedural, distributive, retributive, and restorative justice. Approved preparatory course for Experimental College instructors.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology and Criminal Justice majors; PSY 200 or C J 300.

name: Psychology of Policing
oneLiner: Psychological study of organizational processes and management of police agencies.
description: Psychological study of organizational processes and management of police agencies. Topics include causes and effects of psychological factors affecting police, and implications of military and community-service models of police management on police selection, stress, training, organization development, technology.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology and Criminal Justice majors; PSY 200 or C J 300.

name: Introduction to Data Science for Psychology
oneLiner: Use scientific methods, processes, algorithms, and systems to extract psychological…
description: Use scientific methods, processes, algorithms, and systems to extract psychological insights from data. Examine the basic principles of data science - applied to understanding behavior - including data visualization, statistical concepts, data transformation, basic programming, and fundamentals of neural networks, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Gain experience working with the statistical programming language R.
prereqNotes: PSY 371.

name: Learning
oneLiner: Methods, findings, and theory in animal and human learning and memory.
description: Methods, findings, and theory in animal and human learning and memory.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200 and PSY 371 or equivalents.

name: Perception
oneLiner: Methods, theory, and analysis of sensations and perceptions; the study of the…
description: Methods, theory, and analysis of sensations and perceptions; the study of the psychological and biological approaches to perception.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Motivation
oneLiner: Theory and experimental evidence on the origins and direction of behavior.
description: Theory and experimental evidence on the origins and direction of behavior. Learned and unlearned drives, anxiety, curiosity, and emotions.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Cognitive Psychology
oneLiner: Introduction to how humans perceive, attend, remember, reason, use language, and make…
description: Introduction to how humans perceive, attend, remember, reason, use language, and make decisions through the dominant information-processing approach in cognitive psychology. Emphasis on research methods, scientific reasoning, and applications of cognitive science to real-world problems and artificial intelligence.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: The Psychology of Human Memory
oneLiner: Examination of fundamental theories and research in the study of human memory and…
description: Examination of fundamental theories and research in the study of human memory and explore their real-life applications.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing Psychology majors; PSY 200 and PSY 371.

name: Cognitive Neuroscience: Psychological Models
oneLiner: Prospects and potential limitations of studying cognitive psychological processes from…
description: Prospects and potential limitations of studying cognitive psychological processes from the integrated perspectives of cognitive psychology, neuropsychology, neural network modeling, and neuroscience.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
oneLiner: The methods of clinical psychology, including case study techniques, psychodiagnostic…
description: The methods of clinical psychology, including case study techniques, psychodiagnostic evaluation, remediation of psychological distress. The current scope of professional practices in clinical psychology.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Community Psychology
oneLiner: Introduction to methods practiced within the community psychology and community mental…
description: Introduction to methods practiced within the community psychology and community mental health fields. A range of methods is presented along with the range of underlying assumptions and philosophies of psychological fieldwork. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors and Conflict Resolution Certificate students; PSY 200 and PSY 371 or equivalents.

name: Psycholinguistics
oneLiner: Comprehensive introduction to psycholinguistics.
description: Comprehensive introduction to psycholinguistics. Theory and research are examined in three areas of human functioning--comprehension, production, acquisition. In addition, mental representations of meaning, the relation between language and thought, and bidialectism and bilingualism are studied.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200 or equivalent.

name: Decision Making: A Perspective from Social Psychology
oneLiner: Every day we have the opportunity to make countless decisions: should we eat dessert…
description: Every day we have the opportunity to make countless decisions: should we eat dessert, cheat on a test, or attend a sports event with our friends. But despite our vast experience with decisions, we humans are (highly) imperfect decision-makers. We routinely depart from rationality and optimality, and we do so in systematic and predictable ways. Deeply examine these departures from rational decision making and identify strategies for making better and more effective decisions.

name: Social Conflict and Conflict Resolution
oneLiner: Review of theory and research concerning conflict between individuals and groups.
description: Review of theory and research concerning conflict between individuals and groups. Principles of perception, expectation, subjective expected utility, payoff matrices, prominence, communication restriction, and expectations of personality.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors, Global Peace, Human Rights, and Justice Studies minors, and students enrolled in the Conflict Resolution Certificate program; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Field Services Seminar
oneLiner: Issues in the professional application of psychological principles in community service.
description: Issues in the professional application of psychological principles in community service. May be repeated for a total of 4 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 371; concurrent enrollment in PSY 559.

name: Psychological Field Service
oneLiner: Supervised field services in cooperating community psychological agencies.
description: Supervised field services in cooperating community psychological agencies. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 371; concurrent enrollment in PSY 558.

name: Intermediate Psychological Statistics
oneLiner: Statistical theory and techniques applicable to various experimental designs and other…
description: Statistical theory and techniques applicable to various experimental designs and other forms of psychological research. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 371 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.

name: Physiological Psychology I
oneLiner: Background and contemporary research relating behavior to biological processes.
description: Background and contemporary research relating behavior to biological processes. Data on neural and hormonal systems are summarized and used in examining such complex behaviors as learning, perception, and motivation.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Physiological Psychology II
oneLiner: Selected issues and research dealing with the biological basis of behavior.
description: Selected issues and research dealing with the biological basis of behavior. Students read intensively on a mutually agreed upon topic and report their findings for discussion and development in class sessions.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors or graduate students in psychology; PSY 371, PSY 581, or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Group Processes
oneLiner: Practicum involving observation of interaction within the class and in outside groups…
description: Practicum involving observation of interaction within the class and in outside groups, aimed at the investigation of the psychology of groups.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors and students enrolled in the Conflict Resolution Certificate program; PSY 200, PSY 371, or equivalent.

name: Peer Advising in Psychology
oneLiner: Prepare and deliver academic advising to undergraduates in psychology: academic…
description: Prepare and deliver academic advising to undergraduates in psychology: academic policies and procedures. Individual advising 3 hours weekly. May be repeated for a total of 6 units. Lecture, 2 units; fieldwork, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; 1 year in residence; 12 units of Psychology coursework; and a GPA of 3.0 or better.

name: Projects in the Teaching of Psychology
oneLiner: Training and experience in the teaching of psychology through fieldwork and instruction.
description: Training and experience in the teaching of psychology through fieldwork and instruction. Students work as Instructional Aides to a psychology instructor and receive training in teaching and learning principles as well as participate in teaching-related activities. (Students may earn a maximum of 4 units toward the baccalaureate degree for any course(s) numbered 685 regardless of discipline.)
prereqNotes: A minimum grade of B in the course the student will be assisting in or permission of the instructor.

name: Future Directions for Psychology Majors
oneLiner: Exploration of career options within the field of psychology.
description: Exploration of career options within the field of psychology. Activities include informational interviews with professionals in the field of psychology, practice job interviews, and online networking. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to senior Psychology majors; 19* units of upper-division Psychology coursework; PSY 303*.

name: Proseminar I
oneLiner: First of a two-semester seminar with the principal goal of developing a detailed senior…
description: First of a two-semester seminar with the principal goal of developing a detailed senior project proposal. Work here may include examination of literature reviews, theoretical contributions, methodological studies, experiments, and field studies and practical applications.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; selection as an honors candidate; concurrent enrollment in PSY 697.

name: Proseminar II
oneLiner: Continuation of PSY 693.
description: Continuation of PSY 693. Intended to facilitate and to provide evaluation of progress toward completion of the senior project. Completed senior project culminates the semester.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; completion of Fall semester work in PSY 693 and PSY 697.

name: Senior Project Preparation
oneLiner: First semester of the Honors Program sequence.
description: First semester of the Honors Program sequence. Work closely with a faculty mentor to identify a research question, conduct a literature review, and design a methodologically sound research project. Emphasis is placed on research design, ethical considerations, and developing a detailed project proposal that will be implemented in PSY 698.
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors.

name: Honors Project in Psychology
oneLiner: Second semester of the Honors Program sequence.
description: Second semester of the Honors Program sequence. Execute the research project designed in PSY 697 (or begin directly with faculty approval), analyze data, and prepare a written and/or oral report of findings. Faculty certification of satisfactory completion results in the transcript designation "Honors Project in Psychology."
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division Psychology majors; PSY 697; or permission of the instructor.

name: Independent Study in Psychology
oneLiner: An intensive study of a particular problem in psychology under the direction of a…
description: An intensive study of a particular problem in psychology under the direction of a faculty member. Intended for students who have completed available coursework in the area of a special problem. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. Only 3 units can be applied to the Psychology major elective requirement. [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to upper-division standing.

name: Clinical Methods: Assessment of Intelligence and Perceptual-Motor Functioning
oneLiner: Problems in the assessment of mental and emotional characteristics of individuals.
description: Problems in the assessment of mental and emotional characteristics of individuals. Discussions, demonstrations, and application of individual assessment techniques including the standard individual tests of intelligence for children and adults as well as neuropsychological, educational achievement, and perceptual-motor tests.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students; concurrent enrollment in PSY 729; or permission of the instructor.

name: Clinical Methods: Personality Appraisal and Projective Techniques
oneLiner: Problems in the assessment and diagnosis of individual personality and its disorders.
description: Problems in the assessment and diagnosis of individual personality and its disorders. Discussions, demonstrations, and applications of standard appraisal techniques including projective tests.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students; PSY 721; concurrent enrollment in PSY 729; or permission of the instructor.

name: Clinical Methods: Psychological Assessment
oneLiner: Methods of assessment of mental functioning of individuals, including clinical…
description: Methods of assessment of mental functioning of individuals, including clinical interviewing, psychological diagnosis, report writing, and the administration and interpretation of cognitive/neuropsychological batteries, personality inventories, and projective tests. Assessment considerations for children, older adults, and cross-cultural populations.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students or permission of the instructor.

name: Clinical Issues: Drugs, Brain, and Behavior
oneLiner: Examination of basic mechanisms and advances in psychopharmacology, neurological…
description: Examination of basic mechanisms and advances in psychopharmacology, neurological interventions for psychological disorders, and treatment approaches for substance abuse disorders.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students or permission of the instructor.

name: Conference to Accompany Psychology Practicum
oneLiner: Issues in the practice of clinical psychology including alcohol and substance use…
description: Issues in the practice of clinical psychology including alcohol and substance use, general conceptual framework, models of intervention, professional ethics and law, roles, and responsibilities of psychotherapists. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential Program students; concurrent enrollment in PSY 729.

name: Psychology Practicum
oneLiner: Practicum in the methods and procedures of psychological assessment, diagnosis, and…
description: Practicum in the methods and procedures of psychological assessment, diagnosis, and prognosis and techniques of psychological intervention with individuals, couples, and families. May be repeated for a total of 12 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Clinical or School Psychology graduate students. For Clinical Psychology graduate students, concurrent enrollment in PSY 728 is required.

name: Seminar in Current Issues in Developmental Psychology
oneLiner: Problems and issues in developmental psychology: new directions in theory, method, and…
description: Problems and issues in developmental psychology: new directions in theory, method, and research.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students or permission of the instructor.

name: Laboratory in Observation of Children's Behavior
oneLiner: Observations and experimental studies of human behavior.
description: Observations and experimental studies of human behavior. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students or permission of the instructor; must be taken concurrently with PSY 739.

name: Technical Writing for Psychological Journals
oneLiner: Practicum on preparing written reports on observations of human behavior within the…
description: Practicum on preparing written reports on observations of human behavior within the American Psychological Association format. Activity.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students; concurrent enrollment in PSY 737.

name: Seminar in Social Psychology
oneLiner: Critical examination of current theories and research in social psychology, emphasizing…
description: Critical examination of current theories and research in social psychology, emphasizing social influence processes and personality variables which may affect behavior in diverse organizational and informal settings, and exploring applications of social psychology in the design and assessment of social change.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Survey Research
oneLiner: Principles and methods of survey research are studied and applied in supervised field…
description: Principles and methods of survey research are studied and applied in supervised field experiences covering the entire survey process, from research design to sampling, data collection, and preparation of a report.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Current Trends and Issues
oneLiner: New developments drawn from current overviews and symposia.
description: New developments drawn from current overviews and symposia. Implications for revision of theory, practice, and experimental procedures. Both ethical views and scientific and applied methods are critically examined.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Therapeutic and Developmental Change I
oneLiner: Convergence of developmental theory and psychotherapeutic process, focusing on clinical…
description: Convergence of developmental theory and psychotherapeutic process, focusing on clinical theories relevant across the lifespan from infancy through old age, and end-of-life. Considerations of culture, SES, and other factors shaping development.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Therapeutic and Developmental Change II
oneLiner: Modern versions of psychodynamic theories incorporating family concepts, ethnicity, and…
description: Modern versions of psychodynamic theories incorporating family concepts, ethnicity, and community issues including cultural factors in the dynamics of spousal or partner abuse.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; PSY 753.

name: Seminar in Organizational Psychology
oneLiner: Selected psychological theory and research findings applied to the study of human…
description: Selected psychological theory and research findings applied to the study of human behavior in organizational settings.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; PSY 761 or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Industrial and Organizational Psychology
oneLiner: Current problems and problem-solving approaches in selected areas of personnel…
description: Current problems and problem-solving approaches in selected areas of personnel practices concerning the use and development of human resources in industrial, professional, and other applied fields.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Industrial Psychology
oneLiner: Theory, research, and methods from I/O psychology pertaining to personnel selection and…
description: Theory, research, and methods from I/O psychology pertaining to personnel selection and related decisions in organizations, including job analysis, performance measurement, validation, selection strategies, and test administration.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; PSY 761 or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Industrial Training Program Development
oneLiner: Examination of the theoretical, methodological, and practical approaches to the…
description: Examination of the theoretical, methodological, and practical approaches to the development, installation, and evaluation of training programs in the modern work setting. Considers learning theory and research, training theory and techniques, and methods of assessing and evaluating programs.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program, permission of the instructor.

name: Psychological Foundations of Organizational Change
oneLiner: Psychological theory and research on group and organizational change processes, with…
description: Psychological theory and research on group and organizational change processes, with attention to problems and methods of organizational change and assessment of organizational intervention outcomes.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; PSY 761 or equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar to Accompany Field Experience in Industrial/Organizational Psychology
oneLiner: Experiences in field assignments are explored for theoretical and research implications.
description: Experiences in field assignments are explored for theoretical and research implications. Ethical, professional and inter-professional implications are considered.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Psychology graduate students and School Psychology Credential students or permission of the instructor; concurrent enrollment in PSY 769.

name: Field Experience in Industrial/Organizational Psychology
oneLiner: Supervised field assignments for advanced graduate students in a variety of business…
description: Supervised field assignments for advanced graduate students in a variety of business, professional, and industrial settings. May be repeated for credit for a total of 6 units. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; PSY 760, PSY 761, PSY 762; permission of the instructor.

name: Research Methods and Techniques
oneLiner: Seminar in research designs applicable to the systematic analysis of varieties of human…
description: Seminar in research designs applicable to the systematic analysis of varieties of human behavior.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program or permission of the instructor.

name: Analysis of Variance and Experimental Design
oneLiner: Major analysis of variance designs used in psychological research.
description: Major analysis of variance designs used in psychological research. Topics include an introduction to use of a major statistical package and a brief introduction to use of the General Linear Model. Students in the master's program in psychological research should take this course at the first opportunity. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; intermediate statistics; or permission of the instructor.

name: Applications of Multiple Regression to Psychological Research
oneLiner: Experimental designs using multiple regression and correlation methods.
description: Experimental designs using multiple regression and correlation methods. Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential Program students; intermediate statistics; or permission of the instructor.

name: Statistical Analysis of Multivariate Data Using Computers
oneLiner: Theory and application of multivariate models, illustrative assigned problems, and…
description: Theory and application of multivariate models, illustrative assigned problems, and laboratory in computer data processing. An integration of explanations of linear statistical models, existing computer programs which accomplish multivariate linear analyses, and analyses of data collected in student's own research (e.g., M.A. thesis). Lecture, 3 units; activity, 1 unit.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; two applied statistics courses or equivalent.

name: Proseminar in Foundations of Contemporary Psychological Research
oneLiner: Contemporary theory and research in such basic areas of psychology as learning and…
description: Contemporary theory and research in such basic areas of psychology as learning and motivation, sensory process and perception, physiological, developmental, social and personality, and clinical and abnormal. Each seminar topic is directed by a faculty member specializing in that area and accompanied by comprehensive and systematic readings. Students in the master's program in psychological research should take this course at the first opportunity. Lectures and discussion on criteria for the design, execution, analysis, and report of psychological research on animal and human subjects. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program.

name: Research Colloquium
oneLiner: Presentations and discussions of current or contemplated research projects. (CR/NC…
description: Presentations and discussions of current or contemplated research projects. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program or permission of the instructor.

name: Supervised Selected Research
oneLiner: Experimental research under the direction of a member of the faculty.
description: Experimental research under the direction of a member of the faculty. May be repeated for a total of 9 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology and School Psychology Credential students; PSY 770.

name: Clinical Methods: Diagnosis and Advanced Psychopathology
oneLiner: Examines various approaches to the evaluation and treatment of major mental disorders…
description: Examines various approaches to the evaluation and treatment of major mental disorders including substance abuse disorders and disorders of childhood and adolescence. (Plus-minus letter grade only.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Clinical or School Psychology program or School Psychology Credential Program.

name: Clinical Methods: Marital and Family Systems Theory and Therapy
oneLiner: Characteristic interpersonal interactions including those involving substance abuse or…
description: Characteristic interpersonal interactions including those involving substance abuse or partner abuse and how those appear in the clinical interview are studied from different theoretical viewpoints including assessment and intervention procedures. Conditions which promote psychological change in couples and families including same-sex relationships are studied from an interpersonal, familial, and sociocultural perspective. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; PSY 821.

name: Conference to Accompany Advanced Psychology Practicum
oneLiner: Therapeutic process and change with diverse mental disorders and populations.
description: Therapeutic process and change with diverse mental disorders and populations. Explorations of principles of recovery oriented care, case management, and collaborative treatment. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; concurrent enrollment in PSY 829.

name: Advanced Psychology Practicum
oneLiner: Supervised advanced psychology practicum in clinical psychological evaluation and…
description: Supervised advanced psychology practicum in clinical psychological evaluation and intervention. May be repeated for a total of 12 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Clinical or School Psychology graduate students. For Clinical Psychology graduate students, concurrent enrollment in PSY 828 is required.

name: Qualitative and Applied Research Methods
oneLiner: Training in qualitative and applied research methods in psychology.
description: Training in qualitative and applied research methods in psychology. Examination of the nature, purposes, theories & methods of qualitative research. Introduction to major approaches to qualitative methods, including ethnography, case study, phenomenology, grounded theory, & narrative inquiry. Application of qualitative methods such as interviewing, observing, & making meaning of social settings. Exploration of major methods for analyzing qualitative data, such as thematic analysis, narrative analysis, and discourse analysis. Learning how to assess the quality & trustworthiness of interpretive research.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Psychology graduate students and School Psychology Credential students.

name: Field Experience in Developmental Psychology
oneLiner: Supervised field experience with children and adolescents.
description: Supervised field experience with children and adolescents. May be repeated for a total of 4 units. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Professional School Psychology
oneLiner: Roles, skills, and competencies of professional school psychologists as they apply to…
description: Roles, skills, and competencies of professional school psychologists as they apply to educational, career, developmental, and mental health needs of children and opportunities for working with these needs within the interpersonal, legal, and professional structure of the school.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program and permission of the instructor.

name: Behavior Management
oneLiner: Behavioral, cognitive-behavioral, and ecobehavioral theory and intervention applied to…
description: Behavioral, cognitive-behavioral, and ecobehavioral theory and intervention applied to human behavior change. Primary focus on classroom behavior management. (Plus-minus letter grade only) [Formerly cross-listed with COUN 719]
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Psychology or School Psychology Credential students.

name: Conference to Accompany Psychology Internship
oneLiner: Seminar in problems in the professional practice of psychology.
description: Seminar in problems in the professional practice of psychology. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; concurrent enrollment in PSY 859.

name: Psychology Internship
oneLiner: Internship in the application of psychological principles and procedures including…
description: Internship in the application of psychological principles and procedures including psychological evaluation, treatment. May be repeated for a total of 12 units.
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; PSY 829 or equivalent.

name: Seminar in Selected Problems
oneLiner: Special areas of advanced applications of psychological research and theory.
description: Special areas of advanced applications of psychological research and theory. Topics to be specified in the Class Schedule. May be repeated for a total of 9 units when topics vary.
prereqNotes: Restricted to Psychology graduate students and School Psychology Credential students.

name: Directed Reading
oneLiner: Special problems in psychology, chosen on the basis of individual interests and studied…
description: Special problems in psychology, chosen on the basis of individual interests and studied under the direction of a member of the faculty. May be repeated for a total of 9 units. (Plus-minus letter grade, CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program.

name: Culminating Experience Examination
oneLiner: For students whose culminating experience consists of an examination only.
description: For students whose culminating experience consists of an examination only. Not for students enrolled in PSY 898 as their culminating experience. (CR/NC, RP)
prereqNotes: Permission of the instructor, committee chair, and approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration.

name: Master's Thesis
oneLiner: The student formulates, conducts, and presents an intensive research thesis which must…
description: The student formulates, conducts, and presents an intensive research thesis which must be defended before a committee drawn from the psychology faculty. ATC and Proposal for Culminating Experience Requirement forms must be approved by the Graduate Division before registration. (CR/NC grading only.)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology; permission of the candidate's committee chair; and approval of Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) and Culminating Experience (CE) forms by Graduate Studies.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a member of the faculty.
description: Study is planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a member of the faculty. Open only to graduate students who have demonstrated ability to do independent work. Enrollment by petition (form available in the Psychology Office).
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate students in Psychology or School Psychology Credential Program; permission of the graduate major adviser and supervising faculty member.

name: Multisystem Pathokinesiology
oneLiner: An integrated approach to the pathophysiology, evaluation, treatment, and management…
description: An integrated approach to the pathophysiology, evaluation, treatment, and management considerations related to patients with multi-systems musculoskeletal, cardiopulmonary, medical, and integumentary dysfunctions with a focus on physical therapy practice in the acute care environment. Long-term management, adaptive equipment/procedures, and preventative aspects of care are also discussed. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Doctor of Physical Therapy graduate students; PT 201, PT 204A.

name: Education, Health Promotion, Wellness, and Prevention in Physical Therapy
oneLiner: Principles of communication, learning, and memory affecting physical therapists' roles…
description: Principles of communication, learning, and memory affecting physical therapists' roles as an educator in individualized patient and caregiver instruction, staff development programs, community health, wellness, and prevention programs. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Structure, Function, and Motion in Physical Therapy
oneLiner: Combine knowledge of human anatomy with basic structural and kinesiological principles…
description: Combine knowledge of human anatomy with basic structural and kinesiological principles to understand the normal functional motion of the spine, trunk, and extremities. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Neurological Pathokinesiology I
oneLiner: Pathokinesiological and neuromotor principles applied to physical therapy assessment…
description: Pathokinesiological and neuromotor principles applied to physical therapy assessment and intervention for neurological dysfunction; physical rehabilitation of adults with neurological impairments, limitations, and disability from trauma, tumors, vascular problems, infectious or degenerative diseases. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Neurological Pathokinesiology III
oneLiner: Pathokinesiological and neuromotor principles applied to examination, evaluation…
description: Pathokinesiological and neuromotor principles applied to examination, evaluation, diagnosis, prognosis, plan of care, and intervention of neurological dysfunction in pediatric patients. Includes dysfunction from trauma, congenital defects, and degenerative diseases. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; PT 710 and PT 213.

name: Cardiopulmonary Pathokinesiology I
oneLiner: Assessment and treatment of kinesiological/physiological dysfunction of cardiac and…
description: Assessment and treatment of kinesiological/physiological dysfunction of cardiac and pulmonary systems. Physical rehabilitation or training for cardiac and/or pulmonary limitations arising from trauma, disease, congenital defect, or lifestyle. Lecture, 1 unit; laboratory, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Psychosocial Issues in Rehabilitation Sciences, Part I
oneLiner: Exploration of one's individual biases, values, and judgments of psychosocial factors…
description: Exploration of one's individual biases, values, and judgments of psychosocial factors that influence patient and physical therapist interactions; identifying key psychosocial issues and providing intervention and support services where appropriate. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Ecological and Organizational Issues in Rehabilitation
oneLiner: Cultural, environmental, and legislative issues affecting accessibility of physical…
description: Cultural, environmental, and legislative issues affecting accessibility of physical therapy and related services. Sociocultural issues relative to quality of health as a right; influences of political and fiscal climates on trends in models of health care delivery. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Psychosocial Issues in Rehabilitation Science, Part II
oneLiner: Exploration of one's individual biases, values, and judgments of psychosocial factors…
description: Exploration of one's individual biases, values, and judgments of psychosocial factors that influence patient and physical therapist interactions; identifying key psychosocial issues and providing intervention and support services where appropriate. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Musculoskeletal Pathokinesiology I
oneLiner: Surface anatomy, basic structure, biomechanical principles applied to the understanding…
description: Surface anatomy, basic structure, biomechanical principles applied to the understanding of normal and abnormal human motion in the lower extremities and to the analysis of physical function. Examination, evaluation, treatment skills for musculoskeletal disorders. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; PT 200, PT 201, PT 706.

name: Musculoskeletal Pathokinesiology II
oneLiner: Surface anatomy, basic structure, biomechanical principles applied to the analysis of…
description: Surface anatomy, basic structure, biomechanical principles applied to the analysis of normal/ abnormal human motion, and physical function in the spine, pelvis, upper extremities. Examination, evaluation, and treatment skills for musculoskeletal disorders. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 2 units. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; PT 741.

name: Musculoskeletal Pathokinesiology III
oneLiner: Screening, examination, evaluation, and therapeutic treatment techniques, including…
description: Screening, examination, evaluation, and therapeutic treatment techniques, including both manual and exercise-based treatments, for the management of complex patients with musculoskeletal dysfunctions. Lecture, 2 units; laboratory, 1 unit. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; PT 741 and PT 742.

name: First Full-Time Clinical Education Experience I
oneLiner: Students provide physical therapy examination, evaluation, and intervention under the…
description: Students provide physical therapy examination, evaluation, and intervention under the guidance and supervision of a licensed physical therapist in clinical facilities. This is a 10-week full-time first clinical education experience. Students will submit personal goals and reflections and present an in-service. (CR/NC only, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; First-year coursework with a GPA of 3.0 or better.

name: Intermediate Full-Time Clinical Education Experience II
oneLiner: Students provide physical therapy examination, evaluation, and intervention under the…
description: Students provide physical therapy examination, evaluation, and intervention under the guidance and supervision of a licensed physical therapist in clinical facilities. This is a 12-week full-time intermediate clinical education experience. Students will submit personal goals and reflections and present an in-service. (CR/NC only, RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; First- and second-year coursework with a GPA of 3.0 or better.

name: Independent Study
oneLiner: Independent study or research planned, developed, and completed under the direction of…
description: Independent study or research planned, developed, and completed under the direction of a faculty member. May be repeated for a total of 8 units. (CR/NC grading only) [CSL may be available]
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; permission of the major adviser and supervising faculty member. Open only to graduate students who have demonstrated the ability to do independent work.

name: Professional Colloquium
oneLiner: Topics relative to evidence-based PT practice: ethics, human subjects, research…
description: Topics relative to evidence-based PT practice: ethics, human subjects, research, authorship, scientific writing; and to professional issues: legislation, direct access to PT services and reimbursement for services. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to Physical Therapy doctoral students and PT 208 (UCSF).

name: Evidence Based Practice
oneLiner: Students will continue the evidence-based review they started in PT 209, performing a…
description: Students will continue the evidence-based review they started in PT 209, performing a meta analysis to answer their own research question. Students will present their findings orally and in a publication-style manuscript for the DPT culminating experience. (Plus-minus letter grade; no CR/NC allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; successful completion of PT 209 or the equivalent; or permission of the instructor.

name: Case Reports I
oneLiner: Research and preparation of a case report on the diagnosis and treatment of a patient…
description: Research and preparation of a case report on the diagnosis and treatment of a patient care problem relevant to physical therapy. (CR/NC grading only)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students.

name: Case Reports II
oneLiner: Research, preparation, and presentation of a case report on the diagnosis and treatment…
description: Research, preparation, and presentation of a case report on the diagnosis and treatment of a patient care problem relevant to physical therapy. (Plus-minus letter grade; CR/NC not allowed; RP)
prereqNotes: Restricted to graduate Physical Therapy students; PT 920.

name: Christmas and Hanukkah in the United States
oneLiner: Examination of the social, political, and cultural history of Christmas and Hanukkah in…
description: Examination of the social, political, and cultural history of Christmas and Hanukkah in the United States from the colonial period to the present day. Focus on the relationship between religion, politics, commerce, and popular culture, including gender roles and the changing role of religious, ethnic, and racial minorities in U.S. public culture. (This course is offered as JS 265, AMST 265, HIST 265, and RELS 265. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

name: The Nature of Religious Experience
oneLiner: Nature of religious experience drawn from different religions and academic disciplines…
description: Nature of religious experience drawn from different religions and academic disciplines within the humanities and social sciences; investigation of the meaning of religious commitment in a secular world. (This course is offered as PHIL 525 and RELS 300. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Religion in America
oneLiner: The social history of religion in the United States from contact to the present.
description: The social history of religion in the United States from contact to the present. Changing relations between religious thought and institutions. The range and variety of forms of religious expression in an increasingly urbanized, industrialized, and globalized society. A particular focus on the relationship between religion, science, and modernity. (This course is offered as HIST 482 and RELS 482. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: Upper-division or graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

name: Religions in Iran
oneLiner: Exploration of the major religious traditions of Iran from its inception to the present…
description: Exploration of the major religious traditions of Iran from its inception to the present day over the span of three millennia including Judaism, Zoroastrianism, Mithraism, Mandaeism, Christianity, Manichaeism, Mazdakism, Islam (Sunni and Shia), Sufism, Yarsanism, and Bahai faith. Insight into not only Iranian identity, but also the way in which religious traditions grow, change, and influence one another through the spectrum of Greater Iranian history. (This course is offered as PRSN 503 [formerly PRSN 450], PHIL 503, and RELS 503. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)
prereqNotes: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.

name: Critical Thinking and the Leisure Experience
oneLiner: Introduction to basic concepts and principles of critical thinking.
description: Introduction to basic concepts and principles of critical thinking. Subject matter includes identifying, differentiating, constructing, and evaluating arguments; recognizing fallacies; and applying formal and informal reasoning to the leisure experience within recreation, parks, and tourism.

name: Foundations of Recreation, Parks, and Tourism
oneLiner: Recreation, parks, and tourism as a discipline and profession; introduction to…
description: Recreation, parks, and tourism as a discipline and profession; introduction to concepts, philosophy, history, and science; nature and scope of careers in for-profit, nonprofit, and public sectors; examination of issues and trends, and their implications to leisure systems and processes.

name: Adventure Travel
oneLiner: Culturally sensitive, low impact travel and tourism by individuals that engages…
description: Culturally sensitive, low impact travel and tourism by individuals that engages travelers, protects the global environment and benefits local communities. Assessment of the adverse/beneficial impacts of travel. Development of trip plan incorporating adventure travel principles and sustainable tourism goals.

name: Growth Through Art and Leisure
oneLiner: Arts and crafts skills for recreational and clinical and therapeutic purposes.
description: Arts and crafts skills for recreational and clinical and therapeutic purposes. The development of creativity and self-expression in community programs, resources for materials, leadership skills, and equipment use and maintenance are covered. Extra fee required.

name: Growth Through Adventure
oneLiner: Development of values and an understanding of self through outdoor adventure activities.
description: Development of values and an understanding of self through outdoor adventure activities. Examination of the influences of culture, history, fears, and myths on outdoor adventure activities. Introduction to selected outdoor skills. Survey of selected outdoor adventure activities in the Bay Area and Northern California.

name: Developmental Play Processes
oneLiner: Concepts, trends, and issues related to play, recreation, and leisure including…
description: Concepts, trends, and issues related to play, recreation, and leisure including learning and human development throughout the lifespan, gender and cultural differences, materials and environments, benefits and barriers, engineering and facilitating play experiences, and activity adaptation.

name: Leadership in Recreation, Parks, and Tourism
oneLiner: Leadership theory, self-assessment, intrapersonal and interpersonal communication, and…
description: Leadership theory, self-assessment, intrapersonal and interpersonal communication, and group dynamics in recreation, parks, and tourism settings. Develop leadership competencies in cultural sensitivity, planning, safety/risk management, and problem-solving through experiential learning, influence of power and ethics on decision-making.
